title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
Under the positive isometric generator, rank-six PCA should recover the six-dimensional observed image and constrained skew least squares should approximately recover the two true rotational planes, subject to noise, finite differences, occupancy, and subtraction.
The unrestricted derivative fit cannot have larger training SSE than the constrained skew fit. Similar held-out performance supports a skew-dominant local linear relation under this metric; it does not prove a pure rotational generator in unknown data.
The symmetric-decay control should favor a symmetric derivative map and lack a valid rotational-plane truth target.
Staggered transient latencies may produce curved or rotational-looking projections despite having no shared autonomous six-dimensional state law (Michaels et al. 2016; Lebedev et al. 2019).
Input-driven trajectories can make a state-only matrix absorb correlations with \(u(t)\). The input-aware fit should be judged by held-out derivative prediction and recovery of the declared state/input coefficients, not by whether its projected curves look less circular.
Short arcs can show a strong tangent relation without completing a cycle. Event jitter can reduce condition consistency; light smoothing can reduce derivative noise while changing bandwidth and phase.
Across-condition subtraction can reveal or suppress different variance patterns and is part of the estimand, not neutral cleanup (Lebedev et al. 2019).
A covariance-matched condition shuffle is more informative than an unconstrained shuffle only for the nuisance structure it actually preserves (Michaels et al. 2016).
Under nonorthogonal mixing, the latent physical trajectory is unchanged but Euclidean skew symmetry is not preserved in general. This is a metric-dependence stress, not a failed isometric positive case.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
Use the declared \(A\), eight initial states, isometric \(H\), full \([0,2.4]\) interval, no smoothing, correct alignment, and primary across-condition subtraction. Both true rotational planes and rates are applicable.
The name full_window means the complete predeclared observation interval, not proof that every trajectory completes a cycle. The fastest ideal mode spans \(4.8\) radians and the slower mode spans \(1.68\) radians over this interval; those facts are reported explicitly.



Retain only the first 18 samples, \(t\in[0,0.68]\), before fitting PCA and derivatives. The fastest ideal mode spans \(1.36\) radians and the slower mode \(0.476\) radians. Report angular span, occupancy, plane angle, rate error, and fit stability. A low derivative error on this window cannot establish periodicity, recurrence, or a closed orbit.



For each trial independently, draw an integer offset from \(\{-3,-2,\ldots,3\}\) bins using frozen seeds. Generate or resample the analytic trajectory at the shifted physical times before adding noise, then analyze against the nominal aligned grid. Samples outside \([0,2.4]\) use the analytic generator rather than circular wrapping. Store every offset. This models imperfect event alignment without inventing transitions across window boundaries.



Compare no smoothing with the frozen three-bin moving average applied independently within each condition/trial trajectory. Fit preprocessing, PCA, derivatives, and matrices separately for the two branches using training data only. Do not smooth derivatives after differencing in one branch and before differencing in the other without naming the changed target.



Run the positive generator both with and without the time-varying training across-condition mean subtraction. Retain the same rank, derivative estimator, and split. Report how plane occupancy, true-plane angle, derivative fit, angular rate, and condition consistency change. Neither branch is declared universally correct.



Replace the positive state matrix by
\[
A_{\mathrm{sym}}=operatorname{diag}(-1.2,-0.8,-0.5,-0.35,-0.2,-0.1)
\]
under the same isometric \(H\), initial states, noise, and splits. The true derivative map is symmetric and has no nonzero imaginary eigenvalues. Score derivative prediction for unrestricted, skew-constrained, and symmetric-constrained fits. Do not assign a true rotational-plane angle or angular-rate target.



This control is defined directly in observed coordinates and has no autonomous latent state equation. For observed feature \(j=1,\ldots,10\), condition \(c=0,\ldots,7\), and time \(t\),
\[
y_{c,j}(t)
=
(-1)^j(1+0.08c)
\exp\left[-\left(\frac{t-\tau_{j,c}}{w_j}\right)^2\right],
\]
with
\[
\tau_{j,c}=\operatorname{linspace}(0.35,1.70)_{j}+0.025c,
\qquad
w_j=\operatorname{linspace}(0.13,0.25)_j.
\]
Add the same observation noise and split structure. This produces an ordered sequence of feature peaks. jPCA metrics may be computed, but true-plane and autonomous-matrix recovery are not applicable. The control tests whether delayed transients can yield rotational-looking projections, as motivated by Michaels et al. and Lebedev et al. (Michaels et al. 2016; Lebedev et al. 2019).



Generate
\[
\dot z(t)=A_u z(t)+Bu_c(t),
\]
where
\[
A_u=\operatorname{diag}(-0.25,-0.30,-0.35,-0.40,-0.45,-0.50),
\]
\[
B=
\begin{pmatrix}
0.8&0\\
0&0.7\\
0.5&0.3\\
-0.3&0.5\\
0.2&-0.4\\
0.4&0.25
\end{pmatrix},
\]
and
\[
u_{c,1}(t)=\sin(1.3t+0.35c),
\qquad
u_{c,2}(t)=
\exp\left[-\left(\frac{t-(0.8+0.04c)}{0.28}\right)^2\right].
\]
Use one frozen numerical integration rule and step equal to the observation grid; record its local consistency check. Compare:

state-only affine: \(\Delta x/\Delta t\approx Mx_i+b\);
input-aware affine: \(\Delta x/\Delta t\approx Mx_i+Gu_i+b\).

Both fits use the same frozen noisy trials, training centering, PCA coordinates, and left-endpoint predictors, matching the forward-Euler generator. No time-varying across-condition subtraction is used in this control. The known input columns are supplied only to the input-aware fit. The state-only fit’s skew component can reflect omitted drive. Including \(u\) is a model comparison under known simulator inputs, not proof of causal input identification in observational data (Cunningham and Yu 2014).



Use
\[
G=HS,
\]
with
\[
S= egin{pmatrix}
1&0.35&0&0&0&0\\
0&1.6&0.2&0&0&0\\
0&0&0.7&0.25&0&0\\
0&0&0&1.3&0.2&0\\
0&0&0&0&0.8&0.3\\
0&0&0&0&0&1.8
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Generate \(y=Gz\) from the same positive latent trajectories. The mapped true planes \(G\mathcal P_j\) remain valid geometric images for angle scoring, but \(GAG^+\) is not generally skew-symmetric under the ordinary observed Euclidean metric. Report the Gram matrix \(G^\top G\), its condition number, and plane/rate diagnostics. Do not merge this stress with the isometric positive acceptance criterion.



For each feature independently, permute whole condition trajectories among the eight conditions, preserving each feature’s complete time course and marginal condition distribution while disrupting cross-feature condition identity. Generate 128 frozen permutation proposals per split. Select the proposal with maximum similarity between the original and shuffled flattened feature covariance, using only covariance similarity—not any rotational metric—and report
\[
\operatorname{sim}(C,C_\pi)
=1- rac{\lVert C-C_\pi\rVert_F^2}{\lVert C\rVert_F^2}.
\]
The target threshold is \(0.95\); if no proposal reaches it, use the highest-similarity proposal, record the miss, and narrow interpretation. Refit the complete pipeline on the selected shuffled training/validation data. This bounded construction is motivated by, but is not identical to, the iterative CMPT of Michaels et al. (Michaels et al. 2016). A time-wise permutation that breaks every trajectory is not an acceptable matched control.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
The verifier must assert all of the following.

Positive generator algebra: analytic derivatives equal \(Az(t)\) within floating-point tolerance.
Correct skew sign: the stored \(J(\omega)\) blocks have upper-right \(-\omega\), lower-left \(+\omega\), and \(J^\top=-J\).
Embedding isometry: \(\lVert H^\top H-I\rVert_{\max}\le10^{-12}\).
Split integrity: trial identifiers are disjoint and no condition means, preprocessing, PCA basis, matrix, plane, or hyperparameter use test trials.
Boundary integrity: every derivative pair belongs to one condition and one trial/condition-mean trajectory; the expected pair count is checked exactly.
Derivative oracle: midpoint finite differences on noiseless positive trajectories agree with analytic midpoint derivatives within \(3\times10^{-3}\).
PCA oracle: training PCA projector equals the independent rank-six SVD projector within \(10^{-10}\).
Unrestricted LS: normal-equation residual orthogonality or an independent least-squares recomputation passes tolerance.
True constrained skew LS: \(M_{\mathrm{skew}}+M_{\mathrm{skew}}^\top=0\) and reconstruction from the explicit skew basis agrees within \(10^{-10}\).
No antisymmetrization substitution: the verifier independently solves the skew-basis least-squares problem and does not accept \((M_{\mathrm{un}}-M_{\mathrm{un}}^\top)/2\) as an oracle unless the two happen to agree numerically.
Symmetric constrained LS: \(M_{\mathrm{sym}}-M_{\mathrm{sym}}^\top=0\) and the symmetric-basis solution is independently recomputed.
Nested training loss: unrestricted training SSE is no larger than skew- or symmetric-constrained SSE within numerical tolerance.
Plane extraction: each recovered plane is orthonormal and invariant under the fitted skew matrix; the stored rate equals \(|q_1^\top M_{\mathrm{skew}}q_2|\).
Plane equivalence: plane-angle metrics are invariant to within-plane rotations, axis swaps, and sign changes.
Truth applicability: true-plane/rate rows exist only for the positive and separately labelled nonorthogonal mapped-plane conditions; they are absent for latency and symmetric controls.
Input design: input-aware predictors contain the declared two input columns, are full rank where required, and state-only fits cannot access them.
Jitter integrity: offsets are stored, no circular wrapping occurs, and physical derivative times are handled consistently.
Smoothing/subtraction isolation: each branch refits training preprocessing and changes only its named operation.
Shuffle matching: whole trajectories are permuted, covariance similarity is computed before rotational analysis, and selection never uses jPCA metrics.
Truth and test poison: replacing latent truth and test observations cannot change training/validation fitted parameters or selected controls.
Determinism: a clean temporary rerun produces byte-identical manifest.json, metrics.csv, diagnostics.json, and summary.png.
Metric provenance: every row has unique labels for split, condition, preprocessing, method, target, metric, and finite value.

Passing these checks establishes bounded numerical consistency, not that a real system is an autonomous oscillator.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
Antisymmetrizing the unrestricted fit: Euclidean matrix projection is not generally the skew-constrained derivative least-squares solution.
Wrong skew sign: using \(\begin{psmallmatrix}0&+\omega\\-\omega&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) silently reverses the declared positive orientation.
Cross-condition derivatives: joining condition endpoints creates artificial velocities.
Test-refitted PCA or preprocessing: this is transductive leakage, not held-out evaluation.
Plane selected by visual circularity: plane selection must follow the frozen skew-operator rule.
Fast rate mistaken for high occupancy: frequency, data variance, derivative fit, and stability are separate quantities.
Short tangent arc called oscillation: less than a cycle does not show recurrence or periodicity.
Latency control assigned a latent oscillator: ordered transients can yield rotation without the positive autonomous law.
State-only input fit called autonomous truth: omitted common drive can be absorbed into \(M\).
Across-condition subtraction called harmless: it changes the fitted data and can change displayed rotations (Lebedev et al. 2019).
Smoothing called cosmetic: it changes derivatives and temporal bandwidth.
Unmatched shuffle: destroying covariance, smoothness, and condition structure simultaneously produces an uninformative easy null.
Nonorthogonal mixing pooled with isometry: skew symmetry is metric-dependent and not invariant to arbitrary invertible coordinates.
Projection called posterior state inference: jPCA projections do not perform probabilistic de-noising or state posterior estimation (Cunningham and Yu 2014).
Rotation called a global vector field: the fit is supported only over the sampled, processed condition–time region.
Rotation called mechanism or causality: a fitted local linear relation does not identify circuit implementation or intervention effects.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
Fit \(W\) from training condition means under the declared preprocessing. PCA supplies the observation representation in which all derivative models are compared. It is not a rotational method and receives no angular-rate estimate.



Stack midpoint states \(X\) and derivative targets \(D\) as columns and solve
\[
\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}
\in\arg\min_M\lVert D-MX\rVert_F^2
\]
with lstsq or an equivalent stable solve. Report rank, condition number, training SSE, and held-out derivative error.



Let \(B_{ij}\), \(i<j\), have \(+1\) at \((i,j)\), \(-1\) at \((j,i)\), and zeros elsewhere. Solve
\[
\widehat M_{\mathrm{skew}}
=
\sum_{i<j}\theta_{ij}B_{ij},
\]
\[
\widehat\theta
\in
\arg\min_\theta
\left\lVert
\operatorname{vec}(D)-
\begin{bmatrix}
\operatorname{vec}(B_{12}X)&\cdots
\end{bmatrix}
\theta
\right\rVert_2^2.
\]
This is the actual jPCA constrained fit described in the Churchland supplementary derivation (Churchland et al. 2012). It is not formed by antisymmetrizing \(\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}\).



Fit a matched constrained symmetric model
\[
\widehat M_{\mathrm{sym}}
\in\arg\min_{M^\top=M}\lVert D-MX\rVert_F^2
\]
using an explicit symmetric basis. Also report the algebraic decomposition
\[
\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}
=
\frac{\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}+\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}^\top}{2}
+
\frac{\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}-\widehat M_{\mathrm{un}}^\top}{2}
\]
only as a diagnostic of the unrestricted operator. Neither algebraic part substitutes for its corresponding constrained regression.



For a fitted real skew matrix, diagonalize the symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix
\[
-\widehat M_{\mathrm{skew}}^2.
\]
Each positive repeated eigenvalue \(\omega_j^2\) defines a two-dimensional invariant plane. Group the repeated eigenspace, orient a deterministic orthonormal basis \((q_{j1},q_{j2})\), and set handedness so
\[
q_{j1}^\top\widehat M_{\mathrm{skew}}q_{j2}<0
\]
for the declared \(J(\omega)\) convention, equivalently
\[
Q_j^\top\widehat M_{\mathrm{skew}}Q_j
\approx
\begin{pmatrix}0&-\widehat\omega_j\\\widehat\omega_j&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Order planes by decreasing \(|\widehat\omega_j|\). Near-repeated frequencies are compared as a combined four-dimensional invariant subspace rather than assigned unstable plane labels.



For the input control, solve
\[
D=MX+GU+E
\]
jointly by least squares. Compare held-out prediction with the state-only model and report \(M\), \(G\), rank, and coefficient error in the training PCA representation. Known simulator input does not enter positive or other control fits.



The fixed baseline is the first two training PCs. Five random rank-two planes are generated once in the six-dimensional PCA space, orthonormalized, and frozen before data generation. They receive occupancy, tangential/radial, angular-span, and condition-consistency metrics but no fitted rate unless a separately named in-plane derivative fit is performed.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
Training PCA rank six. Shared representation for every fitted derivative method.
Unrestricted state-only linear derivative regression. Best linear state-only training fit.
True skew-constrained derivative regression. jPCA operator and invariant planes.
True symmetric-constrained derivative regression. Expansion/decay alternative.
Algebraic symmetric/skew parts of the unrestricted matrix. Diagnostic only.
Fixed first-two-PC plane. Variance-oriented baseline.
Five fixed random planes. Data-independent projection references.
Input-aware state-plus-input regression. Applicable only to the declared input control.
Covariance-matched condition shuffle. Structured null, not a fitted dynamical method.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
For method \(m\), report
\[
\operatorname{MSE}_m
=
\frac{1}{N_D}\lVert D^{\mathrm{test}}-widehat D_m^{\mathrm{test}}\rVert_F^2
\]
and
\[
R_m^2
=1-
\frac{\lVert D^{\mathrm{test}}-widehat D_m^{\mathrm{test}}\rVert_F^2}
{\lVert D^{\mathrm{test}}-\bar D^{\mathrm{test}}\rVert_F^2}.
\]
Report train, validation, and test separately. For the forward-Euler input control, \(\widehat D=\widehat MX+\widehat GU+\widehat b\) at left endpoints; state-only methods cannot access \(U\).



For recovered plane \(Q\) and true plane \(T\), use singular values of orthonormal bases:
\[
\theta_1,\theta_2
=
\arccos\left(\operatorname{svd}(Q^\top T)\right).
\]
Report maximum angle, RMS sine error, and projector Frobenius error. Match the two positive recovered planes to the two true planes by minimum total maximum-angle assignment, then report the assignment itself. Plane metrics are invariant to sign, axis swap, and within-plane rotation.



For matched recovered plane \(Q_j\),
\[
\widehat\omega_j
=
\left|q_{j1}^\top\widehat M_{\mathrm{skew}}q_{j2}\right|,
\]
and report absolute and relative errors against \(2.0\) and \(0.7\). Do not report latent-rate recovery as applicable in the nonorthogonal stress unless the metric transformation is explicitly accounted for.



For projected state \(r=Q^\top x=(r_1,r_2)^\top\) with \(\lVert r\rVert>10^{-8}\), define
\[
e_r=\frac{r}{\lVert r\rVert},
\qquad
e_\tau=J(1)e_r,
\]
\[
v_r=e_r^\top Q^\top\dot x,
\qquad
v_\tau=e_\tau^\top Q^\top\dot x.
\]
Report mean radial energy \(E_r=\operatorname{mean}(v_r^2)\), tangential energy \(E_\tau=\operatorname{mean}(v_\tau^2)\), their ratio, the fraction of state–derivative angles within a predeclared tolerance of \(\pi/2\), and the signed rotation-direction consistency across conditions. A high ratio can occur over a short nonrecurrent arc.



Plane occupancy is
\[
\operatorname{Occ}(Q)=
\frac{\sum\lVert Q^\top x\rVert_2^2}
{\sum\lVert x\rVert_2^2}.
\]
Angular span unwraps \(\operatorname{atan2}(r_2,r_1)\) separately by condition, reports each condition’s span, and summarizes median/range. Never unwrap across condition boundaries.



Report:

training-versus-validation and training-versus-test independently fitted plane angles;
leave-one-condition-out plane angles and rate changes;
condition-wise direction consistency and angular-rate dispersion under the training-fitted plane; and
single-trial projected tangential/radial summaries using the frozen condition-mean fit.

Condition means and single trials are different noise regimes. Stable means do not imply stable trial-level rotation.



Report predictor rank and condition number, skew/symmetric constraint violations, unrestricted-versus-constrained SSE gaps, PCA occupancy, subtraction sensitivity, smoothing sensitivity, jitter offsets, shuffle covariance similarity, and nonorthogonal map condition number.



Every metrics.csv row contains exactly:
split,condition,preprocessing,method,target,metric,value
Values are finite. Inapplicable rows are omitted and listed with reasons in diagnostics.json; latency controls never receive zero-valued true-plane errors.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
The positive simulator establishes a narrow implementation and recovery question: under an isometric observation map, known linear state equation, occupied initial conditions, fixed PCA rank, declared preprocessing, and finite-difference target, does the recovered skew operator identify the mapped rotational planes and rates? A favorable answer validates that bounded pipeline, not a general mechanistic interpretation of rotational projections.
The controls separate alternatives. Symmetric decay tests whether constrained model comparison distinguishes contraction. Latency sequences test ordered transients without a shared autonomous state law. The input control tests omitted drive. Short arcs, jitter, smoothing, and subtraction show that preprocessing and sampling define the estimand. Nonorthogonal mixing shows that Euclidean skew symmetry is coordinate/metric dependent.






TipLDG synthesis



A vector field assigns a local velocity to a declared state. jPCA instead fits one linear state-to-derivative relation to sampled, processed trajectories. Agreement on those samples does not establish that the fitted matrix is valid globally, that the observed coordinates are the complete state, or that external inputs are absent.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
It does not prove that a rotational projection is an oscillator or limit cycle.
It does not establish recurrence, periodicity, phase resetting, or self-sustained oscillation.
It does not establish autonomous dynamics when inputs, feedback, clock time, or omitted state may matter.
It does not infer a global vector field beyond the sampled condition–time region.
It does not identify a causal, neural, physical, or biological mechanism.
It does not make projected condition means posterior latent trajectories.
It does not show that one PCA/jPCA plane is a unique state space.
It does not make skew symmetry invariant to arbitrary feature scaling or nonorthogonal coordinates.
It does not turn smoothing, alignment, averaging, or across-condition subtraction into neutral operations.
It does not make covariance-matched shuffles universal hypothesis tests.
It does not imply that high plane occupancy means good derivative prediction, or vice versa.
It does not infer dynamics from visual circularity alone.
It does not establish manifold structure, topology, intrinsic dimension, or nonlinear geometry.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
A real-data analysis must define simultaneously recorded versus pseudo-population features, independent trial/session/subject units, condition balance, alignment events, time window, smoothing, feature normalization, across-condition subtraction, PCA rank, derivative estimator, condition boundaries, input measurements, and nested selection. Trial-averaged projections should be supplemented by single-trial stability and noise-aware analyses.
Competing explanations require matched controls: latency models should preserve realistic time courses; input-aware models require measured inputs and declared system boundaries; shuffles should preserve the nuisance statistics relevant to the tested hypothesis. If arbitrary nonorthogonal coordinates are scientifically plausible, rotation should be evaluated relative to a justified metric rather than treated as coordinate-free. None of those additions turns an observational fit into causal identification.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
The implementation scope is exactly:
toy-models/rotational-projection-controls.py
toy-models/artifacts/rotational-projection-controls/manifest.json
toy-models/artifacts/rotational-projection-controls/metrics.csv
toy-models/artifacts/rotational-projection-controls/diagnostics.json
toy-models/artifacts/rotational-projection-controls/summary.png
No additional artifact is authorized. The script uses only the bundled Python, NumPy, and Pillow environment. JSON ordering, CSV ordering, float formatting, plot dimensions, fonts, and PNG metadata are fixed for byte-comparison determinism.
The manifest records:

exact positive, symmetric, input, latency, and nonorthogonal generator definitions;
the correct \(J(\omega)\) sign convention;
realized initial states, isometric/nonorthogonal maps, split sizes, time grid, and all seeds;
preprocessing, windows, smoothing, subtraction, derivative construction, PCA rank, plane orientation, and random planes;
unrestricted, skew, symmetric, and input-aware solve conventions;
shuffle proposal count, covariance criterion, threshold, selected proposal, and achieved similarity;
applicability rules, tolerances, runtime versions, commands, and SHA-256 hashes; and
exact artifact inventory.

diagnostics.json contains generator, isometry, derivative, boundary, leakage, PCA, constrained-solve, plane-invariance, truth-applicability, input, jitter, smoothing, subtraction, shuffle, metric-dependence, trial-stability, and deterministic-regeneration records.
The expected command is:
/Users/bytedance/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 toy-models/rotational-projection-controls.py
The default command should generate and verify artifacts, with explicit --generate and --verify modes if following the Phase 3 convention. Verification includes clean temporary regeneration and byte comparison.



The following sources were actually retrieved and inspected. Existing LDG Methods and Concepts were terminology anchors, not substitutes for source inspection.

Churchland et al. (2012): the complete openly accessible main-article full text was inspected for the abstract, central reaching results, controls, state–derivative angle analysis, unrestricted-versus-skew comparison, projection interpretation, and Methods preprocessing/alignment description. The 15-page supplementary PDF was inspected for shuffle descriptions, smoothing and cross-condition-mean figures, PCA-rank/plane controls, and the supplementary jPCA derivation on pages 12–14, including the explicit skew-basis constrained least-squares construction and complex-eigenvector plane formation. Supplementary movies, the spreadsheet, and source code were not inspected frame-by-frame or line-by-line. OCR in the supplement drops some minus signs; this object uses the mathematically correct \(M_{\mathrm{skew}}=(M-M^\top)/2\), \(M_{\mathrm{skew}}^\top=-M_{\mathrm{skew}}\), and \(J(\omega)\) convention stated above (Churchland et al. 2012).
Michaels, Dann, and Scherberger (2016): the 22-page PLOS Computational Biology PDF was inspected for the abstract and introduction; latency-augmented representational simulation; jPCA results; covariance-matched permutation-test rationale and results; condition/neuron-count sensitivity; discussion; and Methods sections defining jPCA preprocessing, rotational metrics, latency simulation, and iterative condition-wise covariance matching. RNN training details and every supplementary figure were not checked equation by equation. This source supports latency controls and a covariance-preserving condition-structure null, not a universal significance test (Michaels et al. 2016).
Lebedev et al. (2019): the complete open full-text article was inspected for the abstract; temporal ordering of response peaks; simulated latency sequences; PCA/jPCA reanalysis; condition shuffles; across-condition-subtraction critique; Methods descriptions; discussion; and interpretation limits. The authors’ code was not independently rerun and their stronger mechanistic conclusions are not adopted as settled fact. This source supports treating temporal response order and subtraction as explicit alternatives/sensitivities (Lebedev et al. 2019).
Cunningham and Yu (2014): the complete 10-page author PDF was inspected for the overview of covariance and time-series dimensionality reduction, the discussion of dynamical-model assumptions, and the section distinguishing direct orthogonal projections from trajectories inferred through a probabilistic dynamics/noise tradeoff. The review’s modality examples and reference list were not read exhaustively. This source supports calling jPCA trajectories projections of processed data rather than posterior latent-state trajectories (Cunningham and Yu 2014).

These sources do not supply this Toy Model’s dimensions, matrix values, embeddings, initial states, time grid, trial counts, noise level, windows, jitter, random planes, input functions, shuffle proposal budget, or tolerances. Those are frozen LDG design choices.



The bounded implementation and deterministic artifacts are reconciled with this record at L1/stable after independent scientific and implementation focused PASS, repository validation, target/index/full-site renders, and mechanical promotion under the recorded review decision.



The executor ran structural, target-render, and diff checks; the implementation owner ran generation and artifact verification; and the parent orchestrator completed repository-wide tests, index/control reconciliation, review integration, and stable promotion. This records completed role separation rather than pending work.

title: Rotational Projection Versus Alternatives
text:
Complete L1/stable Toy Model schema and exact five-file implementation contract.
Positive six-dimensional generator, correct skew blocks, isometric observed embedding, and independent splits are frozen.
Observed and PCA-represented true rotational-plane targets are explicit.
Symmetric, latency, input-driven, and nonorthogonal controls are separated.
Rank-six PCA, unrestricted, true skew-constrained, symmetric, fixed/random-plane, and input-aware methods are defined.
Full/short windows, jitter, smoothing, subtraction, matched shuffle, and input-aware stresses are bounded.
Derivative, angle, rate, tangential/radial, occupancy, and stability metrics are defined.
Condition boundaries, split leakage, applicability, and deterministic oracles are explicit.
Projection, oscillator, autonomy, vector-field, causality, metric, and mechanism limits are explicit.
External evidence depth and limitations are recorded.
Deterministic empirical artifacts integrated.
Independent scientific review PASS after focused re-review of input consistency, metric applicability, shuffle selection, and stability.
Independent implementation review PASS after focused re-review of all eight numerical, leakage, manifest, and figure findings.

title: Label-Dependent Demixing
text:
This L1/stable Candidate C Toy Model is a supervised generation/recovery demonstration. It asks whether balanced ANOVA-style task marginalizations and a bounded reduced-rank dPCA map recover the declared label-dependent mean effects, and where that recovery fails. Numerical values are deterministic outputs under master seed 20260819; they are conditional on this simulator and protocol rather than population or real-data claims.
Assumed background: centered PCA, factorial means, linear subspaces, ridge regression, singular value decomposition, and independent train/validation/test trials.


For independent trials with time, binary stimulus, and binary decision labels:

can condition averaging recover the known time, stimulus, decision, and stimulus–decision interaction mean effects;
can global PCA, separate marginal PCA, and regularized rank-one dPCA preserve or isolate those effects on held-out trials;
how do oblique or nearly collinear mixing directions affect demixing;
what becomes invalid when a factorial cell is absent;
what information is lost by pseudo-population construction; and
how different are mean-map recovery and single-trial decoding or reconstruction?

The object keeps four distinctions explicit:

an effect is a feature-by-time-by-condition tensor;
a mixing direction is a feature-space vector multiplying that effect’s scalar temporal/label profile;
a marginal main effect and its time interaction are distinct full-factorial terms even when this object groups them into one time-dependent task marginalization; and
label predictability, marginal reconstruction, statistical independence, causality, and mechanism are different endpoints.

Machens separated task-associated covariance sources but explicitly did not assume statistical independence; Brendel, Romo, and Machens introduced factorial marginalizations and an earlier orthogonality-constrained dPCA; Kobak et al. replaced that formulation with separately fitted reduced-rank encoder/decoder maps that can represent nonorthogonal task subspaces (Machens 2010; Brendel et al. 2011; Kobak et al. 2016).





The ambient feature dimension is \(N=12\), the number of aligned time bins is \(T=24\), and labels are
\[
s,d\in\{-1,+1\}.
\]
For trial \(k\) in cell \((s,d)\), the observed feature vector at time \(t\) is
\[
x_k(t,s,d)
=
G_t(t)+G_s(t,s)+G_d(t,d)+G_{sd}(t,s,d)+\varepsilon_k(t),
\]
where
\[
G_t(t)=a_t f_t(t),
\]
\[
G_s(t,s)=a_s\,s f_s(t),\qquad
G_d(t,d)=a_d\,d f_d(t),
\]
and
\[
G_{sd}(t,s,d)=a_{sd}\,sd f_{sd}(t).
\]
The four \(a_\phi\in\mathbb R^{12}\) are unit feature-space mixing directions. The four \(G_\phi\) are the ground-truth marginal effect tensors. A recovered decoder direction is not itself an effect tensor, and a recovered encoder direction is not interpreted as a causal source.



Normalize the columns below separately, without orthogonalizing them:
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_t={}&(1.0,0.3,-0.2,0.5,0,0.4,-0.6,0.2,0.1,-0.3,0.7,-0.1)^\top,\\
r_s={}&(0.2,1.0,0.4,-0.3,0.6,-0.2,0.3,-0.7,0.1,0.5,-0.4,0.2)^\top,\\
r_d={}&(-0.4,0.2,1.0,0.5,-0.2,0.7,-0.1,0.3,-0.6,0.2,0.4,-0.5)^\top,\\
r_{sd}={}&(0.5,-0.3,0.2,1.0,0.4,-0.6,0.2,0.1,0.7,-0.2,0.3,0.4)^\top,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
a_\phi=r_\phi/\lVert r_\phi\rVert_2.
\]
The implementation records the complete Gram matrix \(a_\phi^\top a_\psi\). These directions are deliberately oblique. dPCA is not allowed to assume that different task effects occupy orthogonal subspaces; the 2016 formulation specifically permits nonorthogonal encoder/decoder axes (Kobak et al. 2016).



Let \(u_t=(t-1)/(T-1)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
f_t(u) &= 0.7\sin(2\pi u)+0.35(u-0.5),\\
f_s(u) &= 1.25\exp\!\left[-\left(\frac{u-0.35}{0.18}\right)^2\right]-0.25,\\
f_d(u) &= \frac{1.1}{1+\exp[-12(u-0.58)]}-0.55,\\
f_{sd}(u) &= 0.85\sin(3\pi u)\exp(-1.3u).
\end{aligned}
\]
The effect amplitudes multiplying these profiles are
\[
(\alpha_t,\alpha_s,\alpha_d,\alpha_{sd})=(1.00,1.35,1.15,0.75).
\]
Thus \(G_\phi\) uses \(\alpha_\phi f_\phi\). Because \(f_s\), \(f_d\), and \(f_{sd}\) need not have zero temporal mean, each grouped task effect contains both a pure label main effect and a label-by-time interaction:
\[
f_s(t)=\bar f_s+[f_s(t)-\bar f_s],
\]
so \(a_s s\bar f_s\) is the pure stimulus term and \(a_s s[f_s(t)-\bar f_s]\) is the stimulus–time term. The analogous decomposition applies to decision and stimulus–decision interaction. Grouping these terms later does not erase their conceptual distinction.



Trials are independent. At each trial and time bin,
\[
\varepsilon_k(t)\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\varepsilon),
\]
independently over trials and time bins, with
\[
\Sigma_\varepsilon=0.16I_{12}+0.10vv^\top,
\qquad
v=\frac{(1,2,\ldots,12)^\top}{\lVert(1,2,\ldots,12)\rVert_2}.
\]
The rank-one term creates simultaneous cross-feature trial noise. It exists so the pseudo-population control can preserve feature-wise condition means while destroying simultaneous noise covariance. This noise is not a latent task effect and is excluded from the noiseless marginal truth.




Generation, condition-mean estimation, marginalization, fitting, regularization selection, scoring, and plotting are separate functions. The retained noiseless effects and exact mixing directions are provided only to scoring and implementation oracles.
For the balanced and nearly collinear conditions, each split contains the following number of independent trials per \((s,d)\) cell:



Split
Trials per cell
Total trials




train
40
160


validation
20
80


test
30
120



Train, validation, and test trials are generated independently rather than partitioned from one realized array. Time bins from one trial never cross split boundaries.
The master seed is 20260819. All random streams use Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence(words))) with explicit condition, split, cell, trial, shuffle, feature-permutation, and method codes recorded in the manifest. Python’s process-dependent hash is prohibited.



The fixed fitting contract is:

four grouped marginalizations: time, stimulus_time, decision_time, and interaction_time;
one component per grouped marginalization;
rank-four global PCA, matching the maximum combined signal rank;
rank-one separate PCA for each marginalization;
dPCA ridge grid \[
\lambda\in\{10^{-4},10^{-2},1,100\};
\]
one common dPCA \(\lambda\) selected by the mean validation normalized marginal reconstruction error across all four groups, with the smaller \(\lambda\) winning exact ties;
trial-level ridge-decoder grid \[
\lambda_{\mathrm{decode}}\in\{10^{-3},10^{-1},10\},
\] selected separately for stimulus and decision by validation accuracy, then smaller-\(\lambda\) tie breaking;
covariance/marginal algebra tolerance \(10^{-10}\);
leakage and fitted-output poison tolerance \(10^{-12}\); and
byte-identical deterministic regeneration.

The grids are finite LDG design choices. They are not claims that the selected values are universal or that the search recovers a population-optimal regularization parameter.





All four label cells are present with equal trial counts. The fixed oblique directions and profiles above define the primary condition. The full noiseless mean tensor has rank at most four in feature space.



For each split, estimate
\[
\bar X(t,s,d)=\frac{1}{K_{sd}}
\sum_{k=1}^{K_{sd}}x_k(t,s,d).
\]
In the balanced condition, every cell receives equal weight after averaging. Trial count affects precision but not the factorial estimand.



Let
\[
\mu_t(t)=\frac14\sum_{s,d}\bar X(t,s,d),
\qquad
\mu=\frac1T\sum_t\mu_t(t).
\]
After subtracting the grand mean \(\mu\), define replicated grouped terms
\[
X_t(t,s,d)=\mu_t(t)-\mu,
\]
\[
X_s(t,s,d)=\frac12\sum_{d'}\bar X(t,s,d')-\mu_t(t),
\]
\[
X_d(t,s,d)=\frac12\sum_{s'}\bar X(t,s',d)-\mu_t(t),
\]
and
\[
X_{sd}(t,s,d)=
\bar X(t,s,d)-\mu_t(t)-X_s(t,s,d)-X_d(t,s,d).
\]
These satisfy
\[
\bar X-\mu=X_t+X_s+X_d+X_{sd}
\]
and are mutually orthogonal in the equal-cell Frobenius inner product, up to floating-point tolerance. The grouped stimulus term equals the full-factorial sum \(X_s^{\mathrm{main}}+X_{ts}\); the decision term equals \(X_d^{\mathrm{main}}+X_{td}\); and the interaction term equals \(X_{sd}^{\mathrm{main}}+X_{tsd}\). This grouping follows the canonical presentation while remaining an analyst-declared estimand (Brendel et al. 2011; Kobak et al. 2016).



The generated artifacts report:

byte-identical manifest, metrics, diagnostics, and PNG



The saturated primary decoder accuracies are not treated as discriminating evidence for demixing. Their independently refit label-shuffle nulls establish that the generator contains strong label information, not that dPCA discovers an independent or causal representation. Under the frozen joint-pair shuffle, refit stimulus/decision decoder accuracies fall to 0.483/0.542. The nearly collinear condition preserves small direction-angle errors while substantially degrading assigned marginal isolation, illustrating that recovering a direction and separating overlapping label effects are different criteria.




The single summary.png contains at most four panels:

one true and held-out estimated stimulus-marginal time course projected onto its known mixing direction;
the complete labelled balanced-condition dPCA normalized confusion matrix;
negative-control summaries for joint label shuffling, decoder nulls, the missing cell, pseudo-population construction, and mean-versus-single-trial transfer; and
executable generator, leakage, marginal-algebra, solve/rank, and interpretation checks.

The in-figure interpretation lines state that labels supervise the decomposition, encoder and decoder axes may be nonorthogonal, decoding is a separate endpoint, and demixing does not mean independence, causality, or mechanism. The negative-control panel distinguishes condition-mean from noiseless and noisy single-trial transfer. Visual separation is not an acceptance oracle; the condition-by-method errors and encoder angles remain in metrics.csv rather than duplicating the bounded matrix/time-course figure.




Balanced empirical condition means should approach the known mean-effect tensors as independent trial counts increase.
Global PCA may reconstruct the combined mean signal well without assigning individual components to task labels.
Separate marginal PCA should compress each provided marginal effectively, but it is given the marginal target directly and therefore does not demonstrate isolation from the full mean tensor.
Regularized dPCA should trade marginal isolation against reconstruction by learning a map from the full condition-mean tensor to each target marginal (Kobak et al. 2016).
Encoder directions may align with true mixing directions, while decoder directions need not: with oblique effects, dPCA can use a nonorthogonal readout/reconstruction pair.
Near-collinear stimulus and decision directions should increase cross-marginal confusion or instability. The empirical direction and magnitude are reported rather than guaranteed.
A missing factorial cell makes the balanced four-cell marginalization unidentified from the observed training design. A pseudoinverse extrapolation is a diagnostic, not valid recovery.
Joint label shuffling should remove systematic label alignment in expectation while preserving observations and cell counts.
Feature-wise pseudo-population permutation should preserve each feature’s condition means exactly but alter simultaneous cross-feature trial covariance and potentially change single-trial decoding.
A condition-mean-trained map can generalize to independent condition means while performing materially differently on noisy single trials. One endpoint does not validate the other.






Use the primary generator, all four complete cells, and the balanced counts above. This is the only condition used for primary marginal-recovery acceptance.



Keep \(a_s\) fixed. Let
\[
r_\perp=
\frac{a_d-a_s(a_s^\top a_d)}
{\lVert a_d-a_s(a_s^\top a_d)\rVert_2}
\]
and replace
\[
a_d^{\mathrm{collinear}}
=
\frac{a_s+0.06r_\perp}{\lVert a_s+0.06r_\perp\rVert_2}.
\]
The resulting acute angle is approximately \(\arctan(0.06)=3.43^\circ\). Labels remain balanced and the temporal profiles remain different. True stimulus and decision marginal effects still exist, but their feature-space directions are practically difficult to separate. Report full confusion and stability; do not force a binary pass/fail based only on one angle.



Use cell order
\[
(-1,-1),\ (-1,+1),\ (+1,-1),\ (+1,+1)
\]
with counts:



Split
Cell counts




train
\((40,30,16,0)\)


validation
\((20,15,8,0)\)


test
\((30,30,30,30)\)



The fourth training and validation cell is absent. Therefore the full intercept/stimulus/decision/interaction design has rank below four, and the balanced factorial mean tensor is not identified from those splits. The implementation may compute a minimum-norm weighted least-squares or pseudoinverse extrapolation for a named negative-control diagnostic, but it must record the design rank and label every resulting marginal, dPCA fit, and test score invalid as balanced-cell recovery. It may not silently fill the cell, apply the balanced formulas, or treat extrapolation as observed condition evidence.
If a future variant uses unequal but nonzero counts, it must first estimate each cell mean and then assign explicit equal-cell weights to target the balanced factorial estimand. Trial-frequency weighting answers a different question and must receive a different label.



For the balanced condition, jointly permute the \((s,d)\) label pairs among complete training trials using fixed shuffle seeds while preserving the exact four cell counts. Observations, validation labels, and test labels remain unchanged. Use one frozen shuffle for the complete dPCA negative-control fit and 32 predeclared shuffle seeds for stimulus/decision decoding null summaries.
Every shuffled fit repeats condition-mean estimation, marginalization, regularization selection, fitting, and scoring. Shuffling only component labels after fitting is prohibited. Shuffled results are null controls, not alternative scientific decompositions.



Within each split and \((s,d)\) cell, independently permute whole-trial identities for each feature. A feature’s complete 24-bin trajectory moves together, but different features generally come from different original trials. This construction:

preserves labels and every feature’s cell-wise condition mean exactly;
preserves each feature’s univariate trial distribution;
destroys simultaneous feature-to-feature trial identity and changes the rank-one noise covariance contribution; and
cannot support claims about simultaneously available population noise correlations.

Mean-based marginalizations and condition-mean dPCA maps should therefore remain equal within the declared algebra tolerance. The realized maximum fitted-map discrepancy is \(8.52\times10^{-15}\), consistent with floating-point summation order rather than a scientific change. Trial-level covariance and decoding may change. Any apparent improvement is not evidence that pseudo-populations are superior data; it reflects a changed noise structure.



Fit dPCA only on training condition means. Evaluate the frozen maps in two distinct ways:

Mean-map transfer: apply each map to independent validation/test condition-mean tensors and compare with their empirical balanced marginals.
Single-trial transfer: apply the same maps to each centered test trial and compare with the corresponding noiseless generator effect tensor for that trial’s \((s,d)\) labels. Also report reconstruction against the noisy observed trial as a separately named descriptive metric.

The second endpoint contains trial noise absent from the fit objective. It is not a likelihood and is not expected to equal condition-mean performance.




The implementation and verifier must assert:

Shape and split integrity: every trial array has shape (trials, 24, 12); all trial identifiers are disjoint across train, validation, and test.
Generator algebra: noiseless trial signals equal the sum of the four declared effects within \(10^{-12}\).
Balanced marginal algebra: grouped marginals sum to the centered condition-mean tensor within \(10^{-10}\) and are pairwise Frobenius-orthogonal under uniform cell weighting.
Truth access boundary: replacing every retained noiseless signal, effect, profile, and mixing-direction array leaves fitted means, marginalizations, lambda selection, PCA, dPCA, decoders, and observation-only predictions unchanged.
No test leakage: poisoning test observations or labels leaves training and validation preprocessing, condition means, selected lambdas, fitted maps, and decoder parameters unchanged.
No validation leakage into candidates: candidate dPCA maps use training means only; validation chooses among already fitted grid candidates; test never selects a candidate.
PCA oracle: global PCA’s projector matches the centered condition-mean SVD rank-four projector within \(10^{-10}\).
Reduced-rank oracle: every dPCA map has numerical rank at most one and agrees with the declared ridge-map-plus-leading-SVD construction within \(10^{-10}\).
Finite solves: every regularized Gram matrix is symmetric and positive definite for the positive grid; the selected map is finite. The unregularized boundary is not in this grid.
Lambda selection: the stored dPCA lambda equals the minimum validation mean normalized marginal error under the frozen tie rule; decoder lambdas equal their independent validation-accuracy selections.
Direction applicability: dPCA and separate-PCA encoder directions receive marginal-direction angles; dPCA decoder directions do not masquerade as generative mixing directions. Global PCA receives only a combined-signal-subspace angle.
Full confusion reporting: all 16 recovered-marginal/source-marginal energy entries exist; a scalar demixing index cannot replace them.
Shuffle integrity: the joint-label permutation preserves cell counts exactly, changes labels, leaves observations unchanged, and refits all supervised steps.
Missing-cell guard: the absent-cell design rank is recorded as deficient; no metric from that fit is labelled valid balanced recovery.
Pseudo-population oracle: labels and feature-wise cell means are exactly preserved, while at least one off-diagonal trial-noise covariance changes by more than numerical tolerance.
Trial-averaging labels: mean-map and single-trial rows use different targets and metric names.
Metric schema: all metric keys are unique, labels are nonempty, values are finite, and inapplicable metrics are omitted rather than encoded as zero.
Determinism: clean temporary regeneration yields byte-identical manifest.json, metrics.csv, diagnostics.json, and summary.png.

These checks establish reproducibility and implementation consistency, not causal or biological validity.




Balanced formulas on a missing cell: a fabricated or silently extrapolated cell invalidates the factorial estimand.
Trial-frequency weighting called balanced marginalization: unequal counts then change the target and confound main effects with label prevalence.
Time bins split across folds: adjacent bins from one trial are not independent held-out units.
Marginal truth passed to fitting: true effects or directions may be used only for final simulation scoring and implementation oracles.
Separate marginal PCA called demixing: it receives the marginal target directly and need not isolate that target from full activity.
Global PCA components assigned task labels post hoc: a rank-four signal subspace does not provide a unique labelled basis.
Decoder aligned to encoder by force: oblique encoder/decoder geometry is part of the dPCA solution, not an error to rotate away using truth.
Only the largest demixing label reported: a high maximum can hide substantial cross-marginal energy.
Shuffle performed after fitting: this does not test the supervised fitting pipeline.
Pseudo-population decoding treated as simultaneous population decoding: independently permuted features do not coexist on one trial.
Condition-mean recovery generalized to single trials: trial averaging suppresses noise and is part of the estimand.
Decoding equated with reconstruction or representation: accuracy tests label predictability under a classifier protocol, not preservation of the mean tensor or a unique internal code.
Demixing equated with independence: different marginal components can be correlated and axes can be nonorthogonal (Machens 2010; Kobak et al. 2016).
Supervised labels treated as causal variables: an experimentally supplied label can correlate with omitted variables, choices, errors, or selection procedures.
Time marginal called dynamics: indexed temporal variation is not a transition law, vector field, autonomous system, or mechanism.
Clean plots replace held-out metrics: visualization does not verify marginal algebra, transfer, leakage, or label handling.






The direct condition-mean record reports empirical train/validation/test marginal tensors and their normalized error against the retained noiseless generator effects. This measures sampling error before dimensionality reduction. It is not a learned projection method.



For flattened centered condition means \(X\in\mathbb R^{12\times96}\) and each grouped marginal \(X_\phi\):

global PCA fits one rank-four projector \(P\) on training \(X\) and reconstructs held-out marginal \(\phi\) as \(PX_\phi^{\mathrm{test}}\); equivalently, linear marginalization of \(PX^{\mathrm{test}}\) yields the same term;
separate marginal PCA fits a rank-one projector \(P_\phi\) on training \(X_\phi\) and reconstructs \(P_\phi X_\phi^{\mathrm{test}}\);
dPCA fits a rank-one map \(A_\phi\) from full training \(X\) to target \(X_\phi\) and reconstructs \(A_\phi X^{\mathrm{test}}\).

These are not the same information problem. Separate marginal PCA is a compression reference; dPCA must isolate a marginal from the full input.



For each positive grid value \(\lambda\), compute
\[
A_{\phi,\lambda}
=
X_\phi X^\top(XX^\top+\lambda I)^{-1}
\]
using a linear solve. Let \(u_{\phi,\lambda}\) be the leading left singular vector of \(A_{\phi,\lambda}X\). Set
\[
F_{\phi,\lambda}=u_{\phi,\lambda},
\qquad
D_{\phi,\lambda}=u_{\phi,\lambda}^\top A_{\phi,\lambda},
\]
and
\[
\widehat X_\phi=F_{\phi,\lambda}D_{\phi,\lambda}X.
\]
This is a deterministic ridge map followed by rank-one spectral truncation, a bounded reduced-rank regression construction consistent with the stable Method. Reduced-rank regression constrains the rank of a multivariate coefficient matrix; its encoder/decoder factorization is nonunique without a convention (Izenman 2008, sec. 6.3.2).



Decoding is a separate trial-level endpoint. Flatten each complete trial into \(24\times12=288\) features. For stimulus and decision separately:

fit feature mean and scale on training trials only;
fit ridge least-squares binary classifiers for the predeclared decoder grid;
select lambda by validation accuracy with smaller-lambda tie breaking; and
report untouched test accuracy and the 32-shuffle null distribution; the exactly balanced test labels make ordinary and balanced accuracy identical.

The classifier is not used to fit dPCA or choose its components. High decoding accuracy does not establish marginal reconstruction, statistical independence, causal relevance, or a unique representation.





Empirical condition means and marginal contrasts. No learned projection; report sampling error and the visible label effects directly.
Time-only condition-mean baseline. Retain the training condition-independent time marginal and set label-dependent marginals to zero. This is not a full mean-only reconstruction.
Global rank-four PCA. Fit one unsupervised principal subspace to the complete training condition-mean tensor. Score combined reconstruction and the angle to the combined true signal span, not per-label component identity.
Separate rank-one marginal PCA. Fit one PCA to each supplied training marginal. This tests compressibility of the marginal but not isolation from the full tensor.
Regularized rank-one-per-marginal dPCA. Fit the declared ridge map plus SVD independently for time, stimulus, decision, and interaction. Select one shared dPCA lambda on validation means only.
Trial-level ridge decoding. Fit stimulus and decision classifiers independently of the dPCA objective and report as a separate endpoint.
Joint-label shuffle controls. Refit supervised condition means, dPCA candidates, lambda selection, and decoders from shuffled training labels.
Pseudo-population control. Preserve condition means while destroying simultaneous trial identity, then compare mean maps, noise covariance, and trial decoding.

No method is called an independent-component method, a causal decomposition, or a latent-state model.





For applicable method \(m\) and marginal \(\phi\), report
\[
\operatorname{NMSE}_{m,\phi}
=
\frac{\lVert X_\phi^{\mathrm{test}}-widehat X_{m,\phi}^{\mathrm{test}}\rVert_F^2}
{\lVert X_\phi^{\mathrm{test}}\rVert_F^2}.
\]
A zero-energy denominator is a declared not-applicable boundary rather than replaced by a favorable constant. Report train, validation, and test separately where used.



For dPCA,
\[
\widehat X^{\mathrm{test}}=\sum_\phi
F_\phi D_\phi X^{\mathrm{test}}.
\]
Report normalized combined error against the centered held-out condition-mean tensor. Global PCA uses \(PX^{\mathrm{test}}\). Separate marginal PCA uses \(\sum_\phi P_\phi X_\phi^{\mathrm{test}}\) and is explicitly labelled as target-supplied marginal compression.



For balanced centered condition means,
\[
q_\phi=\frac{\lVert X_\phi\rVert_F^2}
{\sum_\psi\lVert X_\psi\rVert_F^2}.
\]
Report population-truth, train, validation, and test fractions. These describe the chosen equal-cell tensor and are not additive component variances across nonorthogonal dPCA axes.



For a unit estimated encoder \(\widehat f_\phi\) and true unit mixing direction \(a_\phi\), report the acute rank-one principal angle
\[
\theta_\phi=
\arccos\left(\left|\widehat f_\phi^\top a_\phi\right|\right).
\]
Apply this to separate marginal PCA encoders and dPCA encoders. Do not score dPCA decoder rows against \(a_\phi\). For global PCA, compare its complete rank-four subspace with
\[
\operatorname{span}(a_t,a_s,a_d,a_{sd})
\]
using all four principal angles and the projector Frobenius distance. In the nearly collinear condition, report conditioning and angle instability without pretending that two almost coincident directions are strongly practically identified.



For recovered marginal map \(A_\phi\) and each true or held-out source marginal \(X_\psi\), report all entries
\[
C_{\phi\leftarrow\psi}
=
\frac{\lVert A_\phi X_\psi\rVert_F^2}
{\sum_{\rho}\lVert A_\phi X_\rho\rVert_F^2}.
\]
Also report decoder-score profiles
\[
v_{\phi\leftarrow\psi}
=
\lVert D_\phi X_\psi\rVert_F^2.
\]
Rows and columns are explicitly labelled. The implementation stores raw map-output energy, the row-normalized confusion fraction \(C\), and decoder-score energy separately. It also reports an assigned_marginal_fraction equal to the diagonal confusion entry. A scalar demixing index
\[
\max_\psi v_{\phi\leftarrow\psi}/
\sum_\psi v_{\phi\leftarrow\psi}
\]
uses the maximum source fraction and may supplement but never replace the complete profile. It differs from the assigned fraction when an off-target source dominates, as in the nearly collinear decision control. Nonzero off-target entries mean cross-marginal sensitivity under this design, not causal mixing.



Report stimulus and decision test accuracy, selected decoder lambda, and the 32-shuffle median, interval, and exceedance count. Test labels are exactly balanced, so ordinary and balanced accuracy coincide and are not duplicated. Interaction decoding is omitted from the primary endpoint because four-way condition classification is a different multiclass task. Decoding results remain separate from marginal reconstruction tables.



For every dPCA grid value, report validation NMSE by marginal and their unweighted mean. Store the selected lambda and tie rule. Test metrics are computed once after selection and cannot change the choice.



Every metrics.csv row contains exactly:
split,condition,method,marginal,target,metric,value
Values are finite numeric. Inapplicable rows are omitted and explained in diagnostics.json; they are not encoded as zero or NaN. Missing-cell recovery rows contain the exact target prefix invalid_rank_deficient_balanced_recovery and cannot be pooled with valid recovery rows.




The primary balanced condition tests recovery of a declared supervised mean decomposition. A small dPCA marginal reconstruction error means that one regularized linear map transfers from full training means to an independently estimated held-out marginal under the same labels and equal-cell measure. It does not imply that the labelled effect is statistically independent, uniquely represented, anatomically separate, causally generated by the label, or mechanistic.
Global PCA can preserve the combined signal span without assigning task semantics. Separate marginal PCA can recover a marginal direction after the marginal is supplied. dPCA addresses the harder isolation problem by using labels to define a target and fitting an oblique encoder/decoder map. Label supervision is part of the method, not external validation.






TipLDG synthesis



Demixing is relative to a declared label algebra, averaging measure, grouping convention, rank, regularization, and reconstruction loss. Changing any of those choices changes the estimand. A useful demixed display is therefore a reproducible supervised summary, not discovery of independent latent generators.






It does not establish statistical independence among components or effects.
It does not establish causal separation, intervention effects, or mechanistic modules.
It does not prove that stimulus or decision labels are uniquely represented in the features.
It does not turn decoding accuracy into evidence of representation, necessity, or biological meaning.
It does not infer latent states, transition dynamics, a vector field, or an autonomous system.
It does not claim that smooth mean trajectories are dynamics; they are fixed time-indexed profiles plus trial averaging.
It does not prove manifold structure, topology, nonlinear geometry, or intrinsic dimension.
It does not identify a unique encoder/decoder factorization beyond the declared rank-one sign convention.
It does not make pseudo-population trials simultaneous observations.
It does not validate balanced marginalization when a factorial cell is missing.
It does not claim that mean-level reconstruction predicts single-trial performance.
It does not claim universal superiority of dPCA over PCA, marginal PCA, or decoding.




A real-data analysis would need to define the true independent unit, simultaneity of recording, alignment events, binning/smoothing, feature scaling, label coding, missing cells, label correlations, cell weights, trial exclusions, sessions/subjects, and the grouping of interactions. Trial, session, or subject splits must prevent correlated observations from crossing folds.
If cells are missing, an explicit parametric model, scientifically justified weighting estimand, or redesigned experiment is required; balanced formulas cannot manufacture the absent contrast. If labels are correlated—such as stimulus and decision with few error trials—separate marginal interpretations depend on those rare cells and the chosen estimand. Pseudo-populations cannot estimate simultaneous noise correlations. Condition-mean dPCA should be supplemented by independent single-trial and session-level checks rather than backdating mean-map performance into trial-level claims.

title: Label-Dependent Demixing
Label-Dependent Demixing
text:
The ambient feature dimension is \(N=12\), the number of aligned time bins is \(T=24\), and labels are
\[
s,d\in\{-1,+1\}.
\]
For trial \(k\) in cell \((s,d)\), the observed feature vector at time \(t\) is
\[
x_k(t,s,d)
=
G_t(t)+G_s(t,s)+G_d(t,d)+G_{sd}(t,s,d)+\varepsilon_k(t),
\]
where
\[
G_t(t)=a_t f_t(t),
\]
\[
G_s(t,s)=a_s\,s f_s(t),\qquad
G_d(t,d)=a_d\,d f_d(t),
\]
and
\[
G_{sd}(t,s,d)=a_{sd}\,sd f_{sd}(t).
\]
The four \(a_\phi\in\mathbb R^{12}\) are unit feature-space mixing directions. The four \(G_\phi\) are the ground-truth marginal effect tensors. A recovered decoder direction is not itself an effect tensor, and a recovered encoder direction is not interpreted as a causal source.



Normalize the columns below separately, without orthogonalizing them:
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_t={}&(1.0,0.3,-0.2,0.5,0,0.4,-0.6,0.2,0.1,-0.3,0.7,-0.1)^\top,\\
r_s={}&(0.2,1.0,0.4,-0.3,0.6,-0.2,0.3,-0.7,0.1,0.5,-0.4,0.2)^\top,\\
r_d={}&(-0.4,0.2,1.0,0.5,-0.2,0.7,-0.1,0.3,-0.6,0.2,0.4,-0.5)^\top,\\
r_{sd}={}&(0.5,-0.3,0.2,1.0,0.4,-0.6,0.2,0.1,0.7,-0.2,0.3,0.4)^\top,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
a_\phi=r_\phi/\lVert r_\phi\rVert_2.
\]
The implementation records the complete Gram matrix \(a_\phi^\top a_\psi\). These directions are deliberately oblique. dPCA is not allowed to assume that different task effects occupy orthogonal subspaces; the 2016 formulation specifically permits nonorthogonal encoder/decoder axes (Kobak et al. 2016).



Let \(u_t=(t-1)/(T-1)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
f_t(u) &= 0.7\sin(2\pi u)+0.35(u-0.5),\\
f_s(u) &= 1.25\exp\!\left[-\left(\frac{u-0.35}{0.18}\right)^2\right]-0.25,\\
f_d(u) &= \frac{1.1}{1+\exp[-12(u-0.58)]}-0.55,\\
f_{sd}(u) &= 0.85\sin(3\pi u)\exp(-1.3u).
\end{aligned}
\]
The effect amplitudes multiplying these profiles are
\[
(\alpha_t,\alpha_s,\alpha_d,\alpha_{sd})=(1.00,1.35,1.15,0.75).
\]
Thus \(G_\phi\) uses \(\alpha_\phi f_\phi\). Because \(f_s\), \(f_d\), and \(f_{sd}\) need not have zero temporal mean, each grouped task effect contains both a pure label main effect and a label-by-time interaction:
\[
f_s(t)=\bar f_s+[f_s(t)-\bar f_s],
\]
so \(a_s s\bar f_s\) is the pure stimulus term and \(a_s s[f_s(t)-\bar f_s]\) is the stimulus–time term. The analogous decomposition applies to decision and stimulus–decision interaction. Grouping these terms later does not erase their conceptual distinction.



Trials are independent. At each trial and time bin,
\[
\varepsilon_k(t)\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\varepsilon),
\]
independently over trials and time bins, with
\[
\Sigma_\varepsilon=0.16I_{12}+0.10vv^\top,
\qquad
v=\frac{(1,2,\ldots,12)^\top}{\lVert(1,2,\ldots,12)\rVert_2}.
\]
The rank-one term creates simultaneous cross-feature trial noise. It exists so the pseudo-population control can preserve feature-wise condition means while destroying simultaneous noise covariance. This noise is not a latent task effect and is excluded from the noiseless marginal truth.

title: Label-Dependent Demixing
Label-Dependent Demixing
text:
All four label cells are present with equal trial counts. The fixed oblique directions and profiles above define the primary condition. The full noiseless mean tensor has rank at most four in feature space.



For each split, estimate
\[
\bar X(t,s,d)=\frac{1}{K_{sd}}
\sum_{k=1}^{K_{sd}}x_k(t,s,d).
\]
In the balanced condition, every cell receives equal weight after averaging. Trial count affects precision but not the factorial estimand.



Let
\[
\mu_t(t)=\frac14\sum_{s,d}\bar X(t,s,d),
\qquad
\mu=\frac1T\sum_t\mu_t(t).
\]
After subtracting the grand mean \(\mu\), define replicated grouped terms
\[
X_t(t,s,d)=\mu_t(t)-\mu,
\]
\[
X_s(t,s,d)=\frac12\sum_{d'}\bar X(t,s,d')-\mu_t(t),
\]
\[
X_d(t,s,d)=\frac12\sum_{s'}\bar X(t,s',d)-\mu_t(t),
\]
and
\[
X_{sd}(t,s,d)=
\bar X(t,s,d)-\mu_t(t)-X_s(t,s,d)-X_d(t,s,d).
\]
These satisfy
\[
\bar X-\mu=X_t+X_s+X_d+X_{sd}
\]
and are mutually orthogonal in the equal-cell Frobenius inner product, up to floating-point tolerance. The grouped stimulus term equals the full-factorial sum \(X_s^{\mathrm{main}}+X_{ts}\); the decision term equals \(X_d^{\mathrm{main}}+X_{td}\); and the interaction term equals \(X_{sd}^{\mathrm{main}}+X_{tsd}\). This grouping follows the canonical presentation while remaining an analyst-declared estimand (Brendel et al. 2011; Kobak et al. 2016).
