\begin{aligned}
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(x)\bigr)
&=\phi_\tau(xe^{as})\\
&=(xe^{as})e^{a\tau}\\
&=xe^{a(\tau+s)}\\
&=\phi_{\tau+s}(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
生成元：
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}
=
\left.a xe^{a\tau}\right|_{\tau=0}
=
ax
=
f(x).
\]
该示例使三个层级显式：\(f(x)=ax\) 给出瞬时变化，\(\phi_\tau(x)=xe^{a\tau}\) 给出跨初始状态的有限时间演化，选择一个 \(x_0\) 产生一条轨迹。



对有界二维示例，设状态为
\[
z(t)=
\begin{pmatrix}
x(t)\\
y(t)
\end{pmatrix}
\in\mathbb{R}^2
\]
并固定参数 \(a,\omega\in\mathbb{R}\)。考虑自治 IVP
\[
\dot z=Az,
\qquad
A=
\begin{pmatrix}
a & -\omega\\
\omega & a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
z(t_0)=z_0.
\]
定义平面旋转矩阵
\[
R(\theta)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & \cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
用经过时间 \(\tau=t-t_0\)，提出
\[
z(t_0+\tau)
=
e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z_0.
\]
当 \(\omega\neq0\) 时，旋转改变角位置而因子 \(e^{a\tau}\) 改变半径：\(a<0\) 给出向内螺旋，\(a=0\) 给出恒定半径旋转，\(a>0\) 给出向外螺旋。这些描述只关乎这个声明系统；它们不从绘制轨迹推断螺旋动力学。


在零经过时间，\(e^{a\cdot0}=1\) 且 \(R(0)=I\)，因此
\[
z(t_0)=e^0R(0)z_0=z_0.
\]
设
\[
J=
\begin{pmatrix}
0 & -1\\
1 & 0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A=aI+\omega J.
\]
对正弦与余弦条目直接微分给出
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau}R(\omega\tau)
=
\omega J R(\omega\tau).
\]
因为 \(d\tau/dt=1\)，乘积法则给出
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot z(t_0+\tau)
&=
e^{a\tau}
\left[aI+\omega J\right]
R(\omega\tau)z_0\\
&=
A\left[e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z_0\right]\\
&=Az(t_0+\tau).
\end{aligned}
\]
因此所提曲线同时满足 ODE 与初始条件。




状态空间： \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^2\)。
状态值： \(z(t)=(x(t),y(t))^T\in\mathbb{R}^2\)。
向量场： \(f(z)=Az\)。
初始条件： \(z(t_0)=z_0\)。
轨迹： 对所选 \(z_0\)，\(t\mapsto e^{a(t-t_0)}R(\omega(t-t_0))z_0\)。
经过时间流：
\[
\phi_\tau(z)=e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z.
\]




恒等律立即可得：
\[
\phi_0(z)=e^0R(0)z=z.
\]
使用 \(e^{a\tau}e^{as}=e^{a(\tau+s)}\) 与平面旋转律 \(R(\alpha)R(\beta)=R(\alpha+\beta)\) 给出
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(z)\bigr)
&=
e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)
e^{as}R(\omega s)z\\
&=
e^{a(\tau+s)}R\bigl(\omega(\tau+s)\bigr)z\\
&=
\phi_{\tau+s}(z).
\end{aligned}
\]
该场在 \(\mathbb{R}^2\) 上全局利普希茨，因为对欧氏范数及其诱导矩阵范数，
\[
\|f(z)-f(w)\|
=
\|A(z-w)\|
\leq
\|A\|\,\|z-w\|.
\]
显式公式对每个 \(z\in\mathbb{R}^2\) 与每个有限 \(\tau\in\mathbb{R}\) 有限。因此受支持域是
\[
W=\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^2,
\]
所以该系统具有全局双侧流。每个 \(\phi_\tau\) 是逆为 \(\phi_{-\tau}\) 的全局定义双射。\(a>0\) 时向外增长在 \(\tau\to\infty\) 时无界，但不造成有限时间爆破。




现在考虑
\[
\dot{x}=\sqrt{|x|},
\qquad
x(0)=0,
\qquad
\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}.
\]
向量场 \(f(x)=\sqrt{|x|}\) 连续，因此 Peano 定理保证穿过 \((0,0)\) 至少一个局部解。它在 \(0\) 处不局部利普希茨，因为对 \(x\neq0\)，
\[
\frac{|f(x)-f(0)|}{|x-0|}
=
\frac{\sqrt{|x|}}{|x|}
=
\frac{1}{\sqrt{|x|}},
\]
在 \(x\to0\) 时无界。
一个解是
\[
x(t)=0.
\]
对每个等待时间 \(c\geq0\)，另一个解是
\[
x_c(t)=
\begin{cases}
0, & t\leq c,\\
\dfrac{(t-c)^2}{4}, & t\geq c.
\end{cases}
\]
对 \(t<c\)，\(\dot{x}_c(t)\) 与 \(\sqrt{|x_c(t)|}\) 都为零。对 \(t>c\)，
\[
\dot{x}_c(t)=\frac{t-c}{2}
=
\sqrt{\frac{(t-c)^2}{4}}
=
\sqrt{|x_c(t)|}.
\]
在 \(t=c\)，左右导数都为零，因此 \(x_c\) 在那里可微。因为 \(c\geq0\)，每条这样的曲线也满足 \(x_c(0)=0\)。因此同一 IVP 有无限多个解。这是 Teschl 平方根示例展示的标准非唯一性机制 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 1.3)。
教训是精确的：连续性在此支持存在性，但失败的局部利普希茨条件移除基本唯一性保证。因此 ODE 与初始状态单独不在正经过时间后确定唯一值 \(\phi_\tau(0)\)，从而不诱导唯一确定的单值流。

title: 一阶自治动力系统
text:
把方程当作曲线而非约束。 表达式 \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) 指定哪些可微曲线有资格作为解；它本身不是一条轨迹。
把存在性与唯一性等同。 连续场可以承认解，而不从初始状态选择恰好一个解。
把局部与全局等同。 局部利普希茨连续性给出局部存在性与唯一性，从而唯一极大延拓，而非全时解。
忽略声明域。 解必须保持在 \(\mathcal{X}\) 内。到达其边界可以在坐标值保持有界时结束极大解。
互换使用 \(t\) 与 \(\tau\)。 时钟时间相对 \(t_0\) 标记轨迹；经过时间索引自治演化映射。
把一条轨迹称为流。 一个固定 \(x_0\) 给出一条轨迹。流组织跨多个初始状态的演化，并必须在定义处满足恒等与复合。
假设每个向量场都有全局流。 即使光滑向量场也可以有限时间爆破。
从显示推断场。 绘制曲线或拟合箭头场本身不是唯一自治机制的证据。

该形式体系也并不蕴含：

每个观测时间序列都是动力系统轨迹；
每个时变潜表示都承认有效自治向量场；
一条观测轨迹唯一确定向量场，无论在未完全采样状态之外或沿其；
多条相似轨迹证明一个共享流；
预测成功确立机制正确性；
推断潜状态是唯一真实物理状态；
所有系统自治或连续时间；
所有科学相关状态空间欧氏；或
所有向量场生成全局流。

title: 一阶自治动力系统
text:
给定声明 \(f\)、\(x_0\) 与 \(t_0\)，数值 ODE 求解器在请求时间区间上近似一条解轨迹。步长、误差控制、刚度、域边界与有限时间发散影响计算是否可靠。数值输出不取代此处处理的解析问题：解是否存在、是否唯一，以及请求区间是否位于其极大域内。
流视角在计算上对应为许多初始状态与经过时间求解相同 ODE。有限模拟网格采样所提出的流；它不是完整映射 \(\Phi:W\to\mathcal{X}\)。同样，从数据估计 \(f\) 是涉及采样、观测、噪声、可辨识性与基线的单独方法问题。它不是本数学定义的一部分。

title: 一阶自治动力系统
text:
本对象形式化而非取代六个 Cycle 1 概念：



概念
在自治 IVP 中的形式角色




State
\(x(t)\) 是时钟时间 \(t\) 携带的状态值。


State Space
\(x(t)\in\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\)。


Initial Condition
\(x(t_0)=x_0\) 在参考时间锚定演化。


Vector Field
\(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) 赋予瞬时变化。


Trajectory
\(t\mapsto x(t)\) 是唯一性成立时由初始条件选择的一个解。


Flow
\((\tau,x_0)\mapsto\phi_\tau(x_0)\) 组织跨受支持初始状态的有限时间演化。



对 LDG，主要方法学边界是声明 ODE 模型内的数学自洽不是测得神经、行为或潜变量遵循该模型的经验证据。后续玩具模型可以使用本对象指定已知真值。真实数据主张将额外需要论证状态描述、观测模型、估计规程、更简单基线与区分自治共享规则与输入、非平稳性、被省略状态和测量伪迹的检验。

title: 一阶自治动力系统
text:
IVP 解的存在性、唯一性、光滑性、积分形式与延拓：(Teschl 2012年, ch. 2)。
演示全局演化、有限时间爆破与非唯一性的标量自治示例：(Teschl 2012年, sec. 1.3)。
极大积分曲线、受支持域 \(W\)、局部流复合与无穷小生成元：(Teschl 2012年, sec. 6.2)。

title: 一阶自治动力系统
text:
使用六个稳定 Cycle 1 概念作为规范前置知识。
以良类型化定义域与值域陈述自治欧氏 IVP。
分离连续性、局部利普希茨连续性与更强光滑性。
区分存在性与唯一性，以及局部、极大与全局解。
定义受支持局部流域，并只在定义处陈述恒等与复合。
通过零点导数把可微局部流与其向量场联系起来。
包含并验证完整 \(\dot{x}=ax\) 轨迹与流推导。
包含解析检查的二维旋转–伸缩轨迹与全局流。
包含检查的非唯一性示例与有界有限时间爆破边界。
陈述经验与建模非蕴含，而不进入被排除的下游主题。
完成一次内部数学一致性 / 红队遍历。
应用独立 L2 数学审查的有界修正。
独立聚焦复审确认修订陈述；所有者于 2026-08-18 批准晋升为 L2 / stable。

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
The six Cycle 1 Concepts distinguish a state, its state space, a trajectory, an initial condition, a vector field, and a flow. This Math Object connects those roles in one reusable continuous-time formulation:
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=f(x),
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
The differential equation is not merely a compact description of a plotted curve. It is a constraint on an unknown differentiable state trajectory. Existence, uniqueness, continuation, and finite-time flow statements require separate hypotheses. Making those hypotheses explicit is necessary before later LDG work can use an autonomous ODE as a generative model or recovery target.
The scope is deliberately narrow: \(\mathcal{X}\) is an open subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), time is continuous, and the rule is deterministic and autonomous. Discrete-time, stochastic, input-driven, explicitly time-dependent, and non-Euclidean systems are outside this object.




State: the state value carried by the model at a time.
State Space: the admissible values of that state.
Trajectory: one time-parameterized evolution.
Initial Condition: the assignment \(x(t_0)=x_0\).
Vector Field: the instantaneous state-change rule.
Flow: finite-time evolution across supported initial states.

Assumed background: elementary sets, functions, Euclidean vectors, single-variable differentiation and integration, the chain rule, and composition of functions.





Let
\[
\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n
\]
be open, and let
\[
f:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The equation
\[
\dot{x}=f(x)
\]
is a first-order autonomous ordinary differential equation. It is first-order because the highest derivative is \(\dot{x}\), and autonomous because the right-hand side depends on the current state \(x\) but not explicitly on clock time \(t\).
A solution on an interval \(I\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) is a differentiable curve
\[
x:I\rightarrow\mathcal{X}
\]
such that, for every \(t\in I\),
\[
\dot{x}(t)=f\bigl(x(t)\bigr).
\]
Thus \(x(t)\) is a state value in \(\mathcal{X}\), while both \(\dot{x}(t)\) and \(f(x(t))\) are vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). The equation requires the trajectory to be tangent to the vector assigned by \(f\) at every visited state.



For a reference time \(t_0\) and initial state \(x_0\in\mathcal{X}\), the initial-value problem (IVP) is
\[
\dot{x}=f(x),
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
A solution of the IVP must satisfy both the differential equation and the initial condition. The rule \(f\) describes possible instantaneous evolution across its domain; the initial condition selects the solution or set of solutions that pass through \(x_0\) at \(t_0\).




A local solution is defined on an open interval \(I\) containing \(t_0\).
A solution is maximal if it cannot be extended to a strictly larger interval while remaining a solution in \(\mathcal{X}\). If the IVP admits a unique local solution—that is, local solutions exist and any two compatible local solutions agree on their common domain—those local pieces assemble into one unique maximal solution on an open maximal interval
\[
I_{t_0,x_0}=(T_-(t_0,x_0),T_+(t_0,x_0)).
\]
A global solution in this object’s all-time setting is defined for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), so its maximal interval is \(\mathbb{R}\).

Local existence and uniqueness do not imply global existence. Under the same local solvability assumptions, if a maximal solution has a finite forward endpoint \(T_+\), then as \(t\uparrow T_+\) it eventually leaves every compact subset of \(\mathcal{X}\). When \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^n\), this means \(\|x(t)\|\to\infty\). On a proper open domain, the trajectory can instead remain bounded while approaching the complement of \(\mathcal{X}\); it need not converge to one particular boundary point. The analogous statements hold at a finite backward endpoint. Teschl separates local solvability from maximal continuation and states this compact-set criterion explicitly (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 2.6).



It is useful to measure time from the initial condition. Write
\[
\tau=t-t_0
\]
for elapsed time. For each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), suppose a unique maximal solution through \(x\) at elapsed time \(0\) is defined on an interval \(I_x\) containing \(0\). Define
\[
W=\{(\tau,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{X}:\tau\in I_x\}.
\]
The set \(W\) records which elapsed-time/state pairs are supported. It need not equal \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{X}\): a state can support only a finite interval of forward or backward evolution. For fixed elapsed time \(\tau\), the finite-time map has the typed domain
\[
\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)
=
\{x\in\mathcal{X}:(\tau,x)\in W\}.
\]


Under local existence and uniqueness, the maximal solutions define a single-valued map
\[
\Phi:W\rightarrow\mathcal{X},
\qquad
(\tau,x)\mapsto\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x).
\]
This local evolution family satisfies
\[
\phi_0(x)=x
\]
and, whenever the terms are defined,
\[
\phi_{\tau+s}(x)=\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(x)\bigr).
\]
More explicitly, if \(s\in I_x\) and \(\tau\in I_{\phi_s(x)}\), then \(s+\tau\in I_x\) and evolving first for \(s\) and then for \(\tau\) agrees with evolving for the combined elapsed time \(s+\tau\). These algebraic properties follow from autonomy and uniqueness. They do not by themselves assert joint continuity or differentiability in \((\tau,x)\).
When \(f\) is locally Lipschitz, it is continuous, so each individual curve \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) is \(C^1\) in elapsed time and satisfies
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)
=
f\bigl(\phi_\tau(x)\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}
=
f(x).
\]
This is differentiability along one trajectory in \(\tau\); it is not yet a claim of differentiability with respect to the initial state \(x\).



If \(f\in C^1(\mathcal{X},\mathbb{R}^n)\), Teschl’s smooth-dependence result gives that \(W\) is open and the joint map
\[
\Phi:W\rightarrow\mathcal{X},
\qquad
(\tau,x)\mapsto\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x),
\]
is \(C^1\) jointly in elapsed time and initial state. Under the adopted LDG convention, this jointly \(C^1\) map, together with the identity and composition laws above, is the local flow generated by \(f\). More generally, \(f\in C^k\) with \(k\geq1\) gives a joint \(C^k\) local-flow map (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2).












Symbol
Role




\(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\)
Open Euclidean state-space domain.


\(x\in\mathcal{X}\)
One admissible state value.


\(x(t)\)
State value along one trajectory at clock time \(t\).


\(t_0\)
Reference clock time for the IVP.


\(x_0\)
Initial state satisfying \(x(t_0)=x_0\).


\(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\)
Autonomous vector field.


\(\dot{x}(t)\)
Instantaneous derivative of the trajectory.


\(I_{t_0,x_0}\)
Maximal clock-time interval for the solution through \((t_0,x_0)\).


\(\tau=t-t_0\)
Elapsed time relative to the reference time.


\(I_x\)
Maximal elapsed-time interval for the solution through \(x\) at \(\tau=0\).


\(W\)
Supported elapsed-time/state pairs \((\tau,x)\).


\(\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)\)
States \(x\) for which \((\tau,x)\in W\).


\(\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x)\)
Single-valued local finite-time evolution; jointly \(C^1\) when \(f\in C^1\).



Clock time \(t\) locates a state on a particular trajectory. Elapsed time \(\tau\) indexes how far the autonomous rule advances an initial state. Autonomy is what permits the same one-parameter notation \(\phi_\tau\) to be used independently of the numerical value of \(t_0\).





The formula \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) alone does not settle whether solutions exist, are unique, or persist globally. For the open Euclidean domain above, the following sufficient conditions form a useful ladder.








Assumption on \(f\)
Consequence used here
What is not obtained automatically




\(f\) is an arbitrary map
The expression assigns a candidate instantaneous vector to each state.
Even local existence is not guaranteed.


\(f\) is continuous
For every \((t_0,x_0)\), at least one local solution exists by the autonomous form of Peano’s theorem. Because \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) is then continuous along a solution, each classical solution is \(C^1\) (Teschl 2012, sec. 2.7).
The solution need not be unique.


\(f\) is locally Lipschitz
Local Lipschitz continuity implies continuity. Picard–Lindelöf therefore gives local existence and uniqueness, and the compatible local pieces assemble into a unique maximal solution. The maximal solutions define single-valued local finite-time evolution with identity and composition where defined (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 2.6).
Global existence and joint differentiability with respect to the initial state are not implied.


\(f\in C^k(\mathcal{X},\mathbb{R}^n)\), \(k\geq1\)
The unique solution curves are \(C^{k+1}\) in time. The supported set \(W\) is open, and the joint local-flow map \(\Phi:W\to\mathcal{X}\) is \(C^k\) in \((\tau,x)\) (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 6.2).
Even smoothness does not prevent finite-time blow-up or exit from a proper open domain.



Here locally Lipschitz means that every \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) has a neighborhood \(U\subseteq\mathcal{X}\) and a finite constant \(L_U\) such that
\[
\|f(y)-f(z)\|\leq L_U\|y-z\|
\qquad
\text{for all }y,z\in U.
\]
This ladder gives sufficient, not logically necessary, conditions. Some continuous non-Lipschitz fields still have unique solutions, and some less regular settings admit other existence or uniqueness theorems. The scoped conclusion is only that continuity and local Lipschitz continuity cleanly separate basic existence from basic uniqueness.



Existence asks:

Is there at least one differentiable curve through \((t_0,x_0)\) satisfying the equation?

Uniqueness asks:

If two such curves pass through the same initial state at the same reference time, must they coincide on their common domain?

A theorem can answer the first question without answering the second. This distinction matters for flow notation: \(\phi_\tau(x_0)\) is a single state only when the evolution from \(x_0\) is single-valued under the active assumptions or an additional selection rule has been declared.



Now assume \(f\) is continuous and \(x:I\to\mathcal{X}\) is a classical solution of the IVP. Then \(f\circ x\) is continuous, so \(\dot{x}=f\circ x\) is continuous and \(x\in C^1(I,\mathcal{X})\). The fundamental theorem of calculus therefore gives
\[
x(t)-x_0
=
\int_{t_0}^{t}\dot{x}(s)\,ds
=
\int_{t_0}^{t}f\bigl(x(s)\bigr)\,ds.
\]
Hence every solution satisfies
\[
x(t)=x_0+\int_{t_0}^{t}f\bigl(x(s)\bigr)\,ds.
\]
Conversely, let \(f\) be continuous and let a continuous curve \(x:I\to\mathcal{X}\) satisfy this integral equation for every \(t\in I\). Then \(s\mapsto f(x(s))\) is continuous. The integral on the right is therefore \(C^1\), so \(x\) is \(C^1\) and differentiation gives \(\dot{x}(t)=f(x(t))\); setting \(t=t_0\) gives \(x(t_0)=x_0\). Thus the differential and integral formulations are equivalent in this continuous-\(f\) classical-solution setting. Picard iteration uses the integral equation as a fixed-point problem under the stronger local Lipschitz hypothesis (Teschl 2012, sec. 2.2).



Assume local existence and uniqueness. For an initial state \(x_0\), let \(x(\cdot;t_0,x_0)\) denote its maximal solution. Autonomy permits the finite-time map
\[
\phi_\tau(x_0)
=
x(t_0+\tau;t_0,x_0),
\]
whenever \(t_0+\tau\) lies in the maximal interval. The result does not depend on the numerical choice of \(t_0\): shifting clock time shifts an autonomous solution without changing the elapsed-time evolution rule.
For one fixed \(x_0\),
\[
t\mapsto x(t)=\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)
\]
is one trajectory. By contrast, the flow varies both elapsed time and initial state:
\[
(\tau,x_0)\mapsto\phi_\tau(x_0).
\]
The identity relation follows because no elapsed time has passed. The composition relation follows from autonomy and uniqueness: as functions of a new elapsed-time variable, both continuations start at the intermediate state \(\phi_s(x)\) and solve the same IVP, so they agree wherever both are defined. No differentiability with respect to \(x_0\) is required for these identities.



For locally Lipschitz \(f\), the individual curve \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) is \(C^1\) and its instantaneous generator is
\[
f(x)
=
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}.
\]
This derivative is only with respect to elapsed time. If \(f\in C^1\), the stronger conclusion is that \(\Phi(\tau,x)\) is jointly \(C^1\) in both \(\tau\) and \(x\). Conversely, a jointly differentiable local flow satisfying identity and composition generates an autonomous vector field through the derivative-at-zero relation, and its flow curves satisfy the corresponding ODE (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2, problem 6.5). Thus instantaneous and finite-time descriptions are linked without conflating time differentiability of one trajectory with differentiable dependence on initial state.




The central logical chain is:

Choose the admissible states. Declare an open domain \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
Assign instantaneous change. Specify \(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\).
Constrain a curve. Require a differentiable \(x:I\to\mathcal{X}\) to satisfy \(\dot{x}(t)=f(x(t))\).
Anchor the curve. Add \(x(t_0)=x_0\) to form an IVP.
Invoke the relevant regularity result. Continuity supplies at least one local solution; local Lipschitz continuity supplies local uniqueness as well.
Continue as far as possible. Because local existence and uniqueness both hold at the locally Lipschitz rung, compatible local pieces combine into one unique maximal solution on \(I_{t_0,x_0}\).
Re-index by elapsed time. Set \(\tau=t-t_0\) and define \(\phi_\tau(x_0)=x(t_0+\tau;t_0,x_0)\) where supported.
Use uniqueness to compose. Evolving from \(x\) for \(s\) reaches \(\phi_s(x)\). Starting there and evolving for \(\tau\) solves the same IVP as evolving from \(x\) for \(s+\tau\), so
\[
\phi_{\tau+s}(x)=\phi_\tau(\phi_s(x)).
\]
Differentiate at zero elapsed time. Since locally Lipschitz \(f\) is continuous, each solution curve is \(C^1\) in \(\tau\), and its local slope recovers the instantaneous rule:
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}=f(x).
\]
This is a derivative along the elapsed-time coordinate. Joint \(C^1\) dependence on \((\tau,x)\) is asserted only at the stronger \(f\in C^1\) rung.

No step in this chain turns local existence into global existence. For example, the smooth field \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) has the solution
\[
x(t)=\frac{x_0}{1-x_0(t-t_0)}
\]
for \(x_0>0\). Its maximal interval is
\[
(-\infty,t_0+1/x_0),
\]
because the solution diverges as \(t\uparrow t_0+1/x_0\). Smoothness gives local uniqueness and a smooth local flow, not a global flow on \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\) (Teschl 2012, secs. 1.3, 6.2).



At each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), the vector \(f(x)\) is a local arrow with units of state per unit time. A compatible trajectory is tangent to the arrow at every state it visits:
\[
\text{trajectory tangent at }x(t)
=
\dot{x}(t)
=
f(x(t)).
\]
The flow asks a different question. Rather than showing only the arrow at one point, \(\phi_\tau\) transports every supported initial point through a finite elapsed time \(\tau\). Fixing the point gives one trajectory; fixing the elapsed time gives one state-to-state map.
This picture is intuition, not evidence that measured data possess a vector field or flow. Arrows fitted to samples and curves displayed in a projection inherit the assumptions of the state definition, sampling process, and fitted model.



Consider the scalar IVP
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=a x,
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0,
\]
where \(a\in\mathbb{R}\) is fixed.


Multiply the state by the integrating factor \(e^{-a(t-t_0)}\). By the product rule,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dt}\left(e^{-a(t-t_0)}x(t)\right)
&=
-a e^{-a(t-t_0)}x(t)
+e^{-a(t-t_0)}\dot{x}(t)\\
&=
e^{-a(t-t_0)}\bigl(\dot{x}(t)-a x(t)\bigr)\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(e^{-a(t-t_0)}x(t)\) is constant in \(t\). Evaluating that constant at \(t=t_0\) gives
\[
e^{-a(t_0-t_0)}x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
Hence
\[
x(t)=x_0e^{a(t-t_0)}.
\]
This derivation also covers \(x_0=0\) without dividing by the state.



Differentiate the proposed solution:
\[
\dot{x}(t)
=
a x_0e^{a(t-t_0)}
=
a x(t).
\]
At the reference time,
\[
x(t_0)=x_0e^0=x_0.
\]
It therefore satisfies both the ODE and the initial condition.




State space: \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}\).
State value: \(x(t)\in\mathbb{R}\).
Vector field: \(f(x)=ax\).
Initial state: \(x_0\) at reference time \(t_0\).
Trajectory: \(t\mapsto x_0e^{a(t-t_0)}\) for the chosen \(x_0\).
Elapsed-time flow:
\[
\phi_\tau(x)=xe^{a\tau}.
\]

The field is globally Lipschitz because
\[
|f(x)-f(y)|=|a|\,|x-y|.
\]
The solution is finite for every real \(t\), so this example has a global flow.



Identity:
\[
\phi_0(x)=xe^{a\cdot0}=x.
\]
Composition:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(x)\bigr)
&=\phi_\tau(xe^{as})\\
&=(xe^{as})e^{a\tau}\\
&=xe^{a(\tau+s)}\\
&=\phi_{\tau+s}(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Generator:
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}
=
\left.a xe^{a\tau}\right|_{\tau=0}
=
ax
=
f(x).
\]
The example makes the three levels explicit: \(f(x)=ax\) gives instantaneous change, \(\phi_\tau(x)=xe^{a\tau}\) gives finite-time evolution across initial states, and choosing one \(x_0\) yields one trajectory.



For a bounded two-dimensional example, let the state be
\[
z(t)=
\begin{pmatrix}
x(t)\\
y(t)
\end{pmatrix}
\in\mathbb{R}^2
\]
and fix parameters \(a,\omega\in\mathbb{R}\). Consider the autonomous IVP
\[
\dot z=Az,
\qquad
A=
\begin{pmatrix}
a & -\omega\\
\omega & a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
z(t_0)=z_0.
\]
Define the planar rotation matrix
\[
R(\theta)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & \cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
With elapsed time \(\tau=t-t_0\), propose
\[
z(t_0+\tau)
=
e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z_0.
\]
When \(\omega\neq0\), the rotation changes the angular position while the factor \(e^{a\tau}\) changes the radius: \(a<0\) gives inward spirals, \(a=0\) gives constant-radius rotation, and \(a>0\) gives outward spirals. These descriptions concern this declared system only; they do not infer spiral dynamics from a plotted trajectory.


At zero elapsed time, \(e^{a\cdot0}=1\) and \(R(0)=I\), so
\[
z(t_0)=e^0R(0)z_0=z_0.
\]
Let
\[
J=
\begin{pmatrix}
0 & -1\\
1 & 0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A=aI+\omega J.
\]
Direct differentiation of the sine and cosine entries gives
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau}R(\omega\tau)
=
\omega J R(\omega\tau).
\]
Because \(d\tau/dt=1\), the product rule yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot z(t_0+\tau)
&=
e^{a\tau}
\left[aI+\omega J\right]
R(\omega\tau)z_0\\
&=
A\left[e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z_0\right]\\
&=Az(t_0+\tau).
\end{aligned}
\]
The proposed curve therefore satisfies both the ODE and the initial condition.




State space: \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^2\).
State value: \(z(t)=(x(t),y(t))^T\in\mathbb{R}^2\).
Vector field: \(f(z)=Az\).
Initial condition: \(z(t_0)=z_0\).
Trajectory: \(t\mapsto e^{a(t-t_0)}R(\omega(t-t_0))z_0\) for the chosen \(z_0\).
Elapsed-time flow:
\[
\phi_\tau(z)=e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z.
\]




The identity law follows immediately:
\[
\phi_0(z)=e^0R(0)z=z.
\]
Using \(e^{a\tau}e^{as}=e^{a(\tau+s)}\) and the planar rotation law \(R(\alpha)R(\beta)=R(\alpha+\beta)\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(z)\bigr)
&=
e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)
e^{as}R(\omega s)z\\
&=
e^{a(\tau+s)}R\bigl(\omega(\tau+s)\bigr)z\\
&=
\phi_{\tau+s}(z).
\end{aligned}
\]
The field is globally Lipschitz on \(\mathbb{R}^2\) because, for the Euclidean norm and its induced matrix norm,
\[
\|f(z)-f(w)\|
=
\|A(z-w)\|
\leq
\|A\|\,\|z-w\|.
\]
The explicit formula is finite for every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^2\) and every finite \(\tau\in\mathbb{R}\). Hence the supported domain is
\[
W=\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^2,
\]
so this system has a global two-sided flow. Each \(\phi_\tau\) is a globally defined bijection with inverse \(\phi_{-\tau}\). Outward growth when \(a>0\) is unbounded as \(\tau\to\infty\), but it does not cause finite-time blow-up.




Now consider
\[
\dot{x}=\sqrt{|x|},
\qquad
x(0)=0,
\qquad
\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}.
\]
The vector field \(f(x)=\sqrt{|x|}\) is continuous, so Peano’s theorem guarantees at least one local solution through \((0,0)\). It is not locally Lipschitz at \(0\), because for \(x\neq0\),
\[
\frac{|f(x)-f(0)|}{|x-0|}
=
\frac{\sqrt{|x|}}{|x|}
=
\frac{1}{\sqrt{|x|}},
\]
which is unbounded as \(x\to0\).
One solution is
\[
x(t)=0.
\]
For every waiting time \(c\geq0\), another solution is
\[
x_c(t)=
\begin{cases}
0, & t\leq c,\\
\dfrac{(t-c)^2}{4}, & t\geq c.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(t<c\), both \(\dot{x}_c(t)\) and \(\sqrt{|x_c(t)|}\) are zero. For \(t>c\),
\[
\dot{x}_c(t)=\frac{t-c}{2}
=
\sqrt{\frac{(t-c)^2}{4}}
=
\sqrt{|x_c(t)|}.
\]
At \(t=c\), the left and right derivatives are both zero, so \(x_c\) is differentiable there. Since \(c\geq0\), every such curve also satisfies \(x_c(0)=0\). The same IVP therefore has infinitely many solutions. This is the standard nonuniqueness mechanism illustrated by Teschl’s square-root example (Teschl 2012, sec. 1.3).
The lesson is precise: continuity supports existence here, but the failed local Lipschitz condition removes the basic uniqueness guarantee. Consequently, the ODE and initial state alone do not determine a unique value \(\phi_\tau(0)\) after positive elapsed time and therefore do not induce one uniquely determined single-valued flow.





Treating the equation as a curve rather than a constraint. The expression \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) specifies which differentiable curves qualify as solutions; it is not itself one trajectory.
Equating existence with uniqueness. A continuous field can admit solutions without selecting exactly one solution from an initial state.
Equating local with global. Local Lipschitz continuity gives local existence and uniqueness and hence a unique maximal continuation, not an all-time solution.
Ignoring the declared domain. A solution must remain in \(\mathcal{X}\). Reaching its boundary can end the maximal solution even when the coordinate values stay bounded.
Using \(t\) and \(\tau\) interchangeably. Clock time labels a trajectory relative to \(t_0\); elapsed time indexes autonomous evolution maps.
Calling one trajectory a flow. One fixed \(x_0\) gives one trajectory. A flow organizes evolution across multiple initial states and must satisfy identity and composition where defined.
Assuming every vector field has a global flow. Even a smooth vector field can have finite-time blow-up.
Inferring a field from a display. A plotted curve or fitted arrow field is not by itself evidence for a unique autonomous mechanism.

This formalism also does not imply that:

every observed time series is a dynamical-system trajectory;
every time-varying latent representation admits a valid autonomous vector field;
one observed trajectory uniquely determines a vector field, either away from or along incompletely sampled states;
multiple similar trajectories prove one shared flow;
predictive success establishes mechanistic correctness;
an inferred latent state is the uniquely true physical state;
all systems are autonomous or continuous-time;
all scientifically relevant state spaces are Euclidean; or
all vector fields generate global flows.




Given a declared \(f\), \(x_0\), and \(t_0\), a numerical ODE solver approximates one solution trajectory over a requested time interval. Step size, error control, stiffness, domain boundaries, and finite-time divergence affect whether the computation is reliable. Numerical output does not replace the analytical questions addressed here: whether a solution exists, whether it is unique, and whether the requested interval lies inside its maximal domain.
The flow viewpoint corresponds computationally to solving the same ODE for many initial states and elapsed times. A finite grid of simulations samples a proposed flow; it is not the complete map \(\Phi:W\to\mathcal{X}\). Likewise, estimating \(f\) from data is a separate Method problem involving sampling, observation, noise, identifiability, and baselines. It is not part of this mathematical definition.



This object formalizes, rather than replaces, the six Cycle 1 Concepts:



Concept
Formal role in the autonomous IVP




State
\(x(t)\) is the state value carried at clock time \(t\).


State Space
\(x(t)\in\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).


Initial Condition
\(x(t_0)=x_0\) anchors the evolution at a reference time.


Vector Field
\(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) assigns instantaneous change.


Trajectory
\(t\mapsto x(t)\) is one solution selected by an initial condition when uniqueness holds.


Flow
\((\tau,x_0)\mapsto\phi_\tau(x_0)\) organizes finite-time evolution across supported initial states.



For LDG, the main methodological boundary is that mathematical coherence inside a declared ODE model is not empirical evidence that measured neural, behavioral, or latent variables obey that model. A later toy model may use this object to specify known ground truth. Real-data claims would additionally require a justified state description, observation model, estimation procedure, simpler baselines, and tests that distinguish an autonomous shared rule from inputs, nonstationarity, omitted state, and measurement artifacts.




Existence, uniqueness, smoothness, integral form, and continuation of IVP solutions: (Teschl 2012, ch. 2).
Scalar autonomous examples demonstrating global evolution, finite-time blow-up, and nonuniqueness: (Teschl 2012, sec. 1.3).
Maximal integral curves, the supported domain \(W\), local-flow composition, and the infinitesimal generator: (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2).





Uses the six stable Cycle 1 Concepts as canonical prerequisites.
States the autonomous Euclidean IVP with well-typed domains and codomains.
Separates continuity, local Lipschitz continuity, and stronger smoothness.
Distinguishes existence from uniqueness and local from maximal and global solutions.
Defines the supported local-flow domain and states identity and composition only where defined.
Relates the differentiable local flow to its vector field through the derivative at zero.
Includes and verifies the complete \(\dot{x}=ax\) trajectory and flow derivation.
Includes an analytically checked two-dimensional rotation–dilation trajectory and global flow.
Includes a checked nonuniqueness example and a bounded finite-time blow-up boundary.
States empirical and modeling non-implications without entering excluded downstream topics.
Completed one internal mathematical consistency / Red-Team pass.
Applied the bounded corrections from the independent L2 mathematical review.
Independent focused re-review confirmed the revised statements; the owner approved L2 / stable promotion on 2026-08-18.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
The six Cycle 1 Concepts distinguish a state, its state space, a trajectory, an initial condition, a vector field, and a flow. This Math Object connects those roles in one reusable continuous-time formulation:
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=f(x),
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
The differential equation is not merely a compact description of a plotted curve. It is a constraint on an unknown differentiable state trajectory. Existence, uniqueness, continuation, and finite-time flow statements require separate hypotheses. Making those hypotheses explicit is necessary before later LDG work can use an autonomous ODE as a generative model or recovery target.
The scope is deliberately narrow: \(\mathcal{X}\) is an open subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), time is continuous, and the rule is deterministic and autonomous. Discrete-time, stochastic, input-driven, explicitly time-dependent, and non-Euclidean systems are outside this object.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
State: the state value carried by the model at a time.
State Space: the admissible values of that state.
Trajectory: one time-parameterized evolution.
Initial Condition: the assignment \(x(t_0)=x_0\).
Vector Field: the instantaneous state-change rule.
Flow: finite-time evolution across supported initial states.

Assumed background: elementary sets, functions, Euclidean vectors, single-variable differentiation and integration, the chain rule, and composition of functions.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
Let
\[
\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n
\]
be open, and let
\[
f:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The equation
\[
\dot{x}=f(x)
\]
is a first-order autonomous ordinary differential equation. It is first-order because the highest derivative is \(\dot{x}\), and autonomous because the right-hand side depends on the current state \(x\) but not explicitly on clock time \(t\).
A solution on an interval \(I\subseteq\mathbb{R}\) is a differentiable curve
\[
x:I\rightarrow\mathcal{X}
\]
such that, for every \(t\in I\),
\[
\dot{x}(t)=f\bigl(x(t)\bigr).
\]
Thus \(x(t)\) is a state value in \(\mathcal{X}\), while both \(\dot{x}(t)\) and \(f(x(t))\) are vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). The equation requires the trajectory to be tangent to the vector assigned by \(f\) at every visited state.



For a reference time \(t_0\) and initial state \(x_0\in\mathcal{X}\), the initial-value problem (IVP) is
\[
\dot{x}=f(x),
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
A solution of the IVP must satisfy both the differential equation and the initial condition. The rule \(f\) describes possible instantaneous evolution across its domain; the initial condition selects the solution or set of solutions that pass through \(x_0\) at \(t_0\).




A local solution is defined on an open interval \(I\) containing \(t_0\).
A solution is maximal if it cannot be extended to a strictly larger interval while remaining a solution in \(\mathcal{X}\). If the IVP admits a unique local solution—that is, local solutions exist and any two compatible local solutions agree on their common domain—those local pieces assemble into one unique maximal solution on an open maximal interval
\[
I_{t_0,x_0}=(T_-(t_0,x_0),T_+(t_0,x_0)).
\]
A global solution in this object’s all-time setting is defined for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), so its maximal interval is \(\mathbb{R}\).

Local existence and uniqueness do not imply global existence. Under the same local solvability assumptions, if a maximal solution has a finite forward endpoint \(T_+\), then as \(t\uparrow T_+\) it eventually leaves every compact subset of \(\mathcal{X}\). When \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^n\), this means \(\|x(t)\|\to\infty\). On a proper open domain, the trajectory can instead remain bounded while approaching the complement of \(\mathcal{X}\); it need not converge to one particular boundary point. The analogous statements hold at a finite backward endpoint. Teschl separates local solvability from maximal continuation and states this compact-set criterion explicitly (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 2.6).



It is useful to measure time from the initial condition. Write
\[
\tau=t-t_0
\]
for elapsed time. For each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), suppose a unique maximal solution through \(x\) at elapsed time \(0\) is defined on an interval \(I_x\) containing \(0\). Define
\[
W=\{(\tau,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{X}:\tau\in I_x\}.
\]
The set \(W\) records which elapsed-time/state pairs are supported. It need not equal \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{X}\): a state can support only a finite interval of forward or backward evolution. For fixed elapsed time \(\tau\), the finite-time map has the typed domain
\[
\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)
=
\{x\in\mathcal{X}:(\tau,x)\in W\}.
\]


Under local existence and uniqueness, the maximal solutions define a single-valued map
\[
\Phi:W\rightarrow\mathcal{X},
\qquad
(\tau,x)\mapsto\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x).
\]
This local evolution family satisfies
\[
\phi_0(x)=x
\]
and, whenever the terms are defined,
\[
\phi_{\tau+s}(x)=\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(x)\bigr).
\]
More explicitly, if \(s\in I_x\) and \(\tau\in I_{\phi_s(x)}\), then \(s+\tau\in I_x\) and evolving first for \(s\) and then for \(\tau\) agrees with evolving for the combined elapsed time \(s+\tau\). These algebraic properties follow from autonomy and uniqueness. They do not by themselves assert joint continuity or differentiability in \((\tau,x)\).
When \(f\) is locally Lipschitz, it is continuous, so each individual curve \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) is \(C^1\) in elapsed time and satisfies
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)
=
f\bigl(\phi_\tau(x)\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}
=
f(x).
\]
This is differentiability along one trajectory in \(\tau\); it is not yet a claim of differentiability with respect to the initial state \(x\).



If \(f\in C^1(\mathcal{X},\mathbb{R}^n)\), Teschl’s smooth-dependence result gives that \(W\) is open and the joint map
\[
\Phi:W\rightarrow\mathcal{X},
\qquad
(\tau,x)\mapsto\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x),
\]
is \(C^1\) jointly in elapsed time and initial state. Under the adopted LDG convention, this jointly \(C^1\) map, together with the identity and composition laws above, is the local flow generated by \(f\). More generally, \(f\in C^k\) with \(k\geq1\) gives a joint \(C^k\) local-flow map (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2).

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
Symbol
Role




\(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\)
Open Euclidean state-space domain.


\(x\in\mathcal{X}\)
One admissible state value.


\(x(t)\)
State value along one trajectory at clock time \(t\).


\(t_0\)
Reference clock time for the IVP.


\(x_0\)
Initial state satisfying \(x(t_0)=x_0\).


\(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\)
Autonomous vector field.


\(\dot{x}(t)\)
Instantaneous derivative of the trajectory.


\(I_{t_0,x_0}\)
Maximal clock-time interval for the solution through \((t_0,x_0)\).


\(\tau=t-t_0\)
Elapsed time relative to the reference time.


\(I_x\)
Maximal elapsed-time interval for the solution through \(x\) at \(\tau=0\).


\(W\)
Supported elapsed-time/state pairs \((\tau,x)\).


\(\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)\)
States \(x\) for which \((\tau,x)\in W\).


\(\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x)\)
Single-valued local finite-time evolution; jointly \(C^1\) when \(f\in C^1\).



Clock time \(t\) locates a state on a particular trajectory. Elapsed time \(\tau\) indexes how far the autonomous rule advances an initial state. Autonomy is what permits the same one-parameter notation \(\phi_\tau\) to be used independently of the numerical value of \(t_0\).

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
The formula \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) alone does not settle whether solutions exist, are unique, or persist globally. For the open Euclidean domain above, the following sufficient conditions form a useful ladder.








Assumption on \(f\)
Consequence used here
What is not obtained automatically




\(f\) is an arbitrary map
The expression assigns a candidate instantaneous vector to each state.
Even local existence is not guaranteed.


\(f\) is continuous
For every \((t_0,x_0)\), at least one local solution exists by the autonomous form of Peano’s theorem. Because \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) is then continuous along a solution, each classical solution is \(C^1\) (Teschl 2012, sec. 2.7).
The solution need not be unique.


\(f\) is locally Lipschitz
Local Lipschitz continuity implies continuity. Picard–Lindelöf therefore gives local existence and uniqueness, and the compatible local pieces assemble into a unique maximal solution. The maximal solutions define single-valued local finite-time evolution with identity and composition where defined (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 2.6).
Global existence and joint differentiability with respect to the initial state are not implied.


\(f\in C^k(\mathcal{X},\mathbb{R}^n)\), \(k\geq1\)
The unique solution curves are \(C^{k+1}\) in time. The supported set \(W\) is open, and the joint local-flow map \(\Phi:W\to\mathcal{X}\) is \(C^k\) in \((\tau,x)\) (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 6.2).
Even smoothness does not prevent finite-time blow-up or exit from a proper open domain.



Here locally Lipschitz means that every \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) has a neighborhood \(U\subseteq\mathcal{X}\) and a finite constant \(L_U\) such that
\[
\|f(y)-f(z)\|\leq L_U\|y-z\|
\qquad
\text{for all }y,z\in U.
\]
This ladder gives sufficient, not logically necessary, conditions. Some continuous non-Lipschitz fields still have unique solutions, and some less regular settings admit other existence or uniqueness theorems. The scoped conclusion is only that continuity and local Lipschitz continuity cleanly separate basic existence from basic uniqueness.



Existence asks:

Is there at least one differentiable curve through \((t_0,x_0)\) satisfying the equation?

Uniqueness asks:

If two such curves pass through the same initial state at the same reference time, must they coincide on their common domain?

A theorem can answer the first question without answering the second. This distinction matters for flow notation: \(\phi_\tau(x_0)\) is a single state only when the evolution from \(x_0\) is single-valued under the active assumptions or an additional selection rule has been declared.



Now assume \(f\) is continuous and \(x:I\to\mathcal{X}\) is a classical solution of the IVP. Then \(f\circ x\) is continuous, so \(\dot{x}=f\circ x\) is continuous and \(x\in C^1(I,\mathcal{X})\). The fundamental theorem of calculus therefore gives
\[
x(t)-x_0
=
\int_{t_0}^{t}\dot{x}(s)\,ds
=
\int_{t_0}^{t}f\bigl(x(s)\bigr)\,ds.
\]
Hence every solution satisfies
\[
x(t)=x_0+\int_{t_0}^{t}f\bigl(x(s)\bigr)\,ds.
\]
Conversely, let \(f\) be continuous and let a continuous curve \(x:I\to\mathcal{X}\) satisfy this integral equation for every \(t\in I\). Then \(s\mapsto f(x(s))\) is continuous. The integral on the right is therefore \(C^1\), so \(x\) is \(C^1\) and differentiation gives \(\dot{x}(t)=f(x(t))\); setting \(t=t_0\) gives \(x(t_0)=x_0\). Thus the differential and integral formulations are equivalent in this continuous-\(f\) classical-solution setting. Picard iteration uses the integral equation as a fixed-point problem under the stronger local Lipschitz hypothesis (Teschl 2012, sec. 2.2).



Assume local existence and uniqueness. For an initial state \(x_0\), let \(x(\cdot;t_0,x_0)\) denote its maximal solution. Autonomy permits the finite-time map
\[
\phi_\tau(x_0)
=
x(t_0+\tau;t_0,x_0),
\]
whenever \(t_0+\tau\) lies in the maximal interval. The result does not depend on the numerical choice of \(t_0\): shifting clock time shifts an autonomous solution without changing the elapsed-time evolution rule.
For one fixed \(x_0\),
\[
t\mapsto x(t)=\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)
\]
is one trajectory. By contrast, the flow varies both elapsed time and initial state:
\[
(\tau,x_0)\mapsto\phi_\tau(x_0).
\]
The identity relation follows because no elapsed time has passed. The composition relation follows from autonomy and uniqueness: as functions of a new elapsed-time variable, both continuations start at the intermediate state \(\phi_s(x)\) and solve the same IVP, so they agree wherever both are defined. No differentiability with respect to \(x_0\) is required for these identities.



For locally Lipschitz \(f\), the individual curve \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) is \(C^1\) and its instantaneous generator is
\[
f(x)
=
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}.
\]
This derivative is only with respect to elapsed time. If \(f\in C^1\), the stronger conclusion is that \(\Phi(\tau,x)\) is jointly \(C^1\) in both \(\tau\) and \(x\). Conversely, a jointly differentiable local flow satisfying identity and composition generates an autonomous vector field through the derivative-at-zero relation, and its flow curves satisfy the corresponding ODE (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2, problem 6.5). Thus instantaneous and finite-time descriptions are linked without conflating time differentiability of one trajectory with differentiable dependence on initial state.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
The central logical chain is:

Choose the admissible states. Declare an open domain \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
Assign instantaneous change. Specify \(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\).
Constrain a curve. Require a differentiable \(x:I\to\mathcal{X}\) to satisfy \(\dot{x}(t)=f(x(t))\).
Anchor the curve. Add \(x(t_0)=x_0\) to form an IVP.
Invoke the relevant regularity result. Continuity supplies at least one local solution; local Lipschitz continuity supplies local uniqueness as well.
Continue as far as possible. Because local existence and uniqueness both hold at the locally Lipschitz rung, compatible local pieces combine into one unique maximal solution on \(I_{t_0,x_0}\).
Re-index by elapsed time. Set \(\tau=t-t_0\) and define \(\phi_\tau(x_0)=x(t_0+\tau;t_0,x_0)\) where supported.
Use uniqueness to compose. Evolving from \(x\) for \(s\) reaches \(\phi_s(x)\). Starting there and evolving for \(\tau\) solves the same IVP as evolving from \(x\) for \(s+\tau\), so
\[
\phi_{\tau+s}(x)=\phi_\tau(\phi_s(x)).
\]
Differentiate at zero elapsed time. Since locally Lipschitz \(f\) is continuous, each solution curve is \(C^1\) in \(\tau\), and its local slope recovers the instantaneous rule:
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}=f(x).
\]
This is a derivative along the elapsed-time coordinate. Joint \(C^1\) dependence on \((\tau,x)\) is asserted only at the stronger \(f\in C^1\) rung.

No step in this chain turns local existence into global existence. For example, the smooth field \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) has the solution
\[
x(t)=\frac{x_0}{1-x_0(t-t_0)}
\]
for \(x_0>0\). Its maximal interval is
\[
(-\infty,t_0+1/x_0),
\]
because the solution diverges as \(t\uparrow t_0+1/x_0\). Smoothness gives local uniqueness and a smooth local flow, not a global flow on \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\) (Teschl 2012, secs. 1.3, 6.2).

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
At each \(x\in\mathcal{X}\), the vector \(f(x)\) is a local arrow with units of state per unit time. A compatible trajectory is tangent to the arrow at every state it visits:
\[
\text{trajectory tangent at }x(t)
=
\dot{x}(t)
=
f(x(t)).
\]
The flow asks a different question. Rather than showing only the arrow at one point, \(\phi_\tau\) transports every supported initial point through a finite elapsed time \(\tau\). Fixing the point gives one trajectory; fixing the elapsed time gives one state-to-state map.
This picture is intuition, not evidence that measured data possess a vector field or flow. Arrows fitted to samples and curves displayed in a projection inherit the assumptions of the state definition, sampling process, and fitted model.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
Consider the scalar IVP
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=a x,
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0,
\]
where \(a\in\mathbb{R}\) is fixed.


Multiply the state by the integrating factor \(e^{-a(t-t_0)}\). By the product rule,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d}{dt}\left(e^{-a(t-t_0)}x(t)\right)
&=
-a e^{-a(t-t_0)}x(t)
+e^{-a(t-t_0)}\dot{x}(t)\\
&=
e^{-a(t-t_0)}\bigl(\dot{x}(t)-a x(t)\bigr)\\
&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(e^{-a(t-t_0)}x(t)\) is constant in \(t\). Evaluating that constant at \(t=t_0\) gives
\[
e^{-a(t_0-t_0)}x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
Hence
\[
x(t)=x_0e^{a(t-t_0)}.
\]
This derivation also covers \(x_0=0\) without dividing by the state.



Differentiate the proposed solution:
\[
\dot{x}(t)
=
a x_0e^{a(t-t_0)}
=
a x(t).
\]
At the reference time,
\[
x(t_0)=x_0e^0=x_0.
\]
It therefore satisfies both the ODE and the initial condition.




State space: \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}\).
State value: \(x(t)\in\mathbb{R}\).
Vector field: \(f(x)=ax\).
Initial state: \(x_0\) at reference time \(t_0\).
Trajectory: \(t\mapsto x_0e^{a(t-t_0)}\) for the chosen \(x_0\).
Elapsed-time flow:
\[
\phi_\tau(x)=xe^{a\tau}.
\]

The field is globally Lipschitz because
\[
|f(x)-f(y)|=|a|\,|x-y|.
\]
The solution is finite for every real \(t\), so this example has a global flow.



Identity:
\[
\phi_0(x)=xe^{a\cdot0}=x.
\]
Composition:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(x)\bigr)
&=\phi_\tau(xe^{as})\\
&=(xe^{as})e^{a\tau}\\
&=xe^{a(\tau+s)}\\
&=\phi_{\tau+s}(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Generator:
\[
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}
=
\left.a xe^{a\tau}\right|_{\tau=0}
=
ax
=
f(x).
\]
The example makes the three levels explicit: \(f(x)=ax\) gives instantaneous change, \(\phi_\tau(x)=xe^{a\tau}\) gives finite-time evolution across initial states, and choosing one \(x_0\) yields one trajectory.



For a bounded two-dimensional example, let the state be
\[
z(t)=
\begin{pmatrix}
x(t)\\
y(t)
\end{pmatrix}
\in\mathbb{R}^2
\]
and fix parameters \(a,\omega\in\mathbb{R}\). Consider the autonomous IVP
\[
\dot z=Az,
\qquad
A=
\begin{pmatrix}
a & -\omega\\
\omega & a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
z(t_0)=z_0.
\]
Define the planar rotation matrix
\[
R(\theta)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & -\sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & \cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
With elapsed time \(\tau=t-t_0\), propose
\[
z(t_0+\tau)
=
e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z_0.
\]
When \(\omega\neq0\), the rotation changes the angular position while the factor \(e^{a\tau}\) changes the radius: \(a<0\) gives inward spirals, \(a=0\) gives constant-radius rotation, and \(a>0\) gives outward spirals. These descriptions concern this declared system only; they do not infer spiral dynamics from a plotted trajectory.


At zero elapsed time, \(e^{a\cdot0}=1\) and \(R(0)=I\), so
\[
z(t_0)=e^0R(0)z_0=z_0.
\]
Let
\[
J=
\begin{pmatrix}
0 & -1\\
1 & 0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A=aI+\omega J.
\]
Direct differentiation of the sine and cosine entries gives
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau}R(\omega\tau)
=
\omega J R(\omega\tau).
\]
Because \(d\tau/dt=1\), the product rule yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot z(t_0+\tau)
&=
e^{a\tau}
\left[aI+\omega J\right]
R(\omega\tau)z_0\\
&=
A\left[e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z_0\right]\\
&=Az(t_0+\tau).
\end{aligned}
\]
The proposed curve therefore satisfies both the ODE and the initial condition.




State space: \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^2\).
State value: \(z(t)=(x(t),y(t))^T\in\mathbb{R}^2\).
Vector field: \(f(z)=Az\).
Initial condition: \(z(t_0)=z_0\).
Trajectory: \(t\mapsto e^{a(t-t_0)}R(\omega(t-t_0))z_0\) for the chosen \(z_0\).
Elapsed-time flow:
\[
\phi_\tau(z)=e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)z.
\]




The identity law follows immediately:
\[
\phi_0(z)=e^0R(0)z=z.
\]
Using \(e^{a\tau}e^{as}=e^{a(\tau+s)}\) and the planar rotation law \(R(\alpha)R(\beta)=R(\alpha+\beta)\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(z)\bigr)
&=
e^{a\tau}R(\omega\tau)
e^{as}R(\omega s)z\\
&=
e^{a(\tau+s)}R\bigl(\omega(\tau+s)\bigr)z\\
&=
\phi_{\tau+s}(z).
\end{aligned}
\]
The field is globally Lipschitz on \(\mathbb{R}^2\) because, for the Euclidean norm and its induced matrix norm,
\[
\|f(z)-f(w)\|
=
\|A(z-w)\|
\leq
\|A\|\,\|z-w\|.
\]
The explicit formula is finite for every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^2\) and every finite \(\tau\in\mathbb{R}\). Hence the supported domain is
\[
W=\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^2,
\]
so this system has a global two-sided flow. Each \(\phi_\tau\) is a globally defined bijection with inverse \(\phi_{-\tau}\). Outward growth when \(a>0\) is unbounded as \(\tau\to\infty\), but it does not cause finite-time blow-up.




Now consider
\[
\dot{x}=\sqrt{|x|},
\qquad
x(0)=0,
\qquad
\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}.
\]
The vector field \(f(x)=\sqrt{|x|}\) is continuous, so Peano’s theorem guarantees at least one local solution through \((0,0)\). It is not locally Lipschitz at \(0\), because for \(x\neq0\),
\[
\frac{|f(x)-f(0)|}{|x-0|}
=
\frac{\sqrt{|x|}}{|x|}
=
\frac{1}{\sqrt{|x|}},
\]
which is unbounded as \(x\to0\).
One solution is
\[
x(t)=0.
\]
For every waiting time \(c\geq0\), another solution is
\[
x_c(t)=
\begin{cases}
0, & t\leq c,\\
\dfrac{(t-c)^2}{4}, & t\geq c.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(t<c\), both \(\dot{x}_c(t)\) and \(\sqrt{|x_c(t)|}\) are zero. For \(t>c\),
\[
\dot{x}_c(t)=\frac{t-c}{2}
=
\sqrt{\frac{(t-c)^2}{4}}
=
\sqrt{|x_c(t)|}.
\]
At \(t=c\), the left and right derivatives are both zero, so \(x_c\) is differentiable there. Since \(c\geq0\), every such curve also satisfies \(x_c(0)=0\). The same IVP therefore has infinitely many solutions. This is the standard nonuniqueness mechanism illustrated by Teschl’s square-root example (Teschl 2012, sec. 1.3).
The lesson is precise: continuity supports existence here, but the failed local Lipschitz condition removes the basic uniqueness guarantee. Consequently, the ODE and initial state alone do not determine a unique value \(\phi_\tau(0)\) after positive elapsed time and therefore do not induce one uniquely determined single-valued flow.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
Given a declared \(f\), \(x_0\), and \(t_0\), a numerical ODE solver approximates one solution trajectory over a requested time interval. Step size, error control, stiffness, domain boundaries, and finite-time divergence affect whether the computation is reliable. Numerical output does not replace the analytical questions addressed here: whether a solution exists, whether it is unique, and whether the requested interval lies inside its maximal domain.
The flow viewpoint corresponds computationally to solving the same ODE for many initial states and elapsed times. A finite grid of simulations samples a proposed flow; it is not the complete map \(\Phi:W\to\mathcal{X}\). Likewise, estimating \(f\) from data is a separate Method problem involving sampling, observation, noise, identifiability, and baselines. It is not part of this mathematical definition.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
This object formalizes, rather than replaces, the six Cycle 1 Concepts:



Concept
Formal role in the autonomous IVP




State
\(x(t)\) is the state value carried at clock time \(t\).


State Space
\(x(t)\in\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).


Initial Condition
\(x(t_0)=x_0\) anchors the evolution at a reference time.


Vector Field
\(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) assigns instantaneous change.


Trajectory
\(t\mapsto x(t)\) is one solution selected by an initial condition when uniqueness holds.


Flow
\((\tau,x_0)\mapsto\phi_\tau(x_0)\) organizes finite-time evolution across supported initial states.



For LDG, the main methodological boundary is that mathematical coherence inside a declared ODE model is not empirical evidence that measured neural, behavioral, or latent variables obey that model. A later toy model may use this object to specify known ground truth. Real-data claims would additionally require a justified state description, observation model, estimation procedure, simpler baselines, and tests that distinguish an autonomous shared rule from inputs, nonstationarity, omitted state, and measurement artifacts.

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
Existence, uniqueness, smoothness, integral form, and continuation of IVP solutions: (Teschl 2012, ch. 2).
Scalar autonomous examples demonstrating global evolution, finite-time blow-up, and nonuniqueness: (Teschl 2012, sec. 1.3).
Maximal integral curves, the supported domain \(W\), local-flow composition, and the infinitesimal generator: (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2).

title: First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System
text:
Uses the six stable Cycle 1 Concepts as canonical prerequisites.
States the autonomous Euclidean IVP with well-typed domains and codomains.
Separates continuity, local Lipschitz continuity, and stronger smoothness.
Distinguishes existence from uniqueness and local from maximal and global solutions.
Defines the supported local-flow domain and states identity and composition only where defined.
Relates the differentiable local flow to its vector field through the derivative at zero.
Includes and verifies the complete \(\dot{x}=ax\) trajectory and flow derivation.
Includes an analytically checked two-dimensional rotation–dilation trajectory and global flow.
Includes a checked nonuniqueness example and a bounded finite-time blow-up boundary.
States empirical and modeling non-implications without entering excluded downstream topics.
Completed one internal mathematical consistency / Red-Team pass.
Applied the bounded corrections from the independent L2 mathematical review.
Independent focused re-review confirmed the revised statements; the owner approved L2 / stable promotion on 2026-08-18.

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型（LGSSM）通过未观测状态描述有序观测序列，该状态以高斯过程噪声线性演化，并以高斯观测噪声线性生成测量。它提供一个联合概率模型，其中预测、状态推断、序列似然与参数学习可以被定义而不被当作同一任务 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年; Särkkä 2013年)。
本对象规定有限维、时间不变、离散时间模型，具有固定或外部提供的开环已知输入路径。它不呈现卡尔曼滤波或固定区间平滑算法，那些是后续方法单元。时变、切换、非线性、非高斯、连续时间、未知输入、反馈策略与控制设计变体在有界核心之外。



对长度为 \(T\) 的单个序列，设

\(x_t\in\mathbb R^p\) 是观测向量；
\(u_t\in\mathbb R^r\) 是可选已知输入或回归量；以及
\(z_t\in\mathbb R^q\) 是潜状态。

可复现分析必须声明：

观测单元、序列边界、采样间隔、排序，以及矩阵是否被假设跨序列共同；
特征定义、单位、变换、排除与缺失数据策略；
哪些输入在拟合与预测时固定或外部提供，以及每个值何时可用；
潜维数 \(q\) 及其选择规程；
参数是从外部知识固定还是从训练序列学习；以及
精确目标：预测、滤波、平滑、边际似然、参数学习或模拟。

序列、受试者、会话或试次不是可互换重复。其依赖与参数共享必须被陈述。



模型规格是参数元组
\[
\theta=(m_1,P_1,A,B,C,D,Q,R),
\]
维数与状态、输入与观测空间一致。在 \(\theta\) 条件下，它定义：

联合高斯律 \(p_\theta(z_{1:T},x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})\)；
未来状态与观测的预测分布；
只以目标时间前可用观测为条件的滤波分布；
以完整声明观测区间为条件的平滑分布；
对 \(z_{1:T}\) 积分后的边际序列似然；以及
带不确定性的模型条件潜状态摘要。

实现还可以返回拟合参数、预测均值/协方差、滤波或平滑状态矩、创新与似然贡献。这些输出具有不同条件信息，必须相应标注。



状态携带下一步转移所需信息，而观测是状态的有噪线性视图。马尔可夫分解把一条高维轨迹分布转化为初始状态律、局部转移律与局部观测律。高斯封闭性使相关条件与边际分布为高斯，允许参数已知时精确有限时域推断 (Särkkä 2013年, chs. 4, 8)。
方法的价值不仅在于推断均值轨迹看起来光滑。它在于声明的随机时序模型产生可检验预测分布，并把转移处引入的不确定性与测量处引入的不确定性分开。



规范输入驱动模型是
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N(m_1,P_1),
\]
\[
z_{t+1}=Az_t+Bu_t+w_t,
\qquad
w_t\sim\mathcal N(0,Q),
\]
\[
x_t=Cz_t+Du_t+v_t,
\qquad
v_t\sim\mathcal N(0,R).
\]
无输入核心通过省略 \(u_t\)、\(B\) 与 \(D\) 恢复。除非显式泛化，模型假设：

\(P_1,Q\succeq0\) 且 \(R\succ0\)；
\(z_1\)、每个 \(w_t\) 与每个 \(v_s\) 相互独立；
过程与观测噪声跨时间独立；
\(A,B,C,D,Q,R\) 在序列上恒定；
潜转移是一阶马尔可夫；
观测在给定状态路径与输入时跨时间条件独立；以及
输入预先固定或外部提供，不依赖同期或未来观测，因此是有效条件变量而非未解释随机原因。

高斯性强于只指定均值与协方差。相关过程与观测噪声、有色噪声、异方差、时变矩阵或依赖历史的测量需要显式修改模型，而非对 \(Q\) 或 \(R\) 的非正式重新解读。



对固定开环输入路径，联合律分解为
\[
p_\theta(z_{1:T},x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})
=p_\theta(z_1)
\prod_{t=1}^{T-1}p_\theta(z_{t+1}\mid z_t,u_t)
\prod_{t=1}^{T}p_\theta(x_t\mid z_t,u_t),
\]
其中
\[
p_\theta(z_{t+1}\mid z_t,u_t)
=\mathcal N(Az_t+Bu_t,Q),
\]
\[
p_\theta(x_t\mid z_t,u_t)
=\mathcal N(Cz_t+Du_t,R).
\]
该分解定义若干不同条件目标。下方出现的未来输入值必须是已知场景值，而非编码未来观测的控制：
\[
\text{forecasting:}\quad
p(z_{t+h},x_{t+h}\mid x_{1:t},u_{1:t+h}),
\]
\[
\text{filtering:}\quad
p(z_t\mid x_{1:t},u_{1:t}),
\]
\[
\text{smoothing:}\quad
p(z_t\mid x_{1:T},u_{1:T}),\quad T>t,
\]
或完整路径后验 \(p(z_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T},u_{1:T})\)。Kalman 通过被估计状态时间是早于、等于还是晚于最终条件观测来显式区分平滑、滤波与预测 (Kalman 1960年)。精确递推被有意推迟到单独滤波与平滑方法对象。
边际似然是
\[
p_\theta(x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})
=\int p_\theta(z_{1:T},x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})\,dz_{1:T}.
\]
它可以分解为一步预测密度，
\[
p_\theta(x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})
=\prod_{t=1}^{T}
p_\theta(x_t\mid x_{1:t-1},u_{1:t}),
\]
这使序列评分与状态点估计分离 (Särkkä 2013年, sec. 12.1)。
反馈控制数据需要单独时间与策略模型。有效控制 \(u_t\) 必须可从其驱动转移之前可用的信息测量，且当 \(D\ne0\) 时在同期观测 \(x_t\) 之前可用；在 \(u_t\) 中使用 \(x_t\) 本身会制造代数环。如果未来控制依赖未来观测，以已实现 \(u_{1:T}\) 为条件会泄漏未来信息。策略感知似然与预测必须改为陈述非预期策略，并对尚不知道的控制积分或模拟。



取决于规程，参数学习可以估计 \(m_1,P_1,A,B,C,D,Q,R\) 的部分或全部并选择 \(q\)。给定拟合参数，状态推断确定潜状态上的条件分布；除非使用显式联合或在线学习规程，它不重新学习模型参数。
最大似然学习瞄准对潜状态积分后的可观测序列分布。EM 则在模型条件潜充分统计量的期望与在精确步骤下增加同一边际似然的参数更新之间交替 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年)。因此推断状态路径是中间不确定量，不是观测训练数据。



分析者固定状态维数或其选择搜索、序列边界、时间步、输入定义、矩阵结构与参数共享、高斯与独立假设、协方差约束、初始状态处理、缺失数据机制、学习准则、正则化或先验，以及评估目标。
当某些矩阵来自物理建模时，固定对估计的划分必须显式。如果 \(C\)、\(Q\)、\(R\)、状态坐标或输入是现象学学习的，把 \(A\) 称为「动力学」并不确立它是物理定律。



时间是离散且有序的。置换观测通常会改变似然。一阶马尔可夫假设陈述，在 \(z_t\) 与已知输入条件下，\(z_{t+1}\) 不依赖更早状态。它不蕴含观测序列是一阶马尔可夫的。
稳定性与平稳性不同。 对时间不变无输入均值动力学，\(\rho(A)<1\) 是通常的 Schur 稳定条件，在该条件下确定性扰动衰减。零均值、常值 \(Q\) 与合适有限协方差时，稳定 \(A\) 支持满足
\[
\Sigma=A\Sigma A^\top+Q.
\]
的平稳状态协方差 \(\Sigma\)。只有初始化与输入也与平稳律相容时，过程才平稳。从该律之外初始化的稳定模型具有瞬态；单位根或不稳定的有限时域模型仍可以定义有效分布而不平稳。时变输入可以使均值非平稳，即使 \(A\) 稳定。
不规则采样不能通过静默地把每个索引间隙当作相等来处理。它需要依赖间隙的转移、底层连续时间模型与离散化，或其他显式变体。



潜状态在有限维向量空间中表示。\(A\) 在所选状态坐标中线性，而 \(Q\) 与 \(R\) 定义依赖坐标的马氏不确定性。除非度量与坐标约定被论证，后验状态均值之间的欧氏距离没有不变科学意义。
模型不设定非线性流形或黎曼几何。低维线性潜状态是建模选择，不是本征维数或唯一状态空间的证明。



基于观测序列的似然拟合对外部标签无监督。固定开环输入条件化转移与观测律；其存在在预测标签意义上不自动是「监督」。用于设计状态、约束矩阵、选择超参数或给模型评分的标签、结果或干预会引入任务依赖，必须被声明。
与未建模扰动相关的观测输入不自动外生。包含 \(u_t\) 不辨识由 \(B\) 或 \(D\) 表示的因果效应。反馈依赖输入需要上述界定的策略感知扩展，而非此处使用的开环条件分解。



对已知参数，有限时域线性高斯预测、滤波与平滑是精确高斯条件化问题。它们只在目标与信息集上不同，但需要不同计算。滤波使用到当前时间为止的数据；固定区间平滑在声明区间内使用未来观测 (Särkkä 2013年, chs. 4, 8)。
参数学习是单独优化或贝叶斯推断问题。直接最大似然优化可以使用预测密度分解。在 EM 中，E 步需要当前参数下的平滑期望，如 \(\mathbb E[z_t]\)、\(\mathbb E[z_tz_t^\top]\) 与 \(\mathbb E[z_tz_{t-1}^\top]\)；M 步从这些期望更新模型参数 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年)。因此 EM 实现可以在内部调用滤波与平滑，但学习模型、滤波后验、平滑后验与优化器不是可互换对象。
似然在自由潜参数化中一般非凸。必须报告初始化、协方差约束、正则化、停止准则、多次启动与数值分解。递增的 EM 目标不证明全局最优性或科学有效性。




它定义有序潜与观测序列上的连贯联合分布。
过程与观测不确定性通过 \(Q\) 与 \(R\) 分别表示。
参数固定时精确高斯预测与状态后验可用。
边际似然支持序列级预测比较与参数学习。
可以在不放弃线性高斯易处理性的情况下纳入输入。
在非线性或非高斯潜模型之前，它是透明时序基线。





错误潜维数或结构： 省略模态留下时序残差结构；冗余模态制造弱辨识或未使用状态。
噪声权衡： 短、弱观测序列可能无法区分过程变异与观测变异，因此 \(Q\)、\(R\)、\(C\) 与状态路径可以相互补偿。
未建模依赖： 有色、相关、异方差或状态依赖噪声使白独立高斯假设失效。
非线性或制度变化： 单个全局 \(A\) 与 \(C\) 无法表示切换、饱和、弯曲观测映射或突然干预。
不稳定或近单位根： 预测可以发散或变得高度不确定，短记录中的参数估计可能敏感。
不可观测模态： 不影响可用观测的潜方向无法从这些观测恢复。
弱激励： 输入或过程噪声可能无法探索估计转移效应所需的方向。
缺失或删失： 把有信息缺失观测当作可忽略会偏差学习与状态推断。
边界协方差估计： 近奇异 \(Q\)、\(R\) 或 \(P_1\) 可以制造数值失败或退化似然行为。
局部优化： 不同初始化可以收敛到不同代表或局部最优。
泄漏： 把平滑未来数据放进在线预测、在测试序列上拟合预处理，或跨训练与测试拆分相邻时间点会产生乐观评估。
机制越界： 预测性 \(A\) 可以概括条件演化而不识别生物机制或因果转移律。




对任何可逆 \(T\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\)，定义 \(z'_t=Tz_t\)。变换参数
\[
A'=TAT^{-1},\quad B'=TB,\quad C'=CT^{-1},
\]
\[
m'_1=Tm_1,\quad P'_1=TP_1T^\top,\quad Q'=TQT^\top
\]
在 \(D\) 与 \(R\) 不变时生成相同观测分布。符号变化、置换、旋转与状态坐标缩放是特殊情形。因此没有坐标约定，单个潜轴与矩阵条目不被辨识；不变预测、声明输入下的迁移行为或相似类可能是站得住脚的目标。
相似变换不总是唯一歧义。非最小实现可以包含不可观测或不可达状态；未知 \(C,Q,R,P_1\)、受限输入覆盖、奇异协方差或有限序列长度可以制造更强结构或实用非可辨识性。好的优化器无法在观测设计辨识范围之外恢复唯一参数。
对确定性对，\((A,C)\) 的可观测性询问状态原则上能否从输出历史区分，而 \((A,B)\) 的可控性询问输入能否到达状态方向。在随机估计中，通过 \(Q\) 的激励与可检测性/可镇定性条件引入相关但不同的边界。这些性质不是写出 LGSSM 的自动推论，其本身也不证明因果或物理意义。




训练均值或独立高斯： 忽略潜结构与时间依赖。在其时序复杂度被归功之前，LGSSM 应改善留出预测似然或校准预测。
PCA： 确定性、静态、顺序无感的线性表示。它不提供过程/观测噪声分离或时序似然。
因子分析： 静态概率低秩观测模型。每个时间独立因子且无状态持续性时，它检验是否需要转移层。FA 仍是规范静态概率比较。
观测空间自回归或持续性： 直接预测测量，没有单独潜观测映射。它常常是比静态方法更强的时序基线，并检验潜状态是否增加价值。
已知参数模型： 把状态推断表现与参数学习引入的误差分开。模拟研究应报告已知参数与学习参数两种情形。




评估必须尊重序列顺序与预期任务的信息集：

当依赖跨越相邻时间点时，划分整个受试者、会话、试次或轨迹；
只在训练序列上拟合预处理、维数选择、参数与正则化；
对预测，报告一步与多步预测对数似然、误差与区间校准，不使用预测原点之后的未来观测；
对滤波，只用在线信息评估 \(p(z_t\mid x_{1:t})\) 或观测预测；
对平滑，把任务标注为回顾性，并只在该分别评估目标内允许 \(x_{t+1:T}\)；
报告留出边际序列似然，并与静态与观测空间时序基线比较；
检查创新均值、协方差、自相关、时序残差结构以及对状态维数与协方差约束的敏感性；以及
在合成已知真值下，只在允许相似对齐后评估状态与参数恢复，同时分别对不变预测与可观测协方差评分。

随机逐点训练/测试划分通常对序列预测无效。把平滑器与在线滤波器在同一目标上比较而不承认未来信息也无效。假设模型下的高似然或低状态误差不确立潜坐标唯一或具有机制性。
缺失观测可以通过在每个观测更新上评估观测分量来处理——等价于选择相关行与协方差子矩阵——前提是缺失机制在声明分析下可忽略。有信息缺失、删失、未知输入或观测时间选择需要其自身模型。这些变体不改变把未来信息排除在在线评估之外的需要。



考虑标量无输入模型
\[
z_{t+1}=az_t+w_t,
\qquad
x_t=z_t+v_t,
\]
其中 \(w_t\sim\mathcal N(0,q)\)、\(v_t\sim\mathcal N(0,r)\)。如果 \(|a|<1\) 且
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{q}{1-a^2}\right),
\]
则潜过程平稳，具有
\[
\operatorname{Var}(z_t)=\frac{q}{1-a^2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(x_t,x_{t+h})
=a^h\frac{q}{1-a^2}\quad(h>0),
\]
且 \(\operatorname{Var}(x_t)=q/(1-a^2)+r\)。这把时间持续性 \(a\)、过程变异 \(q\) 与测量变异 \(r\) 分开。设 \(a=0\) 产生时间独立潜变量；设 \(a=1\) 移除平稳协方差公式，尽管有限时域随机游走模型仍良定义。
未来的非可执行玩具契约会用已知 \(a,q,r\) 生成多条独立序列；比较训练均值、静态 FA、观测空间 AR(1)、已知参数 LGSSM 与学习参数 LGSSM；评估分块预测似然、多步校准、创新自相关、滤波对平滑信息集以及相似对齐状态恢复。阴性对照会包括单位根、相关 \(w_t\) 与 \(v_t\)、有信息缺失与不可观测扩维状态。本方法对象不产生数据、代码、拟合结果或基准。



离散时间 LGSSM 是 LDG 的规范概率时序潜基线。它在保持模型结构、状态推断、预测与参数学习之间清晰区分的同时，把因子分析式观测层连接到显式随机转移。它是后续卡尔曼滤波与平滑方法的前置模型类。






警告这并不蕴含



预测良好的 LGSSM 不证明潜坐标唯一、\(A\) 是生物机制或因果律、推断轨迹被直接观测，或数据位于具有已发现本征维数的流形上。稳定性不是平稳性，光滑后验均值可以是模型施加的，精确推断只在声明线性高斯模型与固定参数下精确。




LGSSM 可以建模有序运动学观测与已知任务输入，但必须声明对齐、可变采样间隔、动物级依赖、非线性生物力学与干预。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。



模型可以在声明注视或动眼特征中分离潜时序状态与测量变异性。扫视、删失、事件依赖噪声与不规则样本可以违反单一全局线性高斯模型。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。



传感器序列可以通过潜线性动力学建模，但重参考、空间混合、伪迹、有色噪声与非平稳性挑战 \(C\)、\(Q\) 与 \(R\)。潜状态不自动是神经源。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。



方法为具有有序试次或时间箱的群体记录提供基线。单元缩放、条件平均、试次依赖、输入定义与观测分布必须显式。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。





Kalman 发展线性滤波与预测的状态转移与随机激励方法，并通过其条件时间显式分离平滑、滤波与预测 (Kalman 1960年)。他的经核查表述此处不作为单独加性观测噪声方程的唯一来源。
Ghahramani 与 Hinton 指定离散时间线性高斯转移、观测、初始状态、\(Q/R\) 协方差模型，并从平滑潜充分统计量推导 EM 参数更新 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年)。





Särkkä 给出概率状态空间模型、线性高斯滤波与平滑目标、预测密度似然分解与参数估计的权威贝叶斯处理 (Särkkä 2013年)。
Roweis 与 Ghahramani 在共同生成框架中综述因子分析、PCA 与线性高斯动态模型，并区分静态与有序动态数据 (Roweis 和 Ghahramani 1999年)。





哪些状态维数与协方差约束对短、依赖、高维 LDG 序列仍可靠？
哪些干预或观测设计打破科学上重要的相似性与噪声分配歧义？
何时观测空间自回归充分，使潜状态不必要？
应如何引入不规则采样、有信息缺失与相关过程/观测噪声，而不模糊规范基线？





Schema 完整的方法对象，状态为 L2/review。
指定初始状态、输入驱动转移、观测律、高斯 \(Q/R\) 与独立假设。
区分模型规格、预测、滤波、平滑、边际似然与参数学习。
把滤波与平滑算法推迟到后续单元。
陈述有序离散时间、稳定性/平稳性、可观测性/可控性、缺失与输入边界。
陈述相似变换歧义与更强非可辨识性。
包含学习/固定、几何、监督、失效模式、基线、防泄漏评估与解析/散文玩具契约。
不作出因果、机制、流形或与模型无关本征维数主张。
四个保留来源经核查；元数据与 DOI 或稳定标识符已验证；未保留经验结果。
在一轮有界修正轮次后完成独立混合审查；聚焦复审返回 PASS。
在发布站点审查后，人类所有者根据记录的审查决定授权稳定晋升。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型（LGSSM）通过未观测状态描述有序观测序列，该状态以高斯过程噪声线性演化，并以高斯观测噪声线性生成测量。它提供一个联合概率模型，其中预测、状态推断、序列似然与参数学习可以被定义而不被当作同一任务 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年; Särkkä 2013年)。
本对象规定有限维、时间不变、离散时间模型，具有固定或外部提供的开环已知输入路径。它不呈现卡尔曼滤波或固定区间平滑算法，那些是后续方法单元。时变、切换、非线性、非高斯、连续时间、未知输入、反馈策略与控制设计变体在有界核心之外。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
对长度为 \(T\) 的单个序列，设

\(x_t\in\mathbb R^p\) 是观测向量；
\(u_t\in\mathbb R^r\) 是可选已知输入或回归量；以及
\(z_t\in\mathbb R^q\) 是潜状态。

可复现分析必须声明：

观测单元、序列边界、采样间隔、排序，以及矩阵是否被假设跨序列共同；
特征定义、单位、变换、排除与缺失数据策略；
哪些输入在拟合与预测时固定或外部提供，以及每个值何时可用；
潜维数 \(q\) 及其选择规程；
参数是从外部知识固定还是从训练序列学习；以及
精确目标：预测、滤波、平滑、边际似然、参数学习或模拟。

序列、受试者、会话或试次不是可互换重复。其依赖与参数共享必须被陈述。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
模型规格是参数元组
\[
\theta=(m_1,P_1,A,B,C,D,Q,R),
\]
维数与状态、输入与观测空间一致。在 \(\theta\) 条件下，它定义：

联合高斯律 \(p_\theta(z_{1:T},x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})\)；
未来状态与观测的预测分布；
只以目标时间前可用观测为条件的滤波分布；
以完整声明观测区间为条件的平滑分布；
对 \(z_{1:T}\) 积分后的边际序列似然；以及
带不确定性的模型条件潜状态摘要。

实现还可以返回拟合参数、预测均值/协方差、滤波或平滑状态矩、创新与似然贡献。这些输出具有不同条件信息，必须相应标注。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
状态携带下一步转移所需信息，而观测是状态的有噪线性视图。马尔可夫分解把一条高维轨迹分布转化为初始状态律、局部转移律与局部观测律。高斯封闭性使相关条件与边际分布为高斯，允许参数已知时精确有限时域推断 (Särkkä 2013年, chs. 4, 8)。
方法的价值不仅在于推断均值轨迹看起来光滑。它在于声明的随机时序模型产生可检验预测分布，并把转移处引入的不确定性与测量处引入的不确定性分开。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
规范输入驱动模型是
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N(m_1,P_1),
\]
\[
z_{t+1}=Az_t+Bu_t+w_t,
\qquad
w_t\sim\mathcal N(0,Q),
\]
\[
x_t=Cz_t+Du_t+v_t,
\qquad
v_t\sim\mathcal N(0,R).
\]
无输入核心通过省略 \(u_t\)、\(B\) 与 \(D\) 恢复。除非显式泛化，模型假设：

\(P_1,Q\succeq0\) 且 \(R\succ0\)；
\(z_1\)、每个 \(w_t\) 与每个 \(v_s\) 相互独立；
过程与观测噪声跨时间独立；
\(A,B,C,D,Q,R\) 在序列上恒定；
潜转移是一阶马尔可夫；
观测在给定状态路径与输入时跨时间条件独立；以及
输入预先固定或外部提供，不依赖同期或未来观测，因此是有效条件变量而非未解释随机原因。

高斯性强于只指定均值与协方差。相关过程与观测噪声、有色噪声、异方差、时变矩阵或依赖历史的测量需要显式修改模型，而非对 \(Q\) 或 \(R\) 的非正式重新解读。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
对固定开环输入路径，联合律分解为
\[
p_\theta(z_{1:T},x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})
=p_\theta(z_1)
\prod_{t=1}^{T-1}p_\theta(z_{t+1}\mid z_t,u_t)
\prod_{t=1}^{T}p_\theta(x_t\mid z_t,u_t),
\]
其中
\[
p_\theta(z_{t+1}\mid z_t,u_t)
=\mathcal N(Az_t+Bu_t,Q),
\]
\[
p_\theta(x_t\mid z_t,u_t)
=\mathcal N(Cz_t+Du_t,R).
\]
该分解定义若干不同条件目标。下方出现的未来输入值必须是已知场景值，而非编码未来观测的控制：
\[
\text{forecasting:}\quad
p(z_{t+h},x_{t+h}\mid x_{1:t},u_{1:t+h}),
\]
\[
\text{filtering:}\quad
p(z_t\mid x_{1:t},u_{1:t}),
\]
\[
\text{smoothing:}\quad
p(z_t\mid x_{1:T},u_{1:T}),\quad T>t,
\]
或完整路径后验 \(p(z_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T},u_{1:T})\)。Kalman 通过被估计状态时间是早于、等于还是晚于最终条件观测来显式区分平滑、滤波与预测 (Kalman 1960年)。精确递推被有意推迟到单独滤波与平滑方法对象。
边际似然是
\[
p_\theta(x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})
=\int p_\theta(z_{1:T},x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})\,dz_{1:T}.
\]
它可以分解为一步预测密度，
\[
p_\theta(x_{1:T}\mid u_{1:T})
=\prod_{t=1}^{T}
p_\theta(x_t\mid x_{1:t-1},u_{1:t}),
\]
这使序列评分与状态点估计分离 (Särkkä 2013年, sec. 12.1)。
反馈控制数据需要单独时间与策略模型。有效控制 \(u_t\) 必须可从其驱动转移之前可用的信息测量，且当 \(D\ne0\) 时在同期观测 \(x_t\) 之前可用；在 \(u_t\) 中使用 \(x_t\) 本身会制造代数环。如果未来控制依赖未来观测，以已实现 \(u_{1:T}\) 为条件会泄漏未来信息。策略感知似然与预测必须改为陈述非预期策略，并对尚不知道的控制积分或模拟。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
取决于规程，参数学习可以估计 \(m_1,P_1,A,B,C,D,Q,R\) 的部分或全部并选择 \(q\)。给定拟合参数，状态推断确定潜状态上的条件分布；除非使用显式联合或在线学习规程，它不重新学习模型参数。
最大似然学习瞄准对潜状态积分后的可观测序列分布。EM 则在模型条件潜充分统计量的期望与在精确步骤下增加同一边际似然的参数更新之间交替 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年)。因此推断状态路径是中间不确定量，不是观测训练数据。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
分析者固定状态维数或其选择搜索、序列边界、时间步、输入定义、矩阵结构与参数共享、高斯与独立假设、协方差约束、初始状态处理、缺失数据机制、学习准则、正则化或先验，以及评估目标。
当某些矩阵来自物理建模时，固定对估计的划分必须显式。如果 \(C\)、\(Q\)、\(R\)、状态坐标或输入是现象学学习的，把 \(A\) 称为「动力学」并不确立它是物理定律。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
时间是离散且有序的。置换观测通常会改变似然。一阶马尔可夫假设陈述，在 \(z_t\) 与已知输入条件下，\(z_{t+1}\) 不依赖更早状态。它不蕴含观测序列是一阶马尔可夫的。
稳定性与平稳性不同。 对时间不变无输入均值动力学，\(\rho(A)<1\) 是通常的 Schur 稳定条件，在该条件下确定性扰动衰减。零均值、常值 \(Q\) 与合适有限协方差时，稳定 \(A\) 支持满足
\[
\Sigma=A\Sigma A^\top+Q.
\]
的平稳状态协方差 \(\Sigma\)。只有初始化与输入也与平稳律相容时，过程才平稳。从该律之外初始化的稳定模型具有瞬态；单位根或不稳定的有限时域模型仍可以定义有效分布而不平稳。时变输入可以使均值非平稳，即使 \(A\) 稳定。
不规则采样不能通过静默地把每个索引间隙当作相等来处理。它需要依赖间隙的转移、底层连续时间模型与离散化，或其他显式变体。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
潜状态在有限维向量空间中表示。\(A\) 在所选状态坐标中线性，而 \(Q\) 与 \(R\) 定义依赖坐标的马氏不确定性。除非度量与坐标约定被论证，后验状态均值之间的欧氏距离没有不变科学意义。
模型不设定非线性流形或黎曼几何。低维线性潜状态是建模选择，不是本征维数或唯一状态空间的证明。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
基于观测序列的似然拟合对外部标签无监督。固定开环输入条件化转移与观测律；其存在在预测标签意义上不自动是「监督」。用于设计状态、约束矩阵、选择超参数或给模型评分的标签、结果或干预会引入任务依赖，必须被声明。
与未建模扰动相关的观测输入不自动外生。包含 \(u_t\) 不辨识由 \(B\) 或 \(D\) 表示的因果效应。反馈依赖输入需要上述界定的策略感知扩展，而非此处使用的开环条件分解。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
对已知参数，有限时域线性高斯预测、滤波与平滑是精确高斯条件化问题。它们只在目标与信息集上不同，但需要不同计算。滤波使用到当前时间为止的数据；固定区间平滑在声明区间内使用未来观测 (Särkkä 2013年, chs. 4, 8)。
参数学习是单独优化或贝叶斯推断问题。直接最大似然优化可以使用预测密度分解。在 EM 中，E 步需要当前参数下的平滑期望，如 \(\mathbb E[z_t]\)、\(\mathbb E[z_tz_t^\top]\) 与 \(\mathbb E[z_tz_{t-1}^\top]\)；M 步从这些期望更新模型参数 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年)。因此 EM 实现可以在内部调用滤波与平滑，但学习模型、滤波后验、平滑后验与优化器不是可互换对象。
似然在自由潜参数化中一般非凸。必须报告初始化、协方差约束、正则化、停止准则、多次启动与数值分解。递增的 EM 目标不证明全局最优性或科学有效性。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
它定义有序潜与观测序列上的连贯联合分布。
过程与观测不确定性通过 \(Q\) 与 \(R\) 分别表示。
参数固定时精确高斯预测与状态后验可用。
边际似然支持序列级预测比较与参数学习。
可以在不放弃线性高斯易处理性的情况下纳入输入。
在非线性或非高斯潜模型之前，它是透明时序基线。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
错误潜维数或结构： 省略模态留下时序残差结构；冗余模态制造弱辨识或未使用状态。
噪声权衡： 短、弱观测序列可能无法区分过程变异与观测变异，因此 \(Q\)、\(R\)、\(C\) 与状态路径可以相互补偿。
未建模依赖： 有色、相关、异方差或状态依赖噪声使白独立高斯假设失效。
非线性或制度变化： 单个全局 \(A\) 与 \(C\) 无法表示切换、饱和、弯曲观测映射或突然干预。
不稳定或近单位根： 预测可以发散或变得高度不确定，短记录中的参数估计可能敏感。
不可观测模态： 不影响可用观测的潜方向无法从这些观测恢复。
弱激励： 输入或过程噪声可能无法探索估计转移效应所需的方向。
缺失或删失： 把有信息缺失观测当作可忽略会偏差学习与状态推断。
边界协方差估计： 近奇异 \(Q\)、\(R\) 或 \(P_1\) 可以制造数值失败或退化似然行为。
局部优化： 不同初始化可以收敛到不同代表或局部最优。
泄漏： 把平滑未来数据放进在线预测、在测试序列上拟合预处理，或跨训练与测试拆分相邻时间点会产生乐观评估。
机制越界： 预测性 \(A\) 可以概括条件演化而不识别生物机制或因果转移律。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
对任何可逆 \(T\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\)，定义 \(z'_t=Tz_t\)。变换参数
\[
A'=TAT^{-1},\quad B'=TB,\quad C'=CT^{-1},
\]
\[
m'_1=Tm_1,\quad P'_1=TP_1T^\top,\quad Q'=TQT^\top
\]
在 \(D\) 与 \(R\) 不变时生成相同观测分布。符号变化、置换、旋转与状态坐标缩放是特殊情形。因此没有坐标约定，单个潜轴与矩阵条目不被辨识；不变预测、声明输入下的迁移行为或相似类可能是站得住脚的目标。
相似变换不总是唯一歧义。非最小实现可以包含不可观测或不可达状态；未知 \(C,Q,R,P_1\)、受限输入覆盖、奇异协方差或有限序列长度可以制造更强结构或实用非可辨识性。好的优化器无法在观测设计辨识范围之外恢复唯一参数。
对确定性对，\((A,C)\) 的可观测性询问状态原则上能否从输出历史区分，而 \((A,B)\) 的可控性询问输入能否到达状态方向。在随机估计中，通过 \(Q\) 的激励与可检测性/可镇定性条件引入相关但不同的边界。这些性质不是写出 LGSSM 的自动推论，其本身也不证明因果或物理意义。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
训练均值或独立高斯： 忽略潜结构与时间依赖。在其时序复杂度被归功之前，LGSSM 应改善留出预测似然或校准预测。
PCA： 确定性、静态、顺序无感的线性表示。它不提供过程/观测噪声分离或时序似然。
因子分析： 静态概率低秩观测模型。每个时间独立因子且无状态持续性时，它检验是否需要转移层。FA 仍是规范静态概率比较。
观测空间自回归或持续性： 直接预测测量，没有单独潜观测映射。它常常是比静态方法更强的时序基线，并检验潜状态是否增加价值。
已知参数模型： 把状态推断表现与参数学习引入的误差分开。模拟研究应报告已知参数与学习参数两种情形。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
评估必须尊重序列顺序与预期任务的信息集：

当依赖跨越相邻时间点时，划分整个受试者、会话、试次或轨迹；
只在训练序列上拟合预处理、维数选择、参数与正则化；
对预测，报告一步与多步预测对数似然、误差与区间校准，不使用预测原点之后的未来观测；
对滤波，只用在线信息评估 \(p(z_t\mid x_{1:t})\) 或观测预测；
对平滑，把任务标注为回顾性，并只在该分别评估目标内允许 \(x_{t+1:T}\)；
报告留出边际序列似然，并与静态与观测空间时序基线比较；
检查创新均值、协方差、自相关、时序残差结构以及对状态维数与协方差约束的敏感性；以及
在合成已知真值下，只在允许相似对齐后评估状态与参数恢复，同时分别对不变预测与可观测协方差评分。

随机逐点训练/测试划分通常对序列预测无效。把平滑器与在线滤波器在同一目标上比较而不承认未来信息也无效。假设模型下的高似然或低状态误差不确立潜坐标唯一或具有机制性。
缺失观测可以通过在每个观测更新上评估观测分量来处理——等价于选择相关行与协方差子矩阵——前提是缺失机制在声明分析下可忽略。有信息缺失、删失、未知输入或观测时间选择需要其自身模型。这些变体不改变把未来信息排除在在线评估之外的需要。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
考虑标量无输入模型
\[
z_{t+1}=az_t+w_t,
\qquad
x_t=z_t+v_t,
\]
其中 \(w_t\sim\mathcal N(0,q)\)、\(v_t\sim\mathcal N(0,r)\)。如果 \(|a|<1\) 且
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{q}{1-a^2}\right),
\]
则潜过程平稳，具有
\[
\operatorname{Var}(z_t)=\frac{q}{1-a^2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(x_t,x_{t+h})
=a^h\frac{q}{1-a^2}\quad(h>0),
\]
且 \(\operatorname{Var}(x_t)=q/(1-a^2)+r\)。这把时间持续性 \(a\)、过程变异 \(q\) 与测量变异 \(r\) 分开。设 \(a=0\) 产生时间独立潜变量；设 \(a=1\) 移除平稳协方差公式，尽管有限时域随机游走模型仍良定义。
未来的非可执行玩具契约会用已知 \(a,q,r\) 生成多条独立序列；比较训练均值、静态 FA、观测空间 AR(1)、已知参数 LGSSM 与学习参数 LGSSM；评估分块预测似然、多步校准、创新自相关、滤波对平滑信息集以及相似对齐状态恢复。阴性对照会包括单位根、相关 \(w_t\) 与 \(v_t\)、有信息缺失与不可观测扩维状态。本方法对象不产生数据、代码、拟合结果或基准。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
离散时间 LGSSM 是 LDG 的规范概率时序潜基线。它在保持模型结构、状态推断、预测与参数学习之间清晰区分的同时，把因子分析式观测层连接到显式随机转移。它是后续卡尔曼滤波与平滑方法的前置模型类。






警告这并不蕴含



预测良好的 LGSSM 不证明潜坐标唯一、\(A\) 是生物机制或因果律、推断轨迹被直接观测，或数据位于具有已发现本征维数的流形上。稳定性不是平稳性，光滑后验均值可以是模型施加的，精确推断只在声明线性高斯模型与固定参数下精确。




LGSSM 可以建模有序运动学观测与已知任务输入，但必须声明对齐、可变采样间隔、动物级依赖、非线性生物力学与干预。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。



模型可以在声明注视或动眼特征中分离潜时序状态与测量变异性。扫视、删失、事件依赖噪声与不规则样本可以违反单一全局线性高斯模型。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。



传感器序列可以通过潜线性动力学建模，但重参考、空间混合、伪迹、有色噪声与非平稳性挑战 \(C\)、\(Q\) 与 \(R\)。潜状态不自动是神经源。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。



方法为具有有序试次或时间箱的群体记录提供基线。单元缩放、条件平均、试次依赖、输入定义与观测分布必须显式。此处不保留模态特定经验结果。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
Kalman 发展线性滤波与预测的状态转移与随机激励方法，并通过其条件时间显式分离平滑、滤波与预测 (Kalman 1960年)。他的经核查表述此处不作为单独加性观测噪声方程的唯一来源。
Ghahramani 与 Hinton 指定离散时间线性高斯转移、观测、初始状态、\(Q/R\) 协方差模型，并从平滑潜充分统计量推导 EM 参数更新 (Ghahramani 和 Hinton 1996年)。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
Särkkä 给出概率状态空间模型、线性高斯滤波与平滑目标、预测密度似然分解与参数估计的权威贝叶斯处理 (Särkkä 2013年)。
Roweis 与 Ghahramani 在共同生成框架中综述因子分析、PCA 与线性高斯动态模型，并区分静态与有序动态数据 (Roweis 和 Ghahramani 1999年)。

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
哪些状态维数与协方差约束对短、依赖、高维 LDG 序列仍可靠？
哪些干预或观测设计打破科学上重要的相似性与噪声分配歧义？
何时观测空间自回归充分，使潜状态不必要？
应如何引入不规则采样、有信息缺失与相关过程/观测噪声，而不模糊规范基线？

title: 离散时间线性高斯状态空间模型
text:
Schema 完整的方法对象，状态为 L2/review。
指定初始状态、输入驱动转移、观测律、高斯 \(Q/R\) 与独立假设。
区分模型规格、预测、滤波、平滑、边际似然与参数学习。
把滤波与平滑算法推迟到后续单元。
陈述有序离散时间、稳定性/平稳性、可观测性/可控性、缺失与输入边界。
陈述相似变换歧义与更强非可辨识性。
包含学习/固定、几何、监督、失效模式、基线、防泄漏评估与解析/散文玩具契约。
不作出因果、机制、流形或与模型无关本征维数主张。
四个保留来源经核查；元数据与 DOI 或稳定标识符已验证；未保留经验结果。
在一轮有界修正轮次后完成独立混合审查；聚焦复审返回 PASS。
在发布站点审查后，人类所有者根据记录的审查决定授权稳定晋升。

title: 卡尔曼滤波
text:
卡尔曼滤波在声明线性高斯状态空间模型（LGSSM）中顺序计算当前潜状态分布，只使用到当前时间为止可用的观测。其在时间 \(t\) 的目标是
\[
p(z_t\mid x_{1:t},u_{1:t}),
\]
而非使用 \(x_{t+1:T}\) 的回顾性分布。递推在基于先前滤波分布与转移模型的预测与基于当前观测的更新之间交替 (Kalman 1960年; Särkkä 2013年, ch. 4)。
本对象把模型矩阵与协方差参数视为滤波期间固定且已知。指定或学习 LGSSM、滤波其状态、预测未来观测与平滑过去状态是不同任务。固定区间卡尔曼平滑被推迟到 P2-U10。



使用前置方法中定义的时间不变、输入驱动 LGSSM：
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N(m_1,P_1),
\]
\[
z_{t+1}=Az_t+Bu_t+w_t,
\qquad
w_t\sim\mathcal N(0,Q),
\]
\[
x_t=Cz_t+Du_t+v_t,
\qquad
v_t\sim\mathcal N(0,R).
\]
这里 \(z_t\in\mathbb R^q\)、\(x_t\in\mathbb R^p\)，可选已知输入是 \(u_t\in\mathbb R^r\)。规范假设是 \(P_1,Q\succeq0\)、\(R\succ0\)、初始状态与所有过程与观测噪声相互独立、噪声时间独立，以及固定或外部提供的开环输入路径。
可复现滤波问题必须声明：

固定参数元组 \((m_1,P_1,A,B,C,D,Q,R)\) 及其出处；
状态、观测与输入单位及坐标约定；
序列边界、采样间隔与序列之间重置的处理；
每个输入确切何时可用；
在第一个观测处初始化；
每个时间哪些观测分量可用及原因；
数值线性代数方法、精度与协方差表示；以及
目标是否为当前状态推断、一步预测评分、在线监控或独立学习规程的输入。

对从 \(t\) 到 \(t+1\) 的转移，\(u_t\) 必须在该转移被评估前已知。如果 \(D\ne0\)，测量均值中使用的直接前馈输入 \(u_t\) 必须在 \(x_t\) 被同化前可用。由 \(x_t\) 本身构造的控制会制造同期代数环，除非提供单独步内时间模型。依赖未来观测的未来输入不是已知条件变量。



在每个时间 \(t\)，滤波器返回或定义：

预测状态分布 \[
p(z_t\mid x_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
=\mathcal N(m_{t\mid t-1},P_{t\mid t-1});
\]
一步预测观测分布 \[
p(x_t\mid x_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
=\mathcal N(\widehat x_{t\mid t-1},S_t);
\]
创新 \(\nu_t=x_t-\widehat x_{t\mid t-1}\) 与创新协方差 \(S_t\)；以及
滤波分布 \[
p(z_t\mid x_{1:t},u_{1:t})
=\mathcal N(m_{t\mid t},P_{t\mid t}).
\]

滤波均值是模型条件后验均值，不是观测状态。其协方差描述固定模型与条件信息下的不确定性；除非不确定性被单独建模，它不包含关于学习参数的不确定性。



先前滤波分布概括下一个递归步骤所需的过去观测信息。线性传播加高斯过程噪声保留高斯性。当前线性高斯测量随后产生高斯条件分布。因此在声明模型下，均值与协方差对精确有限维滤波是充分的 (Särkkä 2013年, secs. 4.2–4.3)。
创新是当前观测中未被先前观测与已知输入预测的部分。其协方差把预测状态不确定性投影到观测坐标并与观测噪声组合。卡尔曼增益把这个观测空间差异映射为状态空间修正。



递推继承 LGSSM 的每个假设。特别地：

状态演化与观测在所选坐标中线性；
先验与噪声为高斯；
过程与观测噪声为白噪声、相互独立并独立于初始状态；
马尔可夫状态与条件观测结构被正确指定；
滤波器使用的矩阵与协方差参数在递推期间固定；
输入路径在声明步内时间下非预期；以及
任何缺失观测模式除非添加缺失模型，否则被当作已观测/固定且无信息。

在这些条件与精确算术下，递推给出精确高斯滤波分布。Kalman 的原始状态空间处理通过正交投影推导最优线性估计，并通过被估计时间相对最新条件观测显式区分滤波、预测与平滑 (Kalman 1960年)。本对象使用更窄的贝叶斯线性高斯解读：精确性以所述概率模型为条件，不是模型生成了科学系统的证据。



把 \(\mathcal I_t=\sigma(x_{1:t},u_{1:t})\) 写为同化 \(x_t\) 后可用信息。定义
\[
m_{t\mid s}=\mathbb E[z_t\mid\mathcal I_s],
\qquad
P_{t\mid s}=\operatorname{Cov}(z_t\mid\mathcal I_s).
\]
下方任何量都不以 \(x_{t+1}\) 或任何更晚观测为条件。


在第一个观测之前，
\[
m_{1\mid0}=m_1,
\qquad
P_{1\mid0}=P_1.
\]
该先验是模型的一部分。有信息的外部初始化必须被独立论证。用任意巨大协方差替换未知初始分布不自动是精确扩散初始化，且可能在数值上有害；精确扩散变体在本有界方法之外。



对 \(t\ge2\)，在滤波时间 \(t-1\) 之后，
\[
m_{t\mid t-1}=A m_{t-1\mid t-1}+B u_{t-1},
\]
\[
P_{t\mid t-1}=A P_{t-1\mid t-1}A^\top+Q.
\]
因此
\[
p(z_t\mid x_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
=\mathcal N(m_{t\mid t-1},P_{t\mid t-1}).
\]
转移输入是 \(u_{t-1}\)，因为它驱动 \(z_{t-1}\mapsto z_t\)。条件记号包含 \(u_t\)，因为同期观测均值可能使用 \(D u_t\)；\(u_t\) 不追溯驱动先前转移。



预测观测均值、创新与创新协方差是
\[
\widehat x_{t\mid t-1}=C m_{t\mid t-1}+D u_t,
\]
\[
\nu_t=x_t-\widehat x_{t\mid t-1},
\]
\[
S_t=C P_{t\mid t-1}C^\top+R.
\]
预测观测律是
\[
p(x_t\mid x_{1:t-1},u_{1:t})
=\mathcal N(\widehat x_{t\mid t-1},S_t).
\]
卡尔曼增益是
\[
K_t=P_{t\mid t-1}C^\top S_t^{-1},
\]
滤波矩是
\[
m_{t\mid t}=m_{t\mid t-1}+K_t\nu_t,
\]
\[
P_{t\mid t}=P_{t\mid t-1}-K_tS_tK_t^\top.
\]
这些是闭式高斯条件化方程 (Särkkä 2013年, theorem 4.2)。实现应求解涉及 \(S_t\) 的线性系统，而非显式形成 \(S_t^{-1}\)。



在精确算术中，先前协方差更新等价于
\[
P_{t\mid t}=(I-K_tC)P_{t\mid t-1}.
\]
短形式可以通过浮点消去丢失对称性或半正定结构。Joseph 形式
\[
P_{t\mid t}
=(I-K_tC)P_{t\mid t-1}(I-K_tC)^\top
+K_t R K_t^\top
\]
在 \(K_t\) 为卡尔曼增益时代数等价，并把协方差表示为半正定项之和。Asada 的经核查实现笔记特别使用该形式减少舍入造成的不对称协方差，并讨论因子化协方差表示作为进一步保障 (Asada 2006年, sec. 4.10)。
Joseph 形式不是普遍数值灵药。稳定实现还应使用对称分解与求解、监控对称性与正定性，并避免显式矩阵逆。平方根或因子化滤波器传播协方差因子，对严重缩放或条件数问题可能更可取；它们是同一声明滤波目标的计算实现，不是不同科学模型 (Särkkä 2013年, sec. 4.3; Asada 2006年, sec. 4.10)。详细平方根算法不在范围内。



设 \(M_t\) 是只保留时间 \(t\) 观测分量的行选择矩阵。定义
\[
x_t^{(o)}=M_t x_t,
\quad
C_t=M_tC,
\quad
D_t=M_tD,
\quad
R_t=M_tRM_t^\top.
\]
用 \(x_t^{(o)},C_t,D_t,R_t\) 应用普通更新。这保留保留测量误差之间的相关。如果没有分量被观测，跳过测量更新：
\[
m_{t\mid t}=m_{t\mid t-1},
\qquad
P_{t\mid t}=P_{t\mid t-1}.
\]
该行选择规则只有在缺失指示器在已建模观测与协变量之外不贡献关于 \(z_t\) 的额外信息时才精确。有信息缺失、阈值删失、饱和或状态依赖传感器失效需要显式观测/缺失模型。



在规范假设 \(P_{t\mid t-1}\succeq0\) 与 \(R\succ0\) 下，创新协方差 \(S_t\) 正定。行选择后，对非空不同保留坐标集 \(R_t\succ0\)，因此精确算术中基于 Cholesky 的求解可用。
奇异 \(S_t\) 表明实现已离开该正则模型类——例如使用零噪声精确约束、重复确定性测量行或半定 \(R\)。普通密度与逆公式随后不再原样适用。可以移除冗余行，或单独论证的退化高斯/约束表述可以使用支持感知广义逆。添加任意对角「抖动」会改变观测模型，不得被呈现为中性的数学修复。
如果 \(S_t\) 理论上正定但病态，重标变量、使用 Cholesky 或其他秩揭示分解、避免显式求逆，并检查模型是否有近冗余传感器或极端协方差尺度。分解失败是诊断，不是静默丢弃不确定性的许可。



对完整 \(p\) 维观测与非奇异 \(S_t\)，创新给出一步对数预测密度
\[
\ell_t
=-\frac12\left[
p\log(2\pi)+\log|S_t|+\nu_t^\top S_t^{-1}\nu_t
\right].
\]
有部分观测时，把 \(p,\nu_t,S_t\) 替换为保留维数与所选量。对 \(\ell_t\) 求和给出固定参数边际序列对数似然。在该似然内使用参数估计不把滤波递推本身变成参数学习算法。




参数固定时，滤波器不学习任何模型参数。它从传入观测计算 \(z_t\) 上的相继条件分布与 \(x_t\) 上的一步预测分布。
模型参数可能来自物理、在单独训练序列上估计，或由不同算法更新。EM 与似然优化可以在内部调用滤波器，但外层参数学习准则与更新保持分离。把滤波均值当作无误差观测用于不限定条件的二阶段拟合会丢弃后验不确定性，并可能制造循环结论。



分析者固定 LGSSM 结构、状态维数、参数元组、坐标系、序列/重置策略、输入时序、缺失假设、初始化、数值精度、协方差表示与任何诊断阈值。如果参数被估计，训练划分、估计量、约束与模型选择规则在滤波操作之外固定。
滤波器不通过决定信任动力学还是测量多少来选择 \(Q\) 与 \(R\)。那些协方差是模型参数，其值需要外部指定或声明估计规程。



滤波相对于声明信息顺序是因果的：\(m_{t\mid t}\) 与 \(P_{t\mid t}\) 依赖 \(x_{1:t}\) 而非 \(x_{t+1:T}\)。迟到或修正观测需要单独声明的重放、乱序更新或平滑规程。
算法假设 LGSSM 的离散采样与序列边界。不等时间间隙需要间隙特定转移与过程协方差；把索引递增当作每个间隙相等会改变时间模型。滤波本身不使推断均值轨迹成为动力学证据：其时序结构继承自 \(A,Q\)、初始化与观测。



状态占据有限维向量空间。预测与更新使用声明坐标中的仿射映射与协方差椭球。\(P_{t\mid s}\) 与 \(S_t\) 为不确定性与创新定义依赖坐标的马氏几何。
在可逆状态坐标变换 \(z'_t=Tz_t\) 下，矩与模型矩阵必须一致变换，包括
\[
m'_{t\mid s}=Tm_{t\mid s},
\qquad
P'_{t\mid s}=TP_{t\mid s}T^\top,
\qquad
C'=CT^{-1}.
\]
可观测预测律可以保持不变，而潜轴与增益条目改变。滤波均值之间的欧氏距离、视觉光滑性或协方差椭球不确立流形、黎曼几何、本征维数或特权生物坐标。



不需要外部结果标签。当前测量是概率观测模型中的证据，不是普通预测标签意义上的监督目标。已知输入条件化模型；它们不会仅仅因为被提供而变成标签。
用于选择状态维数、矩阵、协方差参数、预处理或诊断阈值的外部标签或结果会引入任务依赖。此类选择必须发生在训练/验证边界内，并与在线滤波分开报告。



对固定参数，滤波是递归高斯推断而非非凸优化。每步使用矩阵乘法、加法与创新协方差中的求解。计算成本与条件数依赖状态与观测维数以及所选分解。
不保证任意软件实现复现数学递推。测试应比较协方差形式、保留对称性、检查半正定容差，并对照直接联合高斯条件化验证小问题。计算有限输出而无异常不是数值正确性的证据。




固定线性高斯模型下精确有限时域滤波矩。
用固定大小状态摘要顺序处理，而非对整个历史重复条件化。
显式传播过程与观测不确定性。
一步预测密度与创新适合评分与诊断。
通过声明行选择自然处理不规则缺失测量分量。
为后续平滑与近似非线性或非高斯滤波器提供透明基线。





模型误设： 非线性转移、非高斯尾部、有色噪声、相关过程/观测噪声、时变参数或被省略输入使声明递推与模型失配。
错误 \(Q/R\) 平衡： 低估过程噪声可以使滤波器对传播过度自信；低估观测噪声可以使它追逐测量。
不良初始化： 选择不佳的均值或协方差可以主导短序列或与弱可观测性交互。
不可观测或弱观测方向： 即使某些观测坐标拟合良好，不确定性也可以保持大或变得实用病态。
预期输入： 包含同期/未来观测信息的控制或回归量把证据泄漏进预测。
