title: Stability
text:
Stability describes whether specified small perturbations of a dynamical object produce evolutions that remain close under a declared time direction and notion of closeness.



“Stable” is incomplete unless the object, perturbation, time horizon, and comparison criterion are stated. At this stage LDG focuses on forward Lyapunov stability of a fixed point and distinguishes it from asymptotic return.



Balance a ball in a bowl and nudge it slightly. If it stays near the bottom, the equilibrium is stable. If it also returns toward the bottom, it is asymptotically stable. A ball balanced on a hilltop is a fixed point but not stable.



Let \(x^\ast\) be a fixed point of a forward evolution on a state space \(\mathcal X\). In neighborhood form, \(x^\ast\) is Lyapunov stable when, for every neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^\ast\), there exists a neighborhood \(V\subseteq U\) such that every trajectory starting in \(V\) is supported for all \(t\ge0\) and remains in \(U\) for all \(t\ge0\).
On a metric state space \((\mathcal X,d)\) this becomes
\[
\forall\varepsilon>0\;\exists\delta>0\;\forall x_0\in\mathcal X:
\quad
d(x_0,x^\ast)<\delta
\Longrightarrow
\left(
[0,\infty)\subseteq I_{x_0}
\;\text{ and }\;
d(\phi_t(x_0),x^\ast)<\varepsilon\ \forall t\ge0
\right),
\]
where \(I_{x_0}\) is the supported elapsed-time interval through \(x_0\).
The fixed point is asymptotically stable when it is Lyapunov stable and there is a neighborhood \(A\) of \(x^\ast\) such that every trajectory from \(A\) is supported for all forward time and
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}d(\phi_t(x_0),x^\ast)=0.
\]
Convergence without the Lyapunov condition is attraction but is not automatically asymptotic stability. Teschl explicitly notes that the convergence condition alone need not imply stability (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.5).
The fixed point is locally exponentially stable when there exist constants \(C\ge1\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(\delta>0\) such that, for all \(x_0\) with \(d(x_0,x^\ast)<\delta\), the forward trajectory is supported and
\[
d(\phi_t(x_0),x^\ast)
\le
C e^{-\alpha t}d(x_0,x^\ast),
\qquad t\ge0.
\]
This quantitative bound implies Lyapunov stability and local attraction under the stated metric and support assumptions (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.5).


The definitions above are local because they constrain only sufficiently nearby initial states. Global asymptotic stability additionally requires the declared forward domain to include every admissible initial state and requires all of those trajectories to converge to \(x^\ast\), while retaining Lyapunov stability. “Global” is therefore relative to the stated state space and forward domain, not necessarily to all of \(\mathbb R^n\).



The bounded definitions perturb the initial state while holding the evolution rule, parameters, inputs, state description, and metric fixed. Parameter robustness, input-to-state stability, stochastic stability, structural stability, observation robustness, and numerical stability are different questions with different perturbation objects and criteria.









TipLDG Synthesis



The neighborhood definition of Lyapunov and asymptotic stability is preserved under a verified topological conjugacy that transports the evolution and neighborhoods. Exponential stability additionally contains a numerical rate and distance bound, so it is not invariant under an arbitrary homeomorphism or arbitrary rescaling without further regularity and metric-equivalence conditions. LDG therefore records the metric and coordinate convention for quantitative rate claims rather than treating \(C\) or \(\alpha\) as representation-free.







\(x^\ast\): the fixed point whose stability is tested.
\(x_0\): a perturbed initial state.
\(d\): the declared notion of distance or closeness.
\(\varepsilon\): tolerated departure from the reference.
\(\delta\): allowed initial perturbation.
\(t\ge0\): the forward-time direction in scope.
\(A\): local basin neighborhood used in the asymptotic-stability definition.
\(C,\alpha\): multiplicative constant and exponential decay rate.
forward support/completeness: requirement that the quantified trajectories exist for all \(t\ge0\).




Fixed Point identifies the invariant reference state. Flow supplies its evolution and the nearby trajectories being compared. Metric makes the quantitative notion of closeness explicit.
Assumed background: neighborhoods, limits, and elementary metric distance.










Concept
Distinction




Fixed point
Fixedness concerns the unperturbed state; stability concerns nearby initial states.


Attraction
Requires convergence toward a set. It need not imply Lyapunov stability; asymptotic stability requires both attraction and stability.


Global asymptotic stability
Extends attraction to the declared full forward domain while retaining Lyapunov stability. It is stronger than a local statement.


Exponential stability
Adds a metric-dependent quantitative decay bound; it is stronger than asymptotic stability in the stated setting.


Robustness
Robustness may concern parameter, model, input, or observation perturbations rather than initial-state perturbations.


Numerical stability
A property of an algorithm or discretization, not automatically of the underlying dynamical system.


Statistical stationarity
A distributional time-invariance property, not Lyapunov stability.






Stability does not imply:

asymptotic convergence unless that stronger condition is shown;
resilience to parameter changes, inputs, noise, or model misspecification;
global behavior from all initial conditions unless global scope and forward support are proved;
a unique equilibrium or basin;
that a finite observed trajectory will visibly return; or
that low variance in data establishes dynamical stability;
that successful decoding, low reconstruction error, or a smooth posterior mean verifies all nearby initial states and all future times; or
that stability transfers through a non-injective observation or projection.




Three scalar systems separate the principal cases:

For \(\dot x=0\), every point is Lyapunov stable because nearby states remain where they started, but no point attracts a distinct neighboring state.
For \(\dot x=-x\), \(x^\ast=0\) is exponentially stable because \(x(t)=x_0e^{-t}\) satisfies the decay bound with \(C=1\) and \(\alpha=1\).
For \(\dot x=x\), \(x^\ast=0\) is unstable because arbitrarily small nonzero initial states grow in forward time.

These examples classify the stated systems directly. They do not authorize a general Jacobian or linearization criterion for nonlinear models; those theorem-level results remain outside this bounded Concept.



Stability can formalize hypotheses about persistence or recovery of neural and behavioral states after perturbation. Evidence requires specified perturbations and state variables; repeatable occupancy near a region or low trial variance is not enough by itself.



At L2, Stability supplies explicit quantifiers, time-support assumptions, local/global scope, and the hierarchy among Lyapunov, asymptotic, and exponential stability. It also forces analyses to state which perturbation, state space, metric, and coordinate convention define “nearby” and “rate.”




Which perturbations are experimentally realizable and scientifically relevant?
How should stability be assessed when only partial noisy observations are available?
When is a local stability statement adequate for a behavioral claim?





Teschl gives the inspected Lyapunov, asymptotic, and exponential fixed-point definitions and the warning that convergence alone need not imply stability (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.5).
Lyapunov-function, linearization, and eigenvalue criteria in later parts of Teschl are intentionally deferred from this Concept.

title: State Space
text:
A state space is the set of all state values admitted by a specified state description of a specified system.



A state description says what information is carried forward; a state space says which realized values of that description are possible or allowed. This distinction is necessary before asking how a system changes: evolution moves among admissible state values, not among alternative variable lists.
The state space also fixes the domain in which later claims are interpreted. It determines what counts as one state, which combinations of values are allowed, and which system boundary and resolution are being represented. Terman and Izhikevich give the standard formulation that a state space is the set of possible states, with each state represented as a point (Terman and Izhikevich 2008).



First choose a state description. For an idealized pendulum, that description might contain angle and angular velocity. Then imagine every admissible assignment of those two quantities. Each assignment is one state value, and the collection of all such values is the state space.
This collection is broader than the states observed in one experiment. A recording may visit only a small subset, and finite data contain only sampled measurements. Conversely, not every arbitrary combination of coordinate values need be admissible: physical constraints, logical constraints, or the declared model boundary may exclude some combinations.
A state space is therefore relative to:

the system boundary — which entities and influences are inside the system;
the state description — which future-relevant variables are retained;
the resolution and admissibility constraints — which distinctions and combinations the model treats as meaningful.

A coordinate convention is a separate representational choice. It assigns numerical coordinates to state values in the abstract state space. Different coordinate systems can represent the same underlying state information without changing which abstract states are admissible.



Let a state description specify the structure of a system’s state values and let the declared constraints determine which values are admissible. The state space may be written
\[
\mathcal{X} = \{x : x \text{ is an admissible state value under the specified description and constraints}\}.
\]
When state values are represented by \(n\) coordinates, one may write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\). The coordinate tuple is a numerical representation of a state value; it is not the abstract state value or state space by itself. Different coordinate systems may represent the same underlying state values, while admissibility constraints determine which represented values belong to \(\mathcal{X}\).
The definition requires a set of possible state values but does not require a particular equation of motion, distance, or visualization. No dimension need yet be specified or justified at L1. In Teschl’s abstract mathematical formulation, an evolution acts on a set denoted \(M\) (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.1); in LDG notation, that set is \(\mathcal{X}\) once its points have been assigned the role of admissible state values.




\(\mathcal{X}\): the state space.
\(x\in\mathcal{X}\): one admissible state value.
\(x(t)\in\mathcal{X}\): the state value assigned at time \(t\).
\(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\): a coordinate representation when the description uses \(n\) coordinates.

A matrix whose rows are recorded samples is not denoted \(\mathcal{X}\) here: it is a dataset drawn from, projected from, or otherwise related to the proposed state space.




State: distinguishes a state description, state value, and state vector.

Assumed background: elementary sets and vector notation.










Concept
Relationship to state space




State description
Specifies what variables or structure constitute a state. The state space contains the admissible values under that description.


State value
One member \(x\in\mathcal{X}\) of the state space. The space is not itself a single state.


State vector / coordinates
A numerical representation of one state value. Coordinate choices do not define the abstract state space and do not by themselves determine which values are admissible. Different coordinates may represent the same underlying state information.


Observation space or measurement range
Contains possible sensor outputs or measured values. It can coincide with the state space under an ideal direct measurement, but it is generally distinct when observations are partial, noisy, or indirect.


Dataset or data matrix
Contains finitely many recorded values. It samples or represents observed data; it is not automatically the set of all admissible states.


Trajectory
A time-parameterized admissible evolution through state values in the state space. The space contains possible states; a trajectory records one system evolution through them.


Parameter space
Contains alternative parameter values indexing models or evolution rules. Parameters and states have different modeling roles even when both are represented by vectors.


Latent space
A coordinate domain introduced for unobserved or inferred variables. It is a state space only if its values are assigned an adequate state role for the specified evolution.


Phase space
Often used as a synonym for state space in dynamical-systems contexts. Usage varies by field, so LDG requires the intended state description and admissible values to be stated rather than relying on the label alone.






Calling a set a state space does not by itself imply that:

every admissible state has been observed or can be observed;
recorded samples cover the space densely or without bias;
every coordinate is a direct measurement;
the space is identical to a data matrix, point cloud, or plotted projection;
all coordinate combinations are admissible;
the representation is unique, minimal, low-dimensional, or Euclidean;
a particular distance, geometry, or neighborhood relation has been justified;
a rule of evolution, trajectory, or causal mechanism has been identified; or
the model-defined space is the complete physical state space of the real system.




For the pendulum description
\[
x=(\text{angle},\;\text{angular velocity}),
\]
one state value is one particular pendulum condition specified by angle and angular velocity. The abstract state space is the set of all such conditions admitted by the chosen pendulum description and its physical assumptions.
Choosing radians rather than degrees, selecting an angular-velocity unit, or using another equivalent numerical encoding changes the coordinate representation, not the underlying set of admissible pendulum states.
A table containing 1,000 camera samples is not that state space. It is a finite collection of observations. Even if angle and angular velocity are estimated from every frame, the resulting 1,000 state estimates show only the values sampled during that recording, not all admissible pendulum states.



For \(D\) recorded neurons, population activity is often represented by \(D\) firing-rate coordinates; each time point is then a point in the corresponding population-coordinate domain (Cunningham and Yu 2014). The finite set of recorded population vectors is data, not automatically the full neural state space. Calling the coordinate domain a neural state space additionally commits the analysis to treating those population variables as a state description for a declared system and time scale.
Likewise, a pose-estimation matrix or collection of behavioral features is not automatically a behavioral state space. The proposed space must specify which feature combinations are admissible and why the features constitute state rather than partial observations. A lower-dimensional latent representation remains model- and criterion-dependent; its visualization alone does not establish a unique underlying state space.



LDG will repeatedly compare recorded variables, latent coordinates, and proposed dynamical descriptions. State-space language keeps three objects separate: the state description, the set of admissible state values, and the finite data used to study them. This separation is required before trajectories or initial conditions can be defined consistently and before later work can make defensible claims about latent structure.




What empirical evidence would show that a proposed state space excludes state values needed for prediction?
Which apparent constraints reflect the system and which reflect sampling or measurement limits?
When two coordinate systems represent the same future-relevant information, what makes one scientifically preferable?

These are model- and dataset-specific follow-ups, not reasons to enlarge the L1 definition.

Abstract set acted on by a dynamical system: (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.1).
Neural population-coordinate usage: (Cunningham and Yu 2014).

Separates the abstract set of admissible states from its coordinate representations.

title: Tangent Space
text:
The tangent space \(T_pM\) is the vector space of first-order directions available on a smooth manifold \(M\) at a point \(p\).



The tangent space is the local linear arena for velocities, derivatives, vector fields, and Riemannian inner products. It approximates first-order behavior at one point; it is not the manifold itself.



At a point on a sphere, the tangent plane contains the instantaneous directions in which a curve on the sphere can move. The sphere leaves that plane at second order.



Let \(M\) be a smooth \(n\)-manifold and \(p\in M\).


Consider smooth curves \(\gamma:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\to M\) with \(\gamma(0)=p\). Two curves are tangent-equivalent at \(p\) when, in one—and therefore every—chart \((U,x)\) containing \(p\),
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0}x(\gamma_1(t))
=
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0}x(\gamma_2(t)).
\]
A tangent vector is an equivalence class \([\gamma]\), and the tangent space \(T_pM\) is the set of such classes with vector-space operations induced in coordinates. Mrowka gives the equivalent chart-representative construction (Mrowka 2004, sec. 7.2).



Equivalently, a tangent vector at \(p\) is a linear map
\[
v:C^\infty_p(M)\to\mathbb R
\]
on germs of smooth functions satisfying the Leibniz rule
\[
v(fg)=f(p)v(g)+g(p)v(f).
\]
For a curve representative,
\[
v(f)
=
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0}f(\gamma(t)).
\]
The curve-velocity and derivation descriptions define canonically isomorphic tangent spaces (Lee 1997, ch. 2). This Concept states the equivalence but defers its proof.



A chart \(x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)\) supplies the coordinate basis
\[
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x^1}\right|_p,
\ldots,
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x^n}\right|_p,
\]
so every \(v\in T_pM\) has components
\[
v
=
v^i\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\right|_p.
\]
Thus \(\dim T_pM=n\). Under another chart \(y=(y^1,\ldots,y^n)\),
\[
v'^a
=
\frac{\partial y^a}{\partial x^i}(p)v^i,
\]
and
\[
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}\right|_p
=
\frac{\partial y^a}{\partial x^i}(p)
\left.\frac{\partial}{\partial y^a}\right|_p.
\]
The components change, while the intrinsic tangent vector does not.



For a smooth map \(f:M\to N\), the differential at \(p\) is the linear map
\[
df_p:T_pM\to T_{f(p)}N.
\]
Using curve representatives,
\[
df_p([\gamma])=[f\circ\gamma].
\]
Using derivations,
\[
(df_pv)(g)=v(g\circ f).
\]
In charts, the matrix of \(df_p\) is the Jacobian \([\partial f^a/\partial x^i]_p\) (Mrowka 2004, sec. 7.2).



If \(i:M\hookrightarrow\widetilde M\) is a smooth embedding, \(di_p\) identifies \(T_pM\) with a linear subspace of \(T_{i(p)}\widetilde M\). For an embedded manifold in \(\mathbb R^D\), this gives the familiar ambient tangent plane. This represented subspace depends on the embedding, whereas the abstract \(T_pM\) is intrinsic. An arbitrary ambient subspace fitted to data is not automatically the image of an intrinsic tangent space.



The tangent bundle is the disjoint union
\[
TM=\bigsqcup_{p\in M}T_pM
\]
with its compatible smooth bundle structure. A smooth vector field is a smooth section \(X:M\to TM\) satisfying \(X(p)\in T_pM\). Bundle construction proofs and connection theory are deferred.





\(T_pM\): tangent space at \(p\).
\(v\in T_pM\): tangent vector.
\([\gamma]\): equivalence class of curves through \(p\).
\(v(f)\): derivation of a smooth function germ.
\(\partial/\partial x^i|_p\): chart-induced tangent basis.
\(v^i\): tangent-vector components in a chart.
\(df_p:T_pM\to T_{f(p)}N\): differential/pushforward of a smooth map.
\(TM=\bigsqcup_{p\in M}T_pM\): tangent bundle.




Manifold supplies charts and smooth curves. Linear Subspace supplies vector-space language.










Concept
Distinction




Manifold
The nonlinear space of points; \(T_pM\) is one attached local vector space.


Ambient space
An embedding differential represents \(T_pM\) as a subspace of the ambient tangent space; the intrinsic tangent space is not defined by ambient coordinates alone.


Differential / Jacobian
\(df_p\) maps tangent vectors between manifolds. A coordinate Jacobian is its matrix representation, not the intrinsic map itself.


Tangent bundle
The smoothly organized union of all tangent spaces; it is not one vector space because fibers at different points are distinct.


Vector field
Assigns one tangent vector to each point, rather than describing one tangent space.


Local PCA plane
A statistical estimate that may approximate a tangent space under additional sampling and noise assumptions.






A tangent space does not imply global flatness, a canonical identification between different points, a unique ambient orientation, a metric or inner product, accurate estimation from sparse samples, validity far from \(p\), or that local linear dynamics extend globally.



For \(S^1\subset\mathbb R^2\) and \(p=(1,0)\),
\[
T_pS^1=\{(0,a):a\in\mathbb R\}.
\]
This vertical line captures instantaneous motion at \(p\) but not the whole circle.



Local tangent estimates can describe directions of neural or behavioral variation near a state. Their interpretation depends on neighborhood scale and should be compared with simpler local-linear null models.



At L2, Tangent Space connects intrinsic curve/derivation definitions, coordinate representations, differentials, embedded subspaces, vector fields, and later Riemannian geometry without treating local linearization as global structure.




How many samples are needed for reliable tangent estimation?
How should uncertainty in \(T_pM\) propagate to dynamics?
When do tangent estimates vary smoothly across conditions?





Mrowka provides the inspected chart-equivalence, coordinate-basis, differential-map, and tangent-bundle construction (Mrowka 2004, sec. 7.2).
Lee provides the inspected curve/derivation equivalence, embedded-submanifold tangent representation, and tangent-bundle context (Lee 1997, ch. 2).
Bundle proofs, connections, and statistical tangent-estimation algorithms are intentionally deferred.





Defines tangent vectors through curve velocities and charts.
Separates local tangent space, manifold, ambient space, and estimated local planes.
Includes an explicit circle example.
States intrinsic curve-equivalence and derivation definitions.
Types chart bases, component transformations, and \(\dim T_pM=\dim M\).
Defines the differential \(df_p\) intrinsically and in coordinates.
Separates intrinsic and embedded tangent spaces and arbitrary ambient subspaces.
Relates tangent bundles and vector fields while deferring bundle theory.
States empirical scale, sampling, noise, and manifold-assumption limits for tangent estimation.
Independent L2 scientific review completed with PASS under the recorded review decision.

title: Torus
text:
The two-dimensional torus \(T^2\) is the product \(S^1\times S^1\), equivalently a plane with two independent periodic directions.



The torus models systems with two circular variables, such as two phases or two periodic coordinates. Its intrinsic topology is not tied to the familiar doughnut-shaped embedding in \(\mathbb R^3\).



Take a square and identify its left edge with its right edge and its bottom edge with its top edge. Moving off one side returns from the opposite side.



With the product topology and product smooth structure,
\[
T^2=S^1\times S^1
\cong
\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2,
\]
where \(\mathbb Z^2\) acts by coordinatewise integer translations. Quotient coordinates \((t_1,t_2)\pmod{\mathbb Z^2}\) are measured in turns; radian coordinates satisfy \(\theta_i=2\pi t_i\).
It is a compact two-dimensional smooth manifold. The quotient-square, product-of-circles, and embedded doughnut are representations of the same standard topological type under suitable maps.




\(T^2\): two-torus.
\((\theta_1,\theta_2)\): two periodic coordinates.
\(\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2\): quotient representation.




Circle / S¹ supplies each periodic factor. Topology supplies product and quotient constructions.










Concept
Distinction




Doughnut surface
One embedding of a torus; the topology does not require that geometry.


Two-dimensional plane
Locally similar but globally lacks the torus’s periodic identifications.


Limit cycle
One periodic orbit has circle topology; a torus can support two independent phases or quasiperiodic motion.


Product space
The torus is a particular product of two circles.






A toroidal latent claim does not imply a doughnut-shaped point cloud, a flat metric, two identifiable biological oscillators, dense sampling, quasiperiodic dynamics, or a unique embedding.



Two independent clock phases \((\theta_1,\theta_2)\), each taken modulo \(2\pi\), define a point on \(T^2\). Equivalently, \((t_1,t_2)=(\theta_1/2\pi,\theta_2/2\pi)\) is taken modulo \(\mathbb Z^2\). Returning either phase by one full turn leaves the torus point unchanged.



Joint head-direction and rhythmic-phase variables, or two coupled periodic task variables, may motivate toroidal models. Such topology must be compared with simpler circular, planar, and disconnected alternatives.



Torus extends the topology branch from one periodic coordinate to product topology and prepares careful discussion of multi-phase latent structure.




What sampling is required to distinguish a torus from a curved sheet?
How robust are two-hole signatures to noise and missing states?
When does toroidal topology improve prediction?





Sutherland provides the inspected product and quotient topology constructions (Sutherland 2024).
Mrowka’s manifold notes provide product and torus context (Mrowka 2004).





Defines \(T^2\) as a product and quotient.
Separates intrinsic topology from a doughnut embedding.
States empirical and dynamical non-implications.
Independent bounded review completed; initial findings were corrected and focused re-review passed.

title: Vector Field
text:
In a Euclidean continuous-time setting, a vector field is a rule that assigns each admissible state an instantaneous change vector, encoding a rate and, when nonzero, a direction.



A state space specifies which state values are admissible, but not how they change. A vector field adds a local evolution rule: at each state, it gives the velocity that a compatible continuous-time trajectory would have there. This makes it possible to distinguish a rule defined across the state space from one realized trajectory or a finite collection of observations.
For an autonomous differential equation, Teschl treats \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) as a vector field and describes its solution curves as tangent to that field at every visited state (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2). The field is therefore local and instantaneous; finite-time evolution is a different object.



Picture an arrow attached to every admissible state. The arrow at state \(x\) answers a local question: “If the system is at \(x\) under this rule, in what direction and at what instantaneous rate is its state changing?”
One arrow is a vector. The assignment of arrows across the state space is the vector field. Following the arrows over time can produce a trajectory when the evolution is well-defined, but neither a single arrow nor a plotted collection of arrows is itself a trajectory or a complete finite-time evolution.
The arrow is also not a finite jump to the next state. It has rate units—state units per unit time—and describes change at an instant. Over a sufficiently short interval it may support a local approximation, but the system can encounter different arrows as its state changes.



For this Cycle’s core formulation, assume the state space \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open. This is a deliberate scope restriction. For a constrained admissible set, a Euclidean rule can instead be defined on an open neighborhood containing that set, but whether the resulting motion remains admissible requires additional conditions deferred below. On the declared open domain, an autonomous vector field is a map
\[
f:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n,
\qquad x\mapsto f(x),
\]
where \(f(x)\) is the instantaneous state-change vector assigned at \(x\). A differentiable trajectory \(x(t)\) is compatible with the field when
\[
\dot{x}(t)=f\bigl(x(t)\bigr)
\]
at the times under consideration. This equation states a local relation between the trajectory’s derivative and the field; it does not by itself guarantee that a trajectory exists uniquely or for all time.
The bare concept is the assignment \(x\mapsto f(x)\). Continuity, differentiability, local Lipschitz conditions, and other regularity assumptions are additional properties, not part of that bare assignment. Such assumptions become important when asking whether the field generates unique trajectories or a well-defined flow.


The stable First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System Math Object is the canonical location for the corresponding initial-value problem, regularity ladder, maximal-solution statements, and local-flow construction. Given an initial state \(x_0\) at reference time \(t_0\), it writes the field as the local rule in
\[
\dot{x}=f(x),
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
If the active assumptions give a unique finite-time evolution map \(\phi_\tau\) and the curve \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) is differentiable at \(\tau=0\), the vector field is its elapsed-time generator:
\[
f(x)
=
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}.
\]
This relation connects the instantaneous and finite-time descriptions without identifying them. The derivative is taken with respect to elapsed time along the evolution from \(x\); differentiable dependence on the initial state is a stronger property. Neither existence, uniqueness, global continuation, nor joint flow regularity follows from the bare assignment \(x\mapsto f(x)\). Those theorem-level conditions and derivations remain in the Math Object (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 2.6, 6.2).
When explicit time or an external input matters, a model may use
\[
\dot{x}=f(x,u,t).
\]
For each specified input value and time, \(x\mapsto f(x,u,t)\) is a state-dependent velocity assignment; equivalently, the model supplies a family of vector fields indexed by \(u\) and \(t\). The input is not thereby part of the internal state, and its future values may be required to determine later evolution. Åström and Murray use the corresponding state/input separation in continuous-time system descriptions (Åström and Murray 2021, sec. 3.2).
Constrained state spaces with boundaries require separate checks that the assigned change is compatible with admissibility. Boundary conditions, tangent-cone or viability conditions, and vector fields on manifold-valued state spaces are deferred beyond this bounded object. LDG does not import that machinery into the Cycle 1 Euclidean formulation.





\(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\): the open Euclidean state-space domain used in the core Cycle 1 formulation.
\(x\in\mathcal{X}\): one state value.
\(f\): the vector field, defined across its stated domain.
\(f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n\): the instantaneous change vector assigned at \(x\).
\(x(t)\): a state trajectory.
\(\dot{x}(t)\): the instantaneous derivative of the trajectory.
\(u\): an optional external input.
\(t\): time; explicit appearance in \(f(x,u,t)\) indicates time-dependent local rules.

The same letter \(f\) is often used for other kinds of maps. Its domain, codomain, and role must therefore be stated.




State Space: supplies the admissible states on which the field is defined.

Assumed background: elementary vectors and single-variable derivatives.
State and Trajectory are related concepts: the field takes a state value as input, while a compatible trajectory has derivative prescribed by the field.
The First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System is the formal companion for existence, uniqueness, continuation, and local-flow results. It is linked as a related object rather than used to replace the conceptual definition here.










Concept
Distinction from vector field




Vector
A vector is one magnitude-and-direction value. A vector field assigns such a vector to every state in its declared domain.


State
A state value \(x\) describes the system at one time. The field value \(f(x)\) describes the instantaneous change assigned at that state; it is not another state value.


Trajectory
A trajectory is one time-parameterized admissible evolution \(x(t)\). A vector field is the local rule defined across states; a compatible differentiable trajectory satisfies \(\dot{x}(t)=f(x(t))\).


Finite displacement
A displacement such as \(x(t+\Delta t)-x(t)\) compares two states over a finite interval. The field value is an instantaneous rate, not that displacement and not generally equal to it.


External input
An input \(u\) is an influence treated as outside the state. It may select or modify the assigned vector through \(f(x,u,t)\) but is not the vector field’s output or automatically a state variable.


Discrete-time update map
An update map sends a current state directly to a later state, for example \(x_{k+1}=F(x_k)\). A vector field assigns an instantaneous rate in continuous time. One formalism should not be silently substituted for the other.


Flow
A flow, where defined, maps initial states across finite elapsed times. The vector field supplies the local instantaneous rule from which such finite-time evolution may be generated.


Fitted velocity field
A fitted field is an estimate constructed from data under modeling and smoothing choices. It may approximate a proposed vector field, but estimation is not part of the definition.






Calling \(f\) a vector field does not by itself imply that:

observed trajectories uniquely determine \(f\) away from, or even along, the sampled states;
a fitted local velocity field is the true physical or biological mechanism;
time-varying data or arrows drawn on a plot establish vector-field structure;
finite differences are exact instantaneous derivatives;
every state in \(\mathcal{X}\) has been observed;
a compatible trajectory exists uniquely or indefinitely from every state;
the field is autonomous, smooth, linear, low-dimensional, or noise-free;
a continuous-time vector field is the natural description of a discrete-time system; or
knowing the local rule automatically supplies its full finite-time evolution.




For an idealized dimensionless pendulum, treat the angle \(\theta\) as an unwrapped real-valued coordinate in this Euclidean example and use the state
\[
x=(\theta,\omega),
\]
where \(\omega\) is angular velocity. On the resulting open coordinate domain \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^2\), consider
\[
f(\theta,\omega)=\bigl(\omega,-\sin\theta\bigr).
\]
At the state \((\theta,\omega)\), the first component says that angle changes instantaneously at rate \(\omega\); the second says that angular velocity changes instantaneously at rate \(-\sin\theta\). Teschl uses this pendulum field as an example of the autonomous vector-field viewpoint (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2).
The vector \(f(\theta,\omega)\) is one local rate at one state. The vector field is the entire assignment over admissible angle–velocity states. It does not directly give the finite displacement after one second, because the assigned vector generally changes as the pendulum state changes.



Using the population-coordinate convention reviewed by Cunningham and Yu, a proposed neural state can be represented by a vector of population activity at a time (Cunningham and Yu 2014). A neural vector-field model would assign an instantaneous activity-change vector to each admissible population state. The recorded population vectors and their finite differences are observations or estimates; they are not automatically the underlying field.
The same distinction applies to behavior. Local velocity estimates computed from position, pose, or other behavioral variables constitute a vector field only relative to an adequate state description and a continuous-time modeling assumption. Sparse sampling, omitted state variables, input changes, and measurement noise can make different fields consistent with the available trajectories.



Vector fields provide the local-rule layer connecting state-space descriptions to continuous-time dynamics. LDG needs this distinction to ask whether a proposed latent, neural, or behavioral evolution law is supported by data without confusing sampled trajectories, plotted arrows, and mechanism. The concept also prepares the local-versus-finite-time distinction needed for Flow while leaving estimation methods and formal existence theory to later work.




What observations are sufficient to constrain a vector field beyond the sampled trajectories?
How should LDG separate changes in the field from changes in external input or unmeasured state?
When is a continuous-time vector-field description preferable to a discrete-time update rule for sampled data?

These are later modeling and inference questions, not part of this bounded definition.

title: Vector Field
text: In a Euclidean continuous-time setting, a vector field is a rule that assigns each admissible state an instantaneous change vector, encoding a rate and, when nonzero, a direction.

title: Vector Field
text:
A state space specifies which state values are admissible, but not how they change. A vector field adds a local evolution rule: at each state, it gives the velocity that a compatible continuous-time trajectory would have there. This makes it possible to distinguish a rule defined across the state space from one realized trajectory or a finite collection of observations.
For an autonomous differential equation, Teschl treats \(\dot{x}=f(x)\) as a vector field and describes its solution curves as tangent to that field at every visited state (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2). The field is therefore local and instantaneous; finite-time evolution is a different object.

title: Vector Field
text:
Picture an arrow attached to every admissible state. The arrow at state \(x\) answers a local question: “If the system is at \(x\) under this rule, in what direction and at what instantaneous rate is its state changing?”
One arrow is a vector. The assignment of arrows across the state space is the vector field. Following the arrows over time can produce a trajectory when the evolution is well-defined, but neither a single arrow nor a plotted collection of arrows is itself a trajectory or a complete finite-time evolution.
The arrow is also not a finite jump to the next state. It has rate units—state units per unit time—and describes change at an instant. Over a sufficiently short interval it may support a local approximation, but the system can encounter different arrows as its state changes.

title: Vector Field
text:
For this Cycle’s core formulation, assume the state space \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open. This is a deliberate scope restriction. For a constrained admissible set, a Euclidean rule can instead be defined on an open neighborhood containing that set, but whether the resulting motion remains admissible requires additional conditions deferred below. On the declared open domain, an autonomous vector field is a map
\[
f:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n,
\qquad x\mapsto f(x),
\]
where \(f(x)\) is the instantaneous state-change vector assigned at \(x\). A differentiable trajectory \(x(t)\) is compatible with the field when
\[
\dot{x}(t)=f\bigl(x(t)\bigr)
\]
at the times under consideration. This equation states a local relation between the trajectory’s derivative and the field; it does not by itself guarantee that a trajectory exists uniquely or for all time.
The bare concept is the assignment \(x\mapsto f(x)\). Continuity, differentiability, local Lipschitz conditions, and other regularity assumptions are additional properties, not part of that bare assignment. Such assumptions become important when asking whether the field generates unique trajectories or a well-defined flow.


The stable First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System Math Object is the canonical location for the corresponding initial-value problem, regularity ladder, maximal-solution statements, and local-flow construction. Given an initial state \(x_0\) at reference time \(t_0\), it writes the field as the local rule in
\[
\dot{x}=f(x),
\qquad
x(t_0)=x_0.
\]
If the active assumptions give a unique finite-time evolution map \(\phi_\tau\) and the curve \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) is differentiable at \(\tau=0\), the vector field is its elapsed-time generator:
\[
f(x)
=
\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}.
\]
This relation connects the instantaneous and finite-time descriptions without identifying them. The derivative is taken with respect to elapsed time along the evolution from \(x\); differentiable dependence on the initial state is a stronger property. Neither existence, uniqueness, global continuation, nor joint flow regularity follows from the bare assignment \(x\mapsto f(x)\). Those theorem-level conditions and derivations remain in the Math Object (Teschl 2012, secs. 2.2, 2.6, 6.2).
When explicit time or an external input matters, a model may use
\[
\dot{x}=f(x,u,t).
\]
For each specified input value and time, \(x\mapsto f(x,u,t)\) is a state-dependent velocity assignment; equivalently, the model supplies a family of vector fields indexed by \(u\) and \(t\). The input is not thereby part of the internal state, and its future values may be required to determine later evolution. Åström and Murray use the corresponding state/input separation in continuous-time system descriptions (Åström and Murray 2021, sec. 3.2).
Constrained state spaces with boundaries require separate checks that the assigned change is compatible with admissibility. Boundary conditions, tangent-cone or viability conditions, and vector fields on manifold-valued state spaces are deferred beyond this bounded object. LDG does not import that machinery into the Cycle 1 Euclidean formulation.

title: Vector Field
text:
\(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\): the open Euclidean state-space domain used in the core Cycle 1 formulation.
\(x\in\mathcal{X}\): one state value.
\(f\): the vector field, defined across its stated domain.
\(f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n\): the instantaneous change vector assigned at \(x\).
\(x(t)\): a state trajectory.
\(\dot{x}(t)\): the instantaneous derivative of the trajectory.
\(u\): an optional external input.
\(t\): time; explicit appearance in \(f(x,u,t)\) indicates time-dependent local rules.

The same letter \(f\) is often used for other kinds of maps. Its domain, codomain, and role must therefore be stated.

title: Vector Field
text:
State Space: supplies the admissible states on which the field is defined.

Assumed background: elementary vectors and single-variable derivatives.
State and Trajectory are related concepts: the field takes a state value as input, while a compatible trajectory has derivative prescribed by the field.
The First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System is the formal companion for existence, uniqueness, continuation, and local-flow results. It is linked as a related object rather than used to replace the conceptual definition here.

title: Vector Field
text:
Concept
Distinction from vector field




Vector
A vector is one magnitude-and-direction value. A vector field assigns such a vector to every state in its declared domain.


State
A state value \(x\) describes the system at one time. The field value \(f(x)\) describes the instantaneous change assigned at that state; it is not another state value.


Trajectory
A trajectory is one time-parameterized admissible evolution \(x(t)\). A vector field is the local rule defined across states; a compatible differentiable trajectory satisfies \(\dot{x}(t)=f(x(t))\).


Finite displacement
A displacement such as \(x(t+\Delta t)-x(t)\) compares two states over a finite interval. The field value is an instantaneous rate, not that displacement and not generally equal to it.


External input
An input \(u\) is an influence treated as outside the state. It may select or modify the assigned vector through \(f(x,u,t)\) but is not the vector field’s output or automatically a state variable.


Discrete-time update map
An update map sends a current state directly to a later state, for example \(x_{k+1}=F(x_k)\). A vector field assigns an instantaneous rate in continuous time. One formalism should not be silently substituted for the other.


Flow
A flow, where defined, maps initial states across finite elapsed times. The vector field supplies the local instantaneous rule from which such finite-time evolution may be generated.


Fitted velocity field
A fitted field is an estimate constructed from data under modeling and smoothing choices. It may approximate a proposed vector field, but estimation is not part of the definition.

title: Vector Field
Vector Field
text:
For an idealized dimensionless pendulum, treat the angle \(\theta\) as an unwrapped real-valued coordinate in this Euclidean example and use the state
\[
x=(\theta,\omega),
\]
where \(\omega\) is angular velocity. On the resulting open coordinate domain \(\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^2\), consider
\[
f(\theta,\omega)=\bigl(\omega,-\sin\theta\bigr).
\]
At the state \((\theta,\omega)\), the first component says that angle changes instantaneously at rate \(\omega\); the second says that angular velocity changes instantaneously at rate \(-\sin\theta\). Teschl uses this pendulum field as an example of the autonomous vector-field viewpoint (Teschl 2012, sec. 6.2).
The vector \(f(\theta,\omega)\) is one local rate at one state. The vector field is the entire assignment over admissible angle–velocity states. It does not directly give the finite displacement after one second, because the assigned vector generally changes as the pendulum state changes.

title: Vector Field
text:
Using the population-coordinate convention reviewed by Cunningham and Yu, a proposed neural state can be represented by a vector of population activity at a time (Cunningham and Yu 2014). A neural vector-field model would assign an instantaneous activity-change vector to each admissible population state. The recorded population vectors and their finite differences are observations or estimates; they are not automatically the underlying field.
The same distinction applies to behavior. Local velocity estimates computed from position, pose, or other behavioral variables constitute a vector field only relative to an adequate state description and a continuous-time modeling assumption. Sparse sampling, omitted state variables, input changes, and measurement noise can make different fields consistent with the available trajectories.

title: Vector Field
text: Vector fields provide the local-rule layer connecting state-space descriptions to continuous-time dynamics. LDG needs this distinction to ask whether a proposed latent, neural, or behavioral evolution law is supported by data without confusing sampled trajectories, plotted arrows, and mechanism. The concept also prepares the local-versus-finite-time distinction needed for Flow while leaving estimation methods and formal existence theory to later work.

title: 吸引子
text:
吸引子是不变的动力学集合，周围吸引盆中的状态在指定前向演化下接近它，任何额外的最小性或传递性约定都被显式陈述。



吸引子组织跨许多初始条件的长时间行为。它们可以是不动点、周期轨道或更复杂的不变集。该术语也被不一致地使用，因此 LDG 必须指定采用的约定，而不是把任何常被访问的区域都标记为吸引子。



吸引子不只是轨迹经常出现的场所。它是动力学保持的集合，且一簇非平凡的邻近初始状态向它演化。



设 \((\mathcal X,d)\) 是度量状态空间，\(I_x\) 是穿过 \(x\) 的受支持经过时间区间。对非空闭集 \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathcal X\)，定义其前向盆（Teschl 术语中的前向稳定集）为
\[
B^+(\Lambda)
=
\left\{
x\in\mathcal X:
[0,\infty)\subseteq I_x
\text{ and }
\lim_{t\to\infty}d(\phi_t(x),\Lambda)=0
\right\},
\]
其中
\[
d(x,\Lambda)=\inf_{z\in\Lambda}d(x,z).
\]
支持条件防止把有限时间终止误认为长时间吸引。收敛是对集合的：它不要求收敛到单点、单一相位或指定速率。
当 \(\Lambda\) 不变且 \(B^+(\Lambda)\) 包含 \(\Lambda\) 的一个邻域时，集合 \(\Lambda\) 是吸引的。除非 \(B^+(\Lambda)\) 等于声明的完整前向域，否则这是局部吸引。


LDG 在本对象中遵循 Teschl 的约定： 在完整的双侧流下，吸引子是非空闭不变吸引集，且是拓扑传递的。拓扑传递指对任何非空相对开集 \(U,V\subseteq\Lambda\)，存在 \(t\in\mathbb R\) 使得
\[
\phi_t(U)\cap V\ne\varnothing.
\]
这一附加条件排除分解为动力学上独立不变片的吸引超集。这是一个既有约定，不是整个动力学中使用的唯一定义。前向半流、随机系统、随机吸引子与输入驱动系统需要单独声明的变体 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 8.1)。



陷阱区域 \(E\) 是具有紧闭包的开连通集，使得
\[
\phi_t(\overline E)\subset E,
\qquad t>0.
\]
在 Teschl 的完整流假设下，
\[
\Lambda_E
=
\omega^+(E)
=
\bigcap_{t\ge0}\phi_t(\overline E)
\]
是非空紧连通不变吸引集 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 8.1)。这是吸引集的充分构造，不是必要刻画，其本身也不是拓扑传递性的证明。omega 极限与陷阱区域证明仍被推迟。



吸引与李雅普诺夫稳定性是不同谓词。点或集可以在不吸引邻域的情况下李雅普诺夫稳定，向集合收敛本身也不确立李雅普诺夫稳定性。当两个性质都被要求时，必须使用 Stability 定义分别检查。





\(\Lambda\)：候选不变集。
\(d(x,\Lambda)=\inf_{z\in\Lambda}d(x,z)\)：点到集合的距离。
\(I_x\)：穿过 \(x\) 的受支持经过时间区间。
\(B^+(\Lambda)\) 或 \(W^+(\Lambda)\)：\(\Lambda\) 的前向盆/稳定集。
\(E\)：具有紧闭包的陷阱区域。
\(\omega^+(E)\)：\(E\) 的前向 omega 极限集。
\(\phi_t\)：前向演化；采用的传递性约定需要完整双侧流。
\(t\to\infty\)：范围内的长时间极限。




Stability 提供扰动与接近区分。Flow 提供跨初始状态的有限时间演化与受支持域。Metric 提供到集合距离的构造。










概念
区别




吸引集
具有带邻域盆的不变集。在采用约定下，只有拓扑传递性也被确立后它才成为吸引子。


李雅普诺夫稳定对象
稳定性指邻近轨迹保持接近；吸引关乎向集合收敛。任一性质都可能需要单独验证。


极限环
吸引的周期轨道可以是吸引子，但吸引子不必是周期的。


吸引盆
吸引盆是接近吸引子的初始状态集合，而非吸引子本身。


常被访问的区域
高占用率可能来自采样、噪声、缓慢运动或外部输入，而无不变性、邻域盆、前向支持或传递性。


陷阱区域极限集
紧连通吸引集的充分构造；它不自动传递，因此在采用约定下不自动是吸引子。






吸引子并不蕴含：

每个初始状态都接近它；
唯一吸引子或吸引盆；
不动点而非周期或更复杂集合；
对参数变化或随机强迫的鲁棒性；
经验密度峰是吸引子；
有限轨迹识别完整吸引盆；
一条接近 \(\Lambda\) 的轨迹确立来自邻域的吸引；
回归、缓慢运动、聚类、解码、低重构误差或密度峰确立不变性或传递性；
吸引蕴含李雅普诺夫稳定性或对扰动的鲁棒性；或
吸引解释产生数据的生物机制。




对 \(\dot x=-x\)，\(\Lambda=\{0\}\) 不变且
\[
x(t)=x_0e^{-t}\longrightarrow0
\]
对每个 \(x_0\in\mathbb R\) 成立。因此 \(B^+(\Lambda)=\mathbb R\)，且该单点集拓扑传递，所以在采用约定下它是点吸引子。
相反，对 \(\dot x=0\)，每个单点集都李雅普诺夫稳定，但 \(\{p\}\) 的盆只有 \(\{p\}\)，不包含 \(\mathbb R\) 中的邻域；它不是吸引子。吸引的周期轨道提供非点示例，但排斥的或仅仅孤立的周期轨道不提供。



吸引子语言被用于持续活动、类别决策、记忆与重复出现的群体状态。站得住脚的主张要求不变模型集与来自受扰初始状态吸引的证据，而不仅仅是聚类、解码或重复访问。



在 L2 阶段，吸引子提供显式盆、支持条件、到集合距离收敛、所选传递性约定与陷阱区域构造。它保留 LDG 对把可视化、占用率、回归或单条收敛迹线当作动力学证据的禁止。




对带噪或输入驱动模型，哪种吸引子约定合适？
如何从有限干预与部分观测推断吸引盆？
吸引子模型应击败哪些基线解释？





Teschl 发展前向稳定集/盆、吸引集、陷阱区域与采用的传递吸引子约定 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 8.1)。
Teschl 的陷阱区域与 omega 极限证明作为源语境被引用，但不在本概念中复现。





要求不变性与来自盆的吸引。
标记吸引子约定的差异。
区分吸引子、盆、不动点、极限环与占用率。
陈述经验非蕴含。
用前向完整性到集合距离收敛类型化盆。
采用并标记吸引加传递约定。
区分吸引集、陷阱区域极限集与传递吸引子。
把吸引与李雅普诺夫稳定性和经验占用率分开。

title: 吸引子
text:
对 \(\dot x=-x\)，\(\Lambda=\{0\}\) 不变且
\[
x(t)=x_0e^{-t}\longrightarrow0
\]
对每个 \(x_0\in\mathbb R\) 成立。因此 \(B^+(\Lambda)=\mathbb R\)，且该单点集拓扑传递，所以在采用约定下它是点吸引子。
相反，对 \(\dot x=0\)，每个单点集都李雅普诺夫稳定，但 \(\{p\}\) 的盆只有 \(\{p\}\)，不包含 \(\mathbb R\) 中的邻域；它不是吸引子。吸引的周期轨道提供非点示例，但排斥的或仅仅孤立的周期轨道不提供。

title: 吸引子
text: 吸引子语言被用于持续活动、类别决策、记忆与重复出现的群体状态。站得住脚的主张要求不变模型集与来自受扰初始状态吸引的证据，而不仅仅是聚类、解码或重复访问。

title: 卷积
text:
卷积通过求和或积分时滞加权贡献，把信号与移位核组合起来产生输出。



卷积是线性时不变滤波器的规范输入输出运算。它提供固定核基线，潜状态动力学可以与它比较。



在每个输出时间，把核与输入历史对齐，乘以重叠值并相加。核决定哪些时滞重要以及以什么符号。



对标量函数 \(k,u:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\)，连续卷积是
\[
(k*u)(t)
=
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}k(\tau)u(t-\tau)\,d\tau,
\]
在积分存在的时刻成立。常见充分条件是 \(k\in L^1(\mathbb R)\) 且 \(u\) 有界；其他 \(L^p\) 条件也可能并必须被声明。紧支撑只有在配合充分局部可积性或有界性时才有用；支撑本身不保证积分存在。
对序列 \(k=(k_m)\) 与 \(u=(u_m)\)，
\[
(k*u)_n
=
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}k_m u_{n-m},
\]
当级数收敛时成立。一个序列的绝对可和性配合另一个的有界性是一种充分条件；有限支撑序列给出有限和。


对标量函数或序列，当所有所需积分/求和存在且重排被论证时，
\[
k*u=u*k,
\]
\[
(k_1*k_2)*u=k_1*(k_2*u),
\]
且卷积对每个自变量分配且线性。这些恒等式要求兼容域与收敛条件。矩阵乘法不可交换，因此类似矩阵值运算必须保持顺序。



对输入 \(u(t)\in\mathbb R^m\)、输出 \(y(t)\in\mathbb R^q\) 与核 \(H(\tau)\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\)，
\[
y(t)
=
\int H(\tau)u(t-\tau)\,d\tau
\]
在维数上良类型化。每个输出通道是输入通道与对应标量核条目的卷积之和。表达式 \(u*H\) 一般不是可互换的交换形式，因为向量/矩阵乘法顺序与维数重要。



对在 \(t_0\) 初始化、具有零初始状态且无直接前馈的因果 LTI 系统，输出具有零状态响应
\[
y_{\mathrm{zs}}(t)
=
\int_{t_0}^{t}H(t-s)u(s)\,ds
=
\int_{0}^{t-t_0}H(\tau)u(t-\tau)\,d\tau.
\]
因果性由 \(\tau<0\) 时 \(H(\tau)=0\) 表示。完整状态空间输出还可以包含初始条件响应与直接前馈：
\[
y(t)
=
Ce^{A(t-t_0)}x(t_0)
+
\int_{t_0}^{t}Ce^{A(t-s)}Bu(s)\,ds
+
Du(t).
\]
因此对 \(\tau>0\)，\(H(\tau)=Ce^{A\tau}B\) 给出普通零状态核。项 \(Du(t)\) 必须单独保留或由广义脉冲贡献 \(D\delta(\tau)\) 表示；它不是普通函数值时滞核 (Åström 和 Murray 2021年, sec. 6.3)。









注记已确立的数学 / 计算背景



在一种常见约定下，互相关是
\[
(r_{ku})(t)=\int \overline{k(\tau)}u(\tau+t)\,d\tau,
\]
因此它比较移位对齐，而非应用与卷积相同的反转约定。约定各异，尤其对复信号，且必须被陈述。
有限记录数组需要边界选择，如零填充、周期延拓、反射、截断或只报告有效重叠。由离散傅里叶变换产生的循环卷积与线性卷积不同，除非相应选择填充与索引。FFT 乘法是在声明的变换/边界约定下卷积的实现，不是卷积的定义。







\(k\)：标量核或脉冲响应。
\(H(\tau)\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\)：矩阵值核。
\(u(t)\in\mathbb R^m\)：输入信号。
\(y(t)\in\mathbb R^q\)：卷积输出。
\(y_{\mathrm{zs}}\)：零状态响应。
\(\tau\) 或 \(m\)：时滞变量。




Kernel 定义依赖时滞的加权函数。










概念
区别




相关
在声明的共轭/反转约定下比较移位对齐；不自动与卷积相同。


循环卷积
使用周期索引，如未填充 DFT 实现。线性卷积需要合适填充或其他边界约定。


FFT 乘法
变换与边界假设下的计算方法，不是数学定义。


滤波
更宽运算；LTI 滤波由卷积表示。


核
加权函数；卷积是使用它的运算。


状态空间响应
除零状态卷积项外还可能包含初始状态响应与直接前馈。


平滑
特定核的可能效果之一。卷积核也可以微分、延迟、振荡或放大。






卷积并不蕴含因果性、有限记忆、可逆性、已知核、平滑、稳定动力学、特定边界约定、线性生物机制，或所有时间依赖都由固定滤波器捕获。当相关求和/积分发散或维数不兼容时，代数恒等式不适用。



使用离散核 \(k=(1/2,1/2)\)，
\[
y_n=\tfrac12u_n+\tfrac12u_{n-1},
\]
因此输出平均当前与前一输入。这种平滑丢失一些快速变化信息。



卷积出现在时间感受野、传感器响应、平滑与血流动力学模型中。卷积模型的预测成功并不确立隐藏递归动力学。



在 L2 阶段，卷积为 LDG 提供固定核替代的显式存在性、维数、代数、因果、初始条件与直接前馈边界，然后才进入反卷积或更复杂的潜时序模型。

title: 反卷积
text:
反卷积是从被建模为卷积的观测中估计未知输入、源或核的逆问题，通常在有噪声与信息不完整的情况下进行。



卷积可以平滑或抑制信号的分量。恢复该滤波之前的内容常常不稳定：小的观测误差可以对朴素逆产生大的变化。



如果传感器用已知响应核模糊一个尖锐事件，反卷积尝试推断可能产生模糊测量的那个事件。一旦有噪声，多个源可能几乎同样好地拟合。



设 \(\mathcal U\) 是源空间，\(\mathcal K\) 是核空间，\(\mathcal Y\) 是观测空间。对固定核 \(k\)，定义卷积算子
\[
K_k:\mathcal U\to\mathcal Y,
\qquad
K_k u=k*u.
\]
观测数据遵循诸如
\[
y=K_k u+v,
\]
的前向模型，其中 \(v\) 是声明观测律下的观测噪声。已知核反卷积在 \(k\) 固定时估计 \(u\)。盲反卷积同时估计 \(u\) 与 \(k\)，因此具有额外的缩放、移位、边界与分解歧义。没有限制这些等价的约束，盲恢复不可辨识。


如果 \(K_k u_1=K_k u_2\)，则数据无法区分 \(u_1\) 与 \(u_2\)。等价地，它们的差位于零空间，
\[
u_1-u_2\in\ker K_k.
\]
即使零空间平凡，小奇异值或几乎被抑制的频率分量也会使逆病态：\(y\) 的小扰动对朴素恢复源产生大的变化。单射性、稳定求逆与数值条件数是独立性质。



在卷积变为乘法的变换与边界条件下，
\[
\widehat y(\omega)
=
\widehat k(\omega)\widehat u(\omega)
+
\widehat v(\omega).
\]
形式逆
\[
\widehat u(\omega)
=
\frac{\widehat y(\omega)}{\widehat k(\omega)}
\]
只在 \(\widehat k(\omega)\ne0\) 处有定义。如果 \(|\widehat k(\omega)|\) 小，噪声项被 \(1/|\widehat k(\omega)|\) 放大。零点在所述模型下抹去这些分量。有限窗口、采样、混叠、填充与循环对线性卷积进一步改变所实现的算子，因此变换除法不是普遍精确逆。



常见正则化估计量是
\[
\widehat u_\lambda
\in
\arg\min_{u\in\mathcal U}
\left\{
\mathcal D(K_k u,y)
+
\lambda\mathcal R(u)
\right\},
\]
其中 \(\mathcal D\) 是数据拟合或负对数似然项，\(\mathcal R\) 编码平滑性、稀疏性、非负性或有界变差等假设。正则化可以稳定求逆，但引入偏向首选解类的偏差。不同惩罚或先验可以选择对数据拟合相似的不同源。
概率性表述组合观测似然与先验，
\[
p(u\mid y,k)
\propto
p(y\mid K_k u)\,p(u).
\]
后验或 MAP 估计以这些选择为条件；它不是无假设恢复。
对盲反卷积可以优化 \((u,k)\)，
\[
\min_{u,k}
\mathcal D(K_k u,y)
+
\lambda_u\mathcal R_u(u)
+
\lambda_k\mathcal R_k(k),
\]
但必须声明缩放与移位约定、核归一化/支撑、正性及其他可辨识性约束。



小的前向残差 \(\|K_k\widehat u-y\|\) 检查与观测的一致性，但不证明源恢复。在具有已知真值的玩具模型中，评估应分别报告源误差、事件/支撑恢复、时间误差、核误差（当被估计时）以及对噪声、采样、边界与正则化的敏感性。没有真值时，留出前向预测、校准、干预或多个观测通道只提供间接证据，不能确立唯一源。
Richardson 的经核查论文提供主卷积图像恢复示例，展示对噪声与边界的敏感性，并描述无一般收敛证明的迭代近似 (Richardson 1972年)。上述一般逆算子与正则化框架是已确立的逆问题背景，不只归因于该算法。

\(K_k:\mathcal U\to\mathcal Y\)：核 \(k\) 的卷积前向算子。

\(\lambda\)：正则化强度。

概念
区别

反卷积并不蕴含精确恢复、唯一或稳定逆、正确的已知核、可辨识盲因子、信号与结构噪声的分离、无偏正则化，或从测量迹线恢复生物原因。低前向残差可以与大的源误差共存。



设离散核为 \(k=(1/2,1/2)\)，因此
\[
y_n=\frac{u_n+u_{n-1}}{2}+v_n.
\]

示例包括从钙荧光估计神经事件，或从血流动力学响应估计潜神经活动。恢复质量取决于核有效性、采样、噪声与先验假设。

title: 反卷积
text: 反卷积是从被建模为卷积的观测中估计未知输入、源或核的逆问题，通常在有噪声与信息不完整的情况下进行。

title: 反卷积
text: 卷积可以平滑或抑制信号的分量。恢复该滤波之前的内容常常不稳定：小的观测误差可以对朴素逆产生大的变化。

title: 反卷积
text: 如果传感器用已知响应核模糊一个尖锐事件，反卷积尝试推断可能产生模糊测量的那个事件。一旦有噪声，多个源可能几乎同样好地拟合。

title: 反卷积
text:
设 \(\mathcal U\) 是源空间，\(\mathcal K\) 是核空间，\(\mathcal Y\) 是观测空间。对固定核 \(k\)，定义卷积算子
\[
K_k:\mathcal U\to\mathcal Y,
\qquad
K_k u=k*u.
\]
观测数据遵循诸如
\[
y=K_k u+v,
\]
的前向模型，其中 \(v\) 是声明观测律下的观测噪声。已知核反卷积在 \(k\) 固定时估计 \(u\)。盲反卷积同时估计 \(u\) 与 \(k\)，因此具有额外的缩放、移位、边界与分解歧义。没有限制这些等价的约束，盲恢复不可辨识。


如果 \(K_k u_1=K_k u_2\)，则数据无法区分 \(u_1\) 与 \(u_2\)。等价地，它们的差位于零空间，
\[
u_1-u_2\in\ker K_k.
\]
即使零空间平凡，小奇异值或几乎被抑制的频率分量也会使逆病态：\(y\) 的小扰动对朴素恢复源产生大的变化。单射性、稳定求逆与数值条件数是独立性质。



在卷积变为乘法的变换与边界条件下，
\[
\widehat y(\omega)
=
\widehat k(\omega)\widehat u(\omega)
+
\widehat v(\omega).
\]
形式逆
\[
\widehat u(\omega)
=
\frac{\widehat y(\omega)}{\widehat k(\omega)}
\]
只在 \(\widehat k(\omega)\ne0\) 处有定义。如果 \(|\widehat k(\omega)|\) 小，噪声项被 \(1/|\widehat k(\omega)|\) 放大。零点在所述模型下抹去这些分量。有限窗口、采样、混叠、填充与循环对线性卷积进一步改变所实现的算子，因此变换除法不是普遍精确逆。



常见正则化估计量是
\[
\widehat u_\lambda
\in
\arg\min_{u\in\mathcal U}
\left\{
\mathcal D(K_k u,y)
+
\lambda\mathcal R(u)
\right\},
\]
其中 \(\mathcal D\) 是数据拟合或负对数似然项，\(\mathcal R\) 编码平滑性、稀疏性、非负性或有界变差等假设。正则化可以稳定求逆，但引入偏向首选解类的偏差。不同惩罚或先验可以选择对数据拟合相似的不同源。
概率性表述组合观测似然与先验，
\[
p(u\mid y,k)
\propto
p(y\mid K_k u)\,p(u).
\]
后验或 MAP 估计以这些选择为条件；它不是无假设恢复。
对盲反卷积可以优化 \((u,k)\)，
\[
\min_{u,k}
\mathcal D(K_k u,y)
+
\lambda_u\mathcal R_u(u)
+
\lambda_k\mathcal R_k(k),
\]
但必须声明缩放与移位约定、核归一化/支撑、正性及其他可辨识性约束。



小的前向残差 \(\|K_k\widehat u-y\|\) 检查与观测的一致性，但不证明源恢复。在具有已知真值的玩具模型中，评估应分别报告源误差、事件/支撑恢复、时间误差、核误差（当被估计时）以及对噪声、采样、边界与正则化的敏感性。没有真值时，留出前向预测、校准、干预或多个观测通道只提供间接证据，不能确立唯一源。
Richardson 的经核查论文提供主卷积图像恢复示例，展示对噪声与边界的敏感性，并描述无一般收敛证明的迭代近似 (Richardson 1972年)。上述一般逆算子与正则化框架是已确立的逆问题背景，不只归因于该算法。

title: 嵌入
text:
嵌入是把一个空间表示在另一个空间内部的单射映射，其保结构程度足够强，使得原始对象可以从其像恢复。



嵌入语言把对象的忠实表示与可能合并不同点或扭曲相关结构的投影或可视化区分开。



圆可以放在平面中而不自我识别点。把同一圆有重叠地映射到直线上则不能忠实地嵌入它。



在拓扑层面，当映射 \(e:X\to Y\) 单射且给出 \(X\) 与其带子空间拓扑的像 \(e(X)\) 之间的同胚时，它是嵌入。光滑嵌入增加光滑性与单射导数。
本 L1 对象只使用表示原则；完整拓扑与微分条件属于后续对象。Whitney 的经典工作为可微流形确立广泛的光滑嵌入结果 (Whitney 1936年)。




\(X\)：源空间。
\(Y\)：外围目标空间。
\(e:X\hookrightarrow Y\)：嵌入。
\(e(X)\)：嵌入像。




State Space 提供其状态可被表示的源对象。Ambient Dimension 提供目标空间坐标数目。
假定背景： 函数、单射性与初等连续性。






概念
区别




投影
可能合并不同点，且不必保留源结构。


降维
算法目标；其输出不自动是数学嵌入。


特征映射
到特征的任何映射；可能缺少单射性或结构保持。


流形
可以被嵌入的一类空间；嵌入不证明数据构成流形。






嵌入并不蕴含等距、所选度量下的低畸变、唯一坐标、因果或机制意义、流形源，或从有限带噪样本的成功恢复。



映射
\[
e(\theta)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)
\]
当 \(\theta\) 被理解为模 \(2\pi\) 时，把抽象圆表示在 \(\mathbb R^2\) 中。坐标像具有外围维数二，但只有一个本征圆自由度。



学习得到的低维坐标常被称为嵌入。LDG 要求说明「嵌入」只是算法标签，还是受支持的单射保结构主张。



嵌入为精确流形与拓扑语言做准备，同时防止非线性可视化被单独当作证据。

title: 流
text:
流是有限时间演化族，在良定义处把其定义域中的每个初始状态映射到在同一条共享自治连续时间规则下经过一段时间后到达的状态。



向量场给出局部瞬时规则，流描述其跨可能初始状态、在有限时间上的累积效应。在流中固定一个初始状态得到一条轨迹；考虑所有受支持的初始状态得到由同一动力学生成的一致轨迹族。
这一区分防止把观测曲线集合误认为流。流不只是轨迹数据集：其时间演化映射必须一致地作用于状态，并在相继时间区间上复合。Teschl 通过把自治微分方程的积分曲线收集到单一映射中来定义该方程的流 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 6.2)。
稳定的 First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System 数学对象是论证此类映射的存在性、唯一性、极大延拓与正则性结果的规范位置。本概念只保留解读有限时间演化所需的记号与区分，而不重复那些定理级推导。



设想向量场是附着在每个状态上的箭头。流回答有限时间问题：「从这个状态出发，共享规则在经过时间 \(\tau\) 后把系统带到哪里？」
有两种有用的方式固定流的一部分：

固定初始状态 \(x_0\)：变化经过时间 \(\tau\) 描出一条轨迹。
固定经过时间 \(\tau\)：映射 \(\phi_\tau\) 把每个受支持的初始状态移到该时长后的状态。

流是这些有限时间映射的一致集合，而不是任何无关的前后对集合。



考虑自治欧氏系统
\[
\dot{x}=f(x),\qquad x\in\mathcal{X}.
\]
假设有效假设为每个受支持的初始状态提供唯一极大解。对 \(x\in\mathcal{X}\)，设 \(I_x\) 是穿过 \(x\) 的解包含 \(0\) 的极大经过时间区间，并定义受支持域
\[
W
=
\{(\tau,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{X}:\tau\in I_x\}.
\]
联合有限时间演化映射是
\[
\Phi:W\rightarrow\mathcal{X},
\qquad
\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x),
\]
其中 \(\phi_\tau(x)\) 是从 \(x\) 经过时间 \(\tau\) 后到达的状态。对固定 \(\tau\)，相应状态映射具有类型化定义域
\[
\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)
=
\{x\in\mathcal{X}:(\tau,x)\in W\}.
\]
受支持集合不必是全部 \(\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{X}\)，\(\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)\) 也不必等于 \(\mathcal{X}\)。演化族满足
\[
\phi_0(x)=x,
\]
且复合律只在所需演化受支持处成立。显式地，如果 \(s\in I_x\) 且 \(\tau\in I_{\phi_s(x)}\)，则 \(s+\tau\in I_x\) 且
\[
\phi_{\tau+s}(x)=\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_s(x)\bigr).
\]
第一个关系说明零经过时间使状态不变。第二个说明先演化 \(s\) 再演化 \(\tau\) 与一次演化组合经过时间一致。这不是每个映射都定义在所有状态或所有经过时间上的声明 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 6.2)。
局部存在性与唯一性支持这种单值局部有限时间演化。在更强的条件 \(f\in C^1\) 下，稳定数学对象陈述 \(W\) 是开的，且 \(\Phi\) 对经过时间与初始状态联合 \(C^1\)；在采用的 LDG 约定下，这个联合正则映射就是生成的局部流。正则性定理及其推导保留在数学对象中。
对初始条件 \(x(t_0)=x_0\)，关联轨迹可以写作
\[
x(t)=\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)
\]
当 \(t-t_0\in I_{x_0}\)，等价地当 \((t-t_0,x_0)\in W\)。这里 \(t\) 是绝对时钟时间，而 \(\tau=t-t_0\) 是自初始条件起算的经过时间。
当有效的 ODE 假设使每条曲线 \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x)\) 对经过时间可微时，它满足
\[
\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)
=
f\bigl(\phi_\tau(x)\bigr),
\]
且其在零点的导数恢复向量场：
\[
f(x)=\left.\frac{d}{d\tau}\phi_\tau(x)\right|_{\tau=0}.
\]
该导数是沿一条轨迹对经过时间求取。它本身不断言对初始状态 \(x\) 的可微性；联合初始状态正则性是上面更强的局部流结论。这些关系表达局部对有限时间的区分，不是存在性或唯一性证明。
对双侧光滑局部流，反向经过时间提供局部逆：\(\phi_{-\tau}\) 在相应受支持域上逆转 \(\phi_\tau\)。这并不使 \(\phi_\tau\) 对每个 \(\tau\) 成为全局定义的满射 \(\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{X}\) (Teschl 2012年, sec. 6.2)。
单参数记号 \(\phi_\tau\) 对自治动力学最自然。限制在非负经过时间的半流、显式时间相关系统与输入驱动演化都在这个有界 L2 概念之外，而不是被静默地当作同一结构。




\(\mathcal{X}\)：状态空间。
\(f\)：自治向量场或局部瞬时规则。
\(x_0\in\mathcal{X}\)：初始状态值。
\(t_0\)：初始条件的参考时间。
\(t\)：沿轨迹的绝对时钟时间。
\(\tau\)：流经过时间。
\(I_x\)：穿过 \(x\) 的解包含 \(0\) 的极大经过时间区间。
\(W\)：受支持的经过时间/状态对 \((\tau,x)\)，其中 \(\tau\in I_x\)。
\(\Phi(\tau,x)=\phi_\tau(x)\)：\(W\) 上的联合局部有限时间演化映射；在所述更强流条件下联合 \(C^1\)。
\(\phi_\tau\)：对经过时间 \(\tau\) 有定义的状态上的有限时间状态映射；对局部流，其定义域可能依赖 \(\tau\)。
\(\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)=\{x\in\mathcal{X}:(\tau,x)\in W\}\)：单个固定经过时间下受支持的状态。
\(\phi_\tau(x_0)\)：从 \(x_0\) 经过时间 \(\tau\) 后到达的状态。
\(x(t)=\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)\)：与一个初始条件关联的轨迹。

符号 \(\phi\) 是约定。来源可能使用 \(\Phi\)、\(T_t\) 或其他符号；定义角色与复合性质比字母更重要。




State Space：提供可取的初始与后续状态。
Trajectory：提供通过固定一个初始状态得到的时间参数化演化。
Initial Condition：提供 \(x(t_0)=x_0\)。
Vector Field：提供本 Cycle 连续时间设定中的局部瞬时规则。

假定背景： 初等函数、函数复合与导数。
State 通过每个 \(\phi_\tau\) 作用其上的状态值相关联。
First-Order Autonomous Dynamical System 是唯一极大解、受支持域与流正则性的正式伴随对象。它作为相关对象被链接，而非用来取代这里的概念定义。










概念
与流的区别




向量场
给每个状态赋予局部瞬时变化向量 \(f(x)\)。流在演化有定义的状态与经过时间上给出有限时间演化 \(\phi_\tau(x)\)。


轨迹
固定 \(x_0\) 并变化经过时间得到轨迹 \(\tau\mapsto\phi_\tau(x_0)\)；有参考时间 \(t_0\) 时即 \(x(t)=\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)\)。一条轨迹是流组织的族中的一个成员。


初始条件
为一条轨迹选择起始状态与参考时间。流指定所有受支持初始状态如何随经过时间演化。


轨道
一条轨迹丢弃时间标签后访问的状态集合。流包含跨初始状态的有限时间映射，比任何单条轨道保留更多信息。


单个有限时间映射
一个映射 \(\phi_\tau\) 把状态推进一个所选时长。流是跨经过时间的兼容族，包括恒等与复合关系。


离散时间更新规则
诸如 \(F(x)\) 的映射把一个状态推进一个离散步，其迭代定义离散演化。它不自动是连续时间流，也不自动是某条连续时间流的时间一映射。


观测轨迹集合
数据集可能包含带噪声、不同输入或不同动力学的独立时间进程。只有论证了共同的状态演化族，它才表示一个共享流。


状态转移估计
从数据估计的映射依赖模型与推断选择。它可以估计流的一部分，但估计不是定义的一部分。






把演化族称为流，其本身并不蕴含：

任何任意的轨迹集合来自一个共享流；
外观相似的轨迹具有相同向量场或有限时间动力学；
一条观测轨迹确定其他初始状态的映射 \(\phi_\tau\)；
有限带噪观测识别唯一流；
曲线可视化确立动力学机制；
流对每个状态或对所有正负时间都有定义；
每个固定时间映射都是全局定义的满射 \(\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{X}\)，即使双侧光滑局部流在相应受支持域上有反向时间局部逆；
每个向量场都自动生成唯一全局流；或
输入驱动或显式时间相关系统具有相同的单参数流结构。




考虑一维自治规则
\[
\dot{x}=1,
\qquad \mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}.
\]
向量场在每个状态赋予相同瞬时速率 \(f(x)=1\)。其流是
\[
\phi_\tau(x_0)=x_0+\tau.
\]
对固定经过时间 \(\tau\)，\(\phi_\tau\) 把每个初始状态平移 \(\tau\)。对初始条件 \(x(t_0)=x_0\)，轨迹是 \(x(t)=x_0+(t-t_0)\)。这些映射复合，因为
\[
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_\sigma(x_0)\bigr)=x_0+\sigma+\tau=\phi_{\tau+\sigma}(x_0).
\]
该示例在无需高级理论的情况下分离这些对象：\(f\) 是局部速率，\(\{\phi_\tau\}\) 是有限时间演化族，\(t\mapsto\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)\) 是绝对时钟时间中的一条轨迹。



使用群体活动向量作为所提出的神经状态，为描述轨迹提供了坐标设定 (Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。神经流主张更强：它提出跨受支持初始条件的群体状态按照一个一致有限时间族演化。外观相似的试次轨迹或合并轨迹图并不确立那个共享族，尤其在输入、任务条件或未测量状态不同时。
对行为而言，一组运动迹线同样不自动是单一行为流的证据。这些迹线可能反映不同的控制输入、参数、状态定义或测量过程。从这类数据推断共享流是需要本概念对象之外的假设与评估的方法学问题。



在 L2 阶段，流把稳定的向量场概念连接到可复用的自治系统形式体系，而不把瞬时规则、一条轨迹、轨道与受支持的有限时间映射族合并为一个对象。在后续恢复任务能询问观测神经或行为轨迹是否支持共享动力学之前，这一区分必不可少。




什么证据足以支持跨试次或条件的单一共享流？
初始状态与观测中的不确定性应如何传播到流估计中？
何时应以单参数自治流之外的记号表示输入依赖或显式时间相关的演化？

这些是这个有界 L2 范围之外的后续推断与建模问题。




自治向量场、积分曲线、流与复合关系：(Teschl 2012年, secs. 6.1–6.3)。
神经群体坐标与轨迹语境：(Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。





将流定义为跨可能初始状态的有限时间演化。
区分流与向量场、轨迹、轨道、更新规则与观测轨迹集合。
使向量场 / 流 / 轨迹关系显式。
在不进入存在性–唯一性理论的情况下陈述恒等与复合性质。
分离绝对时钟时间 \(t\) 与流经过时间 \(\tau\)，并推迟半流与非自治扩展。
已接受轻量概念审查并纳入要求的 L1 修正。
对 \(I_x\)、\(W\)、\(\Phi\) 与 \(\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)\) 类型化而不蕴含全局支持。
仅在受支持域上陈述恒等与复合。
限定生成元关系，并分离经过时间与初始状态可微性。
把存在性、唯一性、延拓与正则性推导保留在稳定数学对象中。
独立审查确认了有界 L2 形式化；记录的审查决定记录所有者授权，对象被接受为 L2 / stable。

一个映射 \(\phi_\tau\) 把状态推进一个所选时长。流是跨经过时间的兼容族，包括恒等与复合关系。


离散时间更新规则
诸如 \(F(x)\) 的映射把一个状态推进一个离散步，其迭代定义离散演化。它不自动是连续时间流，也不自动是某条连续时间流的时间一映射。


观测轨迹集合
数据集可能包含带噪声、不同输入或不同动力学的独立时间进程。只有论证了共同的状态演化族，它才表示一个共享流。


状态转移估计
从数据估计的映射依赖模型与推断选择。它可以估计流的一部分，但估计不是定义的一部分。

title: 流
text:
把演化族称为流，其本身并不蕴含：

任何任意的轨迹集合来自一个共享流；
外观相似的轨迹具有相同向量场或有限时间动力学；
一条观测轨迹确定其他初始状态的映射 \(\phi_\tau\)；
有限带噪观测识别唯一流；
曲线可视化确立动力学机制；
流对每个状态或对所有正负时间都有定义；
每个固定时间映射都是全局定义的满射 \(\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{X}\)，即使双侧光滑局部流在相应受支持域上有反向时间局部逆；
每个向量场都自动生成唯一全局流；或
输入驱动或显式时间相关系统具有相同的单参数流结构。

title: 流
text:
考虑一维自治规则
\[
\dot{x}=1,
\qquad \mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}.
\]
向量场在每个状态赋予相同瞬时速率 \(f(x)=1\)。其流是
\[
\phi_\tau(x_0)=x_0+\tau.
\]
对固定经过时间 \(\tau\)，\(\phi_\tau\) 把每个初始状态平移 \(\tau\)。对初始条件 \(x(t_0)=x_0\)，轨迹是 \(x(t)=x_0+(t-t_0)\)。这些映射复合，因为
\[
\phi_\tau\bigl(\phi_\sigma(x_0)\bigr)=x_0+\sigma+\tau=\phi_{\tau+\sigma}(x_0).
\]
该示例在无需高级理论的情况下分离这些对象：\(f\) 是局部速率，\(\{\phi_\tau\}\) 是有限时间演化族，\(t\mapsto\phi_{t-t_0}(x_0)\) 是绝对时钟时间中的一条轨迹。

title: 流
text:
使用群体活动向量作为所提出的神经状态，为描述轨迹提供了坐标设定 (Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。神经流主张更强：它提出跨受支持初始条件的群体状态按照一个一致有限时间族演化。外观相似的试次轨迹或合并轨迹图并不确立那个共享族，尤其在输入、任务条件或未测量状态不同时。
对行为而言，一组运动迹线同样不自动是单一行为流的证据。这些迹线可能反映不同的控制输入、参数、状态定义或测量过程。从这类数据推断共享流是需要本概念对象之外的假设与评估的方法学问题。

title: 流
text: 在 L2 阶段，流把稳定的向量场概念连接到可复用的自治系统形式体系，而不把瞬时规则、一条轨迹、轨道与受支持的有限时间映射族合并为一个对象。在后续恢复任务能询问观测神经或行为轨迹是否支持共享动力学之前，这一区分必不可少。

title: 流
text:
什么证据足以支持跨试次或条件的单一共享流？
初始状态与观测中的不确定性应如何传播到流估计中？
何时应以单参数自治流之外的记号表示输入依赖或显式时间相关的演化？

这些是这个有界 L2 范围之外的后续推断与建模问题。

title: 流
text:
自治向量场、积分曲线、流与复合关系：(Teschl 2012年, secs. 6.1–6.3)。
神经群体坐标与轨迹语境：(Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。

title: 流
text:
将流定义为跨可能初始状态的有限时间演化。
区分流与向量场、轨迹、轨道、更新规则与观测轨迹集合。
使向量场 / 流 / 轨迹关系显式。
在不进入存在性–唯一性理论的情况下陈述恒等与复合性质。
分离绝对时钟时间 \(t\) 与流经过时间 \(\tau\)，并推迟半流与非自治扩展。
已接受轻量概念审查并纳入要求的 L1 修正。
对 \(I_x\)、\(W\)、\(\Phi\) 与 \(\operatorname{dom}(\phi_\tau)\) 类型化而不蕴含全局支持。
仅在受支持域上陈述恒等与复合。
限定生成元关系，并分离经过时间与初始状态可微性。
把存在性、唯一性、延拓与正则性推导保留在稳定数学对象中。
独立审查确认了有界 L2 形式化；记录的审查决定记录所有者授权，对象被接受为 L2 / stable。

title: 可辨识性
text:
可辨识性询问在声明的实验设计下，不同模型规格能否产生相同的可观测数据分布。



如果若干参数或潜表示在观测上等价，同一设计的无限数据也无法在无附加约束的情况下选出唯一者。优化质量不能修复结构非可辨识性。



设想两种不同的内部描述对实验能收集的每次观测都作出完全相同的预测。数据无法区分它们。



设 \(\Theta\) 是模型规格空间，\(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\) 表示固定实验设计下可观测样本空间上的概率律。模型诱导参数化映射
\[
\Psi:\Theta\to\mathcal P(\mathcal Y),
\qquad
\Psi(\theta)=P_\theta.
\]
Rothenberg 通过从结构参数到可观测分布的映射来框定辨识 (Rothenberg 1971年)。


当
\[
P_{\theta_1}=P_{\theta_2}
\Longrightarrow
\theta_1=\theta_2.
\]
时，参数化是全局（严格）可辨识的。
当存在 \(\theta\) 的邻域 \(U\) 使得
\[
\Psi^{-1}(P_\theta)\cap U=\{\theta\}.
\]
时，它在 \(\theta\) 处局部可辨识。局部可辨识排除任意接近 \(\theta\) 的不可区分参数，但允许别处的观测等价参数。
在声明约定下，当可辨识性在某个指定的例外子集（通常是低维代数集或测度零集）之外成立时，有限维参数模型是一般可辨识的。「一般」的含义、参考测度/几何以及任何剩余有限对称性都必须陈述。一般可辨识性并不使例外参数不可能或经验上可检测。Allman、Matias 与 Rhodes 对潜结构模型使用这一概念，并显式允许标签置换 (Allman 等 2009年)。



定义
\[
\theta_1\sim\theta_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P_{\theta_1}=P_{\theta_2}.
\]
这是等价关系。当精确参数恢复不可能或科学上不必要时，可辨识目标可以是等价类 \([\theta]\in\Theta/{\sim}\) 或满足
\[
P_{\theta_1}=P_{\theta_2}
\Longrightarrow
\psi(\theta_1)=\psi(\theta_2).
\]
的可辨识函数 \(\psi(\theta)\)。已知对称群 \(G\) 可以产生等价的一部分：\(g\cdot\theta\) 与 \(\theta\) 产生相同可观测律。up to \(G\)（模 \(G\)）可辨识指观测纤维等于声明的群轨道，而非原始坐标被唯一恢复。



结构可辨识性询问理想化的无限信息问题，使用精确可观测分布与声明的模型/设计。






提示LDG 操作综合



LDG 用实用可辨识性指由有限实验覆盖、弱敏感性、病态条件、宽后验不确定性或大估计量方差引起的有限数据弱点。优化失败是单独的计算困难：即使存在良条件可辨识目标，它也可能阻止恢复。结构可辨识的模型可能在实用上困难；结构非可辨识的参数无法通过更好的优化器或来自同一未变设计的更多数据而变得唯一。





对称性必须从特定模型推导：

在有限混合与离散隐状态模型中，置换潜标签可以使可观测分布不变；Allman、Matias 与 Rhodes 称之为标签置换，并把可辨识性表述为 up to permutation（模置换）(Allman 等 2009年)。
在 \(z\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\) 的 PPCA 中，对正交 \(R\) 把 \(W\) 替换为 \(WR\)、\(z\) 替换为 \(R^\top z\) 会保留潜先验与可观测协方差。因此 \(W\) 与潜坐标架在右正交变换下不可辨识 (Tipping 和 Bishop 1999年, sec. 3.2)。把完整模型描述为「up to rotation」（模旋转）可辨识，额外要求排除进一步退化情形的条件。
一般缩放或可逆变换只有在观测映射、潜律、转移模型与其他受影响分量被一致变换时才保留可观测律。它们不是普遍对称性。






\(\theta\)：模型规格或参数。
\(P_\theta\)：诱导的可观测数据分布。
\(\Psi:\Theta\to\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\)：参数化映射。
\(\Psi^{-1}(P_\theta)\)：观测纤维。
\(\theta_1\sim\theta_2\)：观测等价。
\([\theta]\in\Theta/{\sim}\)：可辨识等价类目标。
\(\psi(\theta)\)：在观测纤维上恒定时是可辨识函数。
\(G\cdot\theta\)：声明对称群的轨道。




Latent Variable 与 Observation Model 提供其唯一性受质疑的隐藏量与可观测映射。










概念
区别




可估计性 / 实用可辨识性
关乎有限数据精度、条件数、后验集中性或估计量；结构可辨识性是理想化模型加设计的性质。


可观测性
控制论中关乎从跨时间输出恢复状态；相关但不相同。


可解读性
赋予模型组件的科学意义；可辨识参数仍可能难以解读。


预测准确性
等价模型按定义预测相同可观测律，非等价的误设模型仍可能有相似的有限样本预测。预测不识别内部参数。


因果辨识
在因果模型与识别假设下瞄准干预或反事实量。一些目标在足够强的观测假设下可辨识，另一些需要干预数据或设计；统计参数可辨识性本身不是因果辨识。


标签或坐标约定
可以为报告或计算从等价类中选择一个代表，而不使它被科学辨识。






可辨识性并不蕴含易估计、良条件、低方差、正确模型类、每个实现状态的可观测性、因果解读或机制性真理。一般可辨识性不保证拟合参数在例外集之外。非可辨识性并不蕴含无用的预测，但它限制哪些内部主张可以唯一。





设
\[
z\sim\mathcal N(0,I),
\qquad
y=Wz+\varepsilon,
\qquad
\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I).
\]
对任何正交矩阵 \(R\)，定义 \(z'=R^\top z\) 与 \(W'=WR\)。则 \(z'\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\) 且
\[
W'z'=Wz,
\]
因此可观测分布不变。载荷矩阵 \(W\) 与潜坐标架因此在该正交作用下不被辨识。可观测协方差 \(WW^\top+\sigma^2I\) 由 PPCA 律确定；载荷子空间的辨识需要相关秩与特征值分离条件，此处不在没有这些条件的情况下断言。



在双分量混合中，交换分量标签与所有标签索引参数会使混合分布不变。在合适条件下可以辨识分量的无序对，但没有外部约定就无法辨识带特权的数值标签。
这些是精确模型对称性。任意缩放或非线性变换除非每个受影响模型分量被一致变换，否则不观测等价。




潜神经坐标、动力学矩阵与观测映射在拟合相同记录时可以相互权衡。主张应陈述什么可辨识——预测、子空间、等价类或单个参数。



在 L2 阶段，可辨识性提供从模型规格到可观测律的类型化映射，并阐明科学目标何时是参数、可辨识函数或等价类。它是防止把拟合潜表示等同于唯一生物机制的主要护栏。




哪些干预打破重要等价？
什么变换保留科学主张？
哪些参数只是实用而非结构上弱确定？





Rothenberg 提供经核查的主参数辨识框架与局部辨识视角 (Rothenberg 1971年)。
Allman、Matias 与 Rhodes 提供经核查的严格与一般可辨识性、例外集与潜标签置换主处理 (Allman 等 2009年)。
Tipping 与 Bishop 提供经核查的 PPCA 旋转对称性 (Tipping 和 Bishop 1999年, sec. 3.2)。
信息矩阵/秩检验、代数可辨识性证明、实验设计优化与估计量理论被有意推迟。





定义观测等价与全局辨识。
把可辨识性与估计、预测和解读分开。
包含潜坐标等价示例。
类型化参数化映射与全局/局部/一般可辨识性。
定义观测等价、商目标与可辨识函数。
区分结构可辨识性与实用可辨识性。
把置换、旋转、缩放与坐标对称性限制在保留可观测律的模型中。
把可辨识性与可估计性、可观测性、预测、解读与因果辨识分开。
独立 L2 科学审查已完成；初步发现已被修正，聚焦复审在记录的审查决定下通过。

title: 可辨识性
text: 可辨识性并不蕴含易估计、良条件、低方差、正确模型类、每个实现状态的可观测性、因果解读或机制性真理。一般可辨识性不保证拟合参数在例外集之外。非可辨识性并不蕴含无用的预测，但它限制哪些内部主张可以唯一。

title: 可辨识性
text:
设
\[
z\sim\mathcal N(0,I),
\qquad
y=Wz+\varepsilon,
\qquad
\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I).
\]
对任何正交矩阵 \(R\)，定义 \(z'=R^\top z\) 与 \(W'=WR\)。则 \(z'\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\) 且
\[
W'z'=Wz,
\]
因此可观测分布不变。载荷矩阵 \(W\) 与潜坐标架因此在该正交作用下不被辨识。可观测协方差 \(WW^\top+\sigma^2I\) 由 PPCA 律确定；载荷子空间的辨识需要相关秩与特征值分离条件，此处不在没有这些条件的情况下断言。



在双分量混合中，交换分量标签与所有标签索引参数会使混合分布不变。在合适条件下可以辨识分量的无序对，但没有外部约定就无法辨识带特权的数值标签。
这些是精确模型对称性。任意缩放或非线性变换除非每个受影响模型分量被一致变换，否则不观测等价。

title: 可辨识性
text: 潜神经坐标、动力学矩阵与观测映射在拟合相同记录时可以相互权衡。主张应陈述什么可辨识——预测、子空间、等价类或单个参数。

title: 可辨识性
text: 在 L2 阶段，可辨识性提供从模型规格到可观测律的类型化映射，并阐明科学目标何时是参数、可辨识函数或等价类。它是防止把拟合潜表示等同于唯一生物机制的主要护栏。

title: 可辨识性
text:
哪些干预打破重要等价？
什么变换保留科学主张？
哪些参数只是实用而非结构上弱确定？

title: 可辨识性
text:
Rothenberg 提供经核查的主参数辨识框架与局部辨识视角 (Rothenberg 1971年)。
Allman、Matias 与 Rhodes 提供经核查的严格与一般可辨识性、例外集与潜标签置换主处理 (Allman 等 2009年)。
Tipping 与 Bishop 提供经核查的 PPCA 旋转对称性 (Tipping 和 Bishop 1999年, sec. 3.2)。

title: 可辨识性
text:
定义观测等价与全局辨识。
把可辨识性与估计、预测和解读分开。
包含潜坐标等价示例。
类型化参数化映射与全局/局部/一般可辨识性。
定义观测等价、商目标与可辨识函数。
区分结构可辨识性与实用可辨识性。

title: 初始条件
text:
初始条件为所考虑的演化把某个指定状态值赋予某个指定参考时刻。



演化规则本身不说明讨论的是哪条已实现演化。初始条件提供启动描述所依据的状态值，并锚定在一个参考时刻。因此它把一般状态描述连接到一条特定轨迹或一组可能的轨迹。
「初始」相对于问题而言，不一定相对于系统的物理起点。研究者可以选择试次开始、刺激起始、运动起始或任何其他声明的参考时刻。同一个状态值可以作为一次分析的初始条件，也可以作为另一次分析的中间状态。



假设摆模型已准备好描述角度与角速度如何变化。要从时刻 \(t_0\) 继续该模型，必须指定摆在那里的状态。说「角度为零」通常不充分，因为不同的角速度导致不同的后续运动。说「在 \(t_0\)，角度为零且角速度为 1」则赋予完整的状态值，从而为该状态描述提供初始条件。
初始条件不是额外一类物理量。它是被置于特定角色的状态值：在参考时刻锚定演化问题的值。



设 \(\mathcal{X}\) 是状态空间，\(t_0\) 是所选参考时刻。初始条件具有如下形式
\[
x(t_0)=x_0,\qquad x_0\in\mathcal{X}.
\]
这里 \(x_0\) 是可取状态值。该方程是对轨迹 \(x(t)\) 施加的条件：为问题考虑的任何轨迹都必须在 \(t_0\) 穿过 \(x_0\)。Teschl 在定义初值问题时使用这一标准形式 (Teschl 2012年, sec. 2.2)。
该条件只有与指定的演化规则、参数以及 \(t_0\) 之后任何所需的未来输入值或规定一起，才约束轨迹。在 L1 阶段不作普遍的存在性或唯一性声明：取决于描述与假设，一个条件与规则在所请求的时间区间上可能允许一条、多条或零条轨迹。




\(t_0\)：为问题选择的参考时刻。
\(\mathcal{X}\)：状态空间。
\(x_0\in\mathcal{X}\)：被赋予的初始状态值。
\(x(t_0)=x_0\)：初始条件陈述。
\(x(t)\)：当这样的轨迹被定义时满足条件的轨迹。

下标零标记参考角色；它不要求时钟时间数值上为零。




State：区分状态值与观测和参数。
State Space：提供 \(x_0\) 从中选取的可取状态值。
Trajectory：提供在 \(t_0\) 被约束的时间索引对象。

假定背景： 初等函数记号。










概念
与初始条件的区别




状态值
系统在某一时刻的任何已实现条件。当它被赋予演化问题所选参考时刻时，就成为初始条件。


轨迹
以时间为参数的可取状态演化。初始条件约束其在某个参考时刻的值，但不是整条轨迹。


参数
参数对演化规则进行索引或指定，并在声明描述下保持固定。初始状态由该规则初始化并传播。常数未知量只有在显式改变模型角色分配时才能移入扩维状态。


参考时刻的观测
测量 \(y(t_0)\) 可能是有噪声、部分或间接的。它是关于 \(x_0\) 的证据，而非自动就是初始条件本身。


首个记录样本
第一个可用数据点可能出现在建模区间开始之后，可能省略状态变量，也可能只是观测。它不自动是完整的初始条件。


外部输入
未来输入可能影响后续轨迹，但一般不包含在 \(x_0\) 中。模型必须单独指定其所需的任何输入信息。


边界条件
边界条件是更宽泛的约束，可以在其他时间或位置施加。初始条件特指在所选参考时刻赋予状态信息。


重置或试次起始
实验事件可以定义 \(t_0\)，但它不保证系统的状态已知、各试次相同或独立于更早的历史。






把 \(x(t_0)=x_0\) 称为初始条件，其本身并不蕴含：

\(t_0\) 是物理系统开始存在的时间；
\(x_0\) 被直接或精确测量；
首个数据行是完整状态值；
相同的名义实验条件在每次试次产生相同的 \(x_0\)；
演化规则与参数已知；
轨迹对所有后续时间都存在或唯一；
在改变参数或输入的同时改变 \(x_0\) 就能隔离初始条件效应；或
后续行为的差异完全由初始条件差异造成。




对摆状态 \(x=(\text{angle},\text{angular velocity})\)，选择参考时刻 \(t_0\) 并赋予
\[
x(t_0)=(0,1).
\]
这表示在 \(t_0\)，摆处于零角度、所选单位下角速度为 1。这一对是初始状态值；\(t_0\) 是条件的一部分。摆长与阻尼仍是声明模型的参数，而如果模型包含力矩，\(t_0\) 之后施加的力矩是外部输入。
报告角度接近零的相机测量不足以确立这一初始条件，因为缺少角速度且测得的角度不确定。在 \(t_0\) 估计完整状态产生估计的初始条件，不应被静默地当作精确值。



在神经动力学中，声明事件时刻的群体活动向量可以被建模为后续群体演化的初始条件。Cunningham 与 Yu 概括了运动皮层研究，其中准备期群体活动被解读为设定运动期动力学的初始状态 (Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。这是对记录活动的模型解读，而非证明该向量是完整的物理神经状态，也非证明后续差异仅由该初始值造成。
对行为而言，试次起始时仅有位置可能不是充分的初始条件，当速度、姿态、情境或内部任务状态影响后续行为时尤其如此。LDG 应区分实验对齐事件、那里可用的测量以及实际赋予模型的状态值。



许多 LDG 问题比较跨试次、条件、受试者或模态的时间进程。初始条件语言使这些比较更精确：轨迹不同是因为它们从不同所提状态开始、因为演化规则或输入不同，还是因为状态未被完整观测？该概念不回答这一经验问题，但防止这些备选被混为一谈。




应如何把估计 \(x_0\) 的不确定性传播到关于后续轨迹的主张中？
对特定神经或行为分析，哪个事件应定义 \(t_0\)？
什么证据能区分初始状态变异与参数、输入或未测量状态变量的变化？





初值记号与角色：(Teschl 2012年, sec. 2.2)。
神经科学特定的初始状态解读：(Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。





将初始条件定义为参考时刻的状态赋值。
区分初始状态、观测、首个样本、参数与输入。
在不进入存在性或唯一性理论的情况下使 \(t_0\) 的角色显式。
包含明确的非蕴含与估计初始条件警示。
仅使用现有规范前置知识。
已接受轻量概念审查并纳入要求的 L1 修正。

title: 本征维数
text:
本征维数是在指定结构模型、尺度与准则下赋予对象的独立坐标或自由度数目。



本征维数可以小于外围维数，但它不是有限带噪数据集的与模型无关性质。不同估计量、尺度、噪声模型与容差可以给出不同答案。



高维记录空间中靠近曲线的点可能主要沿一个方向在粗尺度上变化，而细尺度噪声占据许多方向。



对表示在 \(\mathbb R^D\) 中的光滑 \(d\) 维流形，\(d\) 是其流形维数，\(D\) 是其外围维数。更一般地，「本征维数」可以指流形维数、局部维数、有效线性秩或另一个声明的复杂度准则。
LDG 因此要求每个估计 \(\widehat d\) 陈述模型类、邻域或尺度、估计量与噪声假设。Levina 与 Bickel 展示一个行为依赖邻域以及数据靠近而非恰在流形上的估计量 (Levina 和 Bickel 2004年)。




\(D\)：外围维数。
\(d\)：声称的本征维数。
\(\widehat d\)：估计维数。
尺度或邻域大小：评估维数所依据的分辨率。




Ambient Dimension 提供与本征主张比较的周围表示。










概念
区别




秩
矩阵或子空间的精确线性维数；本征维数可以是非线性或尺度相关的。


潜维数
所选潜模型中的变量数目；它可以是选定的，而非被辨识为本征真值。


流形维数
当流形假设成立时的特定数学维数。


解释方差
近似准则，不是维数的普遍定义。






低本征维数估计并不证明流形、识别唯一潜变量、确立机制、跨尺度保持恒定，或论证特定非线性嵌入。



\(\mathbb R^{10}\) 中直线上的无噪点具有一维线性结构。添加小的各向同性噪声可以使细尺度估计接近十，而粗尺度估计保持接近一。



神经维数依赖试次条件、预处理、时间尺度、模型类与准则。因此报告的维数应被视为操作性估计。



本征维数强制执行 LDG 的核心禁令之一：维数是模型与准则相关的，降维不是几何的证明。

title: 本征维数
text:

title: 潜轨迹
text:
潜轨迹是以时间为索引的潜随机元素或该元素的一条实现路径，区别于观测以及用于估计它的任何点摘要。



潜轨迹语言被用于几个不同对象：模型指定的潜过程、观测数据后它的后验分布、后验抽样，以及绘制的点估计。保持这些对象分开，可以防止把光滑估计误认为唯一恢复的状态演化或动力学机制的证据。



观测序列可以支持许多隐藏路径。模型为这些路径赋予相对概率，推断用数据更新该分布。绘制单个后验均值或单条最大后验路径会抑制这种不确定性，也可能隐藏潜坐标对称性。



设 \((\mathcal Z,\Sigma_{\mathcal Z})\) 是潜空间，离散时间中 \(I=\{0,\ldots,T\}\)。潜轨迹随机元素是可测映射
\[
Z_{0:T}:\Omega\to\mathcal Z^{T+1}.
\]
一个实现是路径 \(z_{0:T}=(z_0,\ldots,z_T)\)。在连续时间中，必须声明路径空间 \(\mathcal P(I,\mathcal Z)\)——例如带指定可测结构的连续或 càdlàg 路径——并写 \(Z:\Omega\to\mathcal P(I,\mathcal Z)\)。时间索引本身不使 \(Z_t\) 成为充分的动力学状态，也不指定转移律。
假设合适的正则条件分布存在，给定观测 \(Y_{0:T}=y_{0:T}\) 与生成模型，推断目标一般是完整路径上的条件概率测度，
\[
\Pi(A\mid y_{0:T})
=
\Pr(Z_{0:T}\in A\mid Y_{0:T}=y_{0:T}),
\qquad A\in\Sigma_{\mathcal Z}^{\otimes(T+1)},
\]
或在存在合适参考测度时的条件密度 \(p(z_{0:T}\mid y_{0:T})\)。该后验律不等于任何单条绘制的路径。


在 State-Space Model 声明的一阶状态空间假设下，路径律可以通过初始律与转移核分解，
\[
p(z_{0:T},y_{0:T})
=
p(z_0)
\prod_{k=0}^{T-1}p(z_{k+1}\mid z_k)
\prod_{k=0}^{T}p(y_k\mid z_k).
\]
该分解是模型假设，不是「潜轨迹」一词的推论。常见推断对象包括：

滤波分布： \(p(z_k\mid y_{0:k})\)，使用到时间 \(k\) 为止可用的观测；
固定区间平滑分布： \(p(z_{0:T}\mid y_{0:T})\)，或其边际 \(p(z_k\mid y_{0:T})\)，同样使用后续观测；
后验样本： 随机抽样 \(\tilde z_{0:T}\sim p(z_{0:T}\mid y_{0:T})\)；
联合 MAP 路径： 当声明路径密度与最大化者存在时，值 \(\hat z^{\mathrm{MAP}}_{0:T}\in\arg\max p(z_{0:T}\mid y_{0:T})\)；
边际 MAP 序列： 独立选择的 \(p(z_k\mid y_{0:T})\) 最大化者，不必等于联合 MAP 路径，也不必形成受支持的转移序列；
后验均值路径： 当 \(\mathcal Z\) 在向量空间中表示且期望存在时，\(\hat z^{\mathrm{mean}}_k=\mathbb E[Z_k\mid y_{0:T}]\)。

Kalman 根据目标时间等于、早于还是晚于最后观测时间区分平滑、滤波与预测，并把估计视为条件分布与损失的函数 (Kalman 1960年)。因此后验均值与声明坐标中的平方误差损失绑定；它不是「恢复轨迹」的与表示无关定义。基于密度的 MAP 值也可能依赖参考测度与坐标参数化。
点摘要不自动是可许实现路径。逐点边际均值或众数可能离开离散或非线性状态空间、违反硬路径约束，或组合在后验抽样中从未同时出现的特征。即使摘要位于路径空间中，它在后验下也不必典型，也不必满足无强迫确定性演化律。精确后验样本尊重被建模后验支撑，但那只确立与拟合模型的兼容性。



设 \(h:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z'\) 是双可测双射，并定义 \(Z'_k=h(Z_k)\)。变换路径律是逐分量路径映射 \(h^{0:T}\) 下的前推。保持相同可观测模型要求每个受影响分量一致变换：
\[
\mu'=h_\#\mu,
\]
\[
Q'_k(z',A')
=
Q_k\!\left(h^{-1}(z'),h^{-1}(A')\right),
\]
\[
G'_k(z',B)
=
G_k\!\left(h^{-1}(z'),B\right).
\]
对确定性动力学 \(z_{k+1}=f_k(z_k)\)，这给出 \(f'_k=h\circ f_k\circ h^{-1}\)。变换路径上的后验同样必须是前推 \((h^{0:T})_\#\Pi\)。只变换报告的轨迹而不变换潜律、转移模型与观测模型，通常改变生成规格而非仅仅改变坐标。
因此诸如欧氏 RMSE 的逐坐标轨迹误差只有在声明坐标、单位、度量、时间对应与任何允许对齐后才具有意义。如果已知群 \(G\) 生成观测对称性，评估可以转而瞄准轨道或等价类，例如
\[
\inf_{g\in G}
\frac{1}{T+1}\sum_{k=0}^{T}
d_{\mathcal Z}\!\left(z_k^\star,g\cdot\hat z_k\right)^2,
\]
并陈述群、度量、拟合数据与对齐的留出使用。当潜坐标本身未被辨识时，也可以比较可观测预测或其他可辨识函数。例如在 PPCA 中，载荷矩阵与潜坐标架具有正交旋转歧义 (Tipping 和 Bishop 1999年, sec. 3.2)。这一精确对称性不授权对每个潜模型进行任意非线性对齐。









提示LDG 操作综合



以下规程把上述后验、可辨识性与状态空间区分连接成有界评估设计。它是提出的 LDG 实践，不是归因于经核查来源的定理。


在模拟或其他声明潜真值 \(z_{0:T}^\star\) 的设定中，评估应报告多于一条视觉对齐路径：

状态或轨迹误差： 使用声明度量，并在必要时使用被论证的对称性/对齐约定；
时间泛化： 评估留出时间、试次、初始条件或参数条件，而不仅是拟合序列；
不确定性覆盖： 跨重复数据集，检查边际状态区域或同时路径区域是否以它们广告的比率包含合适对齐的真值，并且不要把这两个覆盖目标混为一谈；
校准或评分： 用正确评分规则或重复模拟校准比较后验或预测分布，而不仅是单个区间的宽度；
模型比较： 对照更简单的静态或弱动力学基线检验，确定转移模型是否改善留出预测或恢复。

如果对齐是用用于评分的同一真值估计的，必须报告该依赖与任何由此产生的乐观偏差。覆盖是声明数据生成过程下重复规程的性质；一条视觉上合理的可信带不是校准结果。模拟真值只相对模拟器与声明等价约定确立恢复，而非唯一物理或生物真值。





\(Z_{0:T}\)：潜轨迹随机元素。
\(z_{0:T}\)：一条实现潜路径。
\(Y_{0:T}=y_{0:T}\)：观测随机变量与实现数据。
\(\Pi(\mathrm dz_{0:T}\mid y_{0:T})\)：路径上的后验概率测度。
\(p(z_k\mid y_{0:k})\)：滤波分布。
\(p(z_{0:T}\mid y_{0:T})\)：固定区间平滑分布。
\(\tilde z_{0:T}\)：后验样本。
\(\hat z^{\mathrm{MAP}}_{0:T}\)、\(\hat z^{\mathrm{mean}}_{0:T}\)：声明的点摘要。
\(h\) 与 \(h^{0:T}\)：潜坐标与逐分量路径重参数化。
\(G\)：当科学目标是轨道或等价类时声明的对称群。




Trajectory 提供类型化时间索引路径。Latent Variable 提供模型隐藏量。Observation Model 与 State-Space Model 分离前向测量关系、转移律与后验推断任务。










概念
区别




观测轨迹
直接从测得变量构造的路径。它可以作为潜推断的输入，但不是隐藏路径本身。


确定性嵌入路径
由数据的固定变换产生的序列 \(e(y_k)\)。它不必定义潜概率律、后验不确定性或充分动力学状态。


潜状态轨迹
更强的建模角色，其中每个潜值被处理为对指定演化与系统边界充分的状态。


轨迹上的后验分布
可能路径上的条件概率律；它不是单个后验均值、MAP 路径或样本。


向量场 / 转移律
在受支持状态上赋予局部变化或转移分布的规则。一条推断路径不决定访问状态之外的此类规则。


流
在受支持初始状态上的兼容有限时间演化映射族。一条潜轨迹只是流下的一条轨道/路径，当这样的流存在时。


可辨识性
决定潜路径、参数或只是等价类/函数是否被可观测律唯一约束。






潜轨迹并不蕴含可辨识坐标、低本征维数、光滑性、自治动力学、流形结构、马尔可夫充分性、因果或机制意义，或来自观测的唯一逆。低重构误差或准确解码并不确立潜路径是真实状态。光滑后验均值并不确立光滑真实动力学。



设潜状态空间为 \(\mathcal Z=\{-1,+1\}\)，并假设后验以概率 \(1/2\) 赋予常值路径 \((-1,\ldots,-1)\)，以概率 \(1/2\) 赋予 \((+1,\ldots,+1)\)。两个后验样本都是可许路径，但逐点后验均值是 \((0,\ldots,0)\)，它不在 \(\mathcal Z^{T+1}\) 中。这显示后验均值为何可以是损失最优的摘要，却未必是可能的潜实现。
在线性高斯状态空间模型中，
\[
z_{k+1}=Az_k+w_k,
\qquad
y_k=Cz_k+v_k,
\]
滤波与平滑返回状态或路径上的条件分布，而不仅是单条线。在一致变换 \(A\)、\(C\)、潜律与后验的同时旋转潜坐标，可以在相关对称性下保留相同可观测模型；只旋转绘制估计则不确立等价。



Cunningham 与 Yu 描述 HMM、GPFA、LDS 与非线性动力系统方法返回低维潜神经轨迹，但明确告诫提取的轨迹反映带噪数据与拟合动力学模型之间的统计权衡 (Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。因此 GPFA 光滑性与 LDS/NLDS 动力学母题可以由模型假设促成，而非在数据中被独立发现。行为潜路径需要在测量、模型隐藏变量、后验摘要与状态主张之间进行同样分离。



在 L2 阶段，潜轨迹连接路径空间概率、状态空间推断、坐标对称性与已知真值评估。它提供比较生成与恢复方法所需的护栏，而不把可视化、后验均值或对齐重构当作机制性证据。




对不规则采样或不连续轨迹，哪种路径空间拓扑与不确定性表示合适？
给定模型中哪些潜对称性保留科学主张？
对齐不确定性应如何传播到轨迹误差与覆盖估计中？
何时转移模型在独立潜因子或平滑观测之上改善留出恢复？





Kalman 提供经核查的平滑、滤波与预测主区分，并在线性随机设定中把条件分布、损失、估计与估计误差协方差联系起来 (Kalman 1960年)。
Cunningham 与 Yu 提供经核查的神经群体轨迹语境，以及提取的光滑性或动力学母题可以既反映拟合模型又反映带噪数据的告诫 (Cunningham 和 Yu 2014年)。
Tipping 与 Bishop 提供经核查的概率潜变量观测模型、条件潜分布、条件均值摘要与 PPCA 正交旋转歧义 (Tipping 和 Bishop 1999年, secs. 3.1–3.4)。
一般路径空间测度论、非线性滤波/平滑算法、后验一致性定理与校准定理被有意推迟。





把潜轨迹类型化为随机元素，并区分实现路径与其后验律。
区分滤波、平滑、后验样本、联合 MAP 路径与后验均值。
显示点摘要为何不必是可许或典型的潜路径。
在坐标变换下一致变换潜律、转移模型、观测模型与后验。
把依赖坐标的误差与声明对称性/等价类目标分开。
把模型诱导的光滑性当作推断假设，而非真实动力学证据。
规定带已知真值的不确定性感知评估与对齐警示。
区分观测路径、确定性嵌入、潜状态、向量场与流。
